These equalities extend to finite direct sums by linearity and to all homogeneous morphisms by naturality of scalar maps. The grade $0$ acts as the tensor unit because normalization makes every unit associator and braiding scalar equal to $1$.

The chosen evaluation and coevaluation have the stated sources and targets. The first snake has scalar $\omega(g,-g,g)^{-1}\omega(g,-g,g)=1$. By [F2], every relative class is $u\cap[M,\Sigma]$ for some $u\in H^1(M;\mathbb R)$. The cap boundary identity gives $\partial(u\cap[M,\Sigma])=\pm(i^*u)\cap[\Sigma]$. Therefore $\lambda_M=PD_\Sigma(\operatorname{im}i^*)$; the sign does not change this subspace.

Let $E=\operatorname{im}i^*\subseteq H^1(\Sigma;\mathbb R)$. For $x\in H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb R)$, [F3] gives $\omega_\Sigma(x,PD_\Sigma\beta)=\langle\beta,x\rangle$ for $\beta\in E$. Hence $x$ is orthogonal to $PD_\Sigma(E)=\lambda_M$ exactly when every functional in $E$ vanishes on $x$.

By [F4], $E$ is the annihilator of $\ker i_*$ in $H^1(\Sigma;\mathbb R)$; finite-dimensional double-annihilator duality says the vectors annihilated by every element of $E$ are exactly $\ker i_*=\lambda_M$. Step 2.1 therefore gives $\lambda_M^\perp=\lambda_M$. This equality implies isotropy and half-dimension, so $\lambda_M$ is Lagrangian. If $\Sigma$ is empty, both sides are zero directly.

derivations.claim: For an integer $r$ with $0<|r|<2\ell$, put $C_r=\sum_{m=1}^{\ell-1}\cos(rm\pi/\ell)$. If $r$ is even, then $z=e^{2\pi i(r/2)/\ell}$ is a nontrivial $\ell$-th root of unity; the geometric sum $\sum_{m=0}^{\ell-1}z^m=0$ has real part $1+C_r$, so $C_r=-1$. If $r$ is odd, the geometric sum of $e^{i\pi rm/\ell}$ for $0\le m<2\ell$ is zero. Pairing terms at $m$ and $2\ell-m$ for $1\le m\le\ell-1$ leaves twice $C_r$; the two unpaired real terms are $1+\cos(r\pi)=0$, so $C_r=0$. Also $C_0=\ell-1$.

The product-to-sum identity gives the left side as $\tfrac12(C_{a-b}-C_{a+b})$, with $C_0$ used when $a=b$. If $a=b$, then $a+b$ is nonzero even and less than $2\ell$, so the value is $\tfrac12((\ell-1)-(-1))=\ell/2$. If $a\ne b$ and $a,b$ have the same parity, both nonzero indices $a-b$ and $a+b$ are even and their $C$ values are $-1$; if they have opposite parity, both indices are odd and their values are $0$. In both off-diagonal cases the difference is zero, proving the formula.

derivations.claim: For each fixed $a$, put $h_a(b)=s_{ab}/d_a$. By [F1], $h_a(0)=1$ and the truncated products $b\otimes1=(b-1)\oplus(b+1)$ for $1\le b\le\ell-3$ give $h_a(b+1)=h_a(1)h_a(b)-h_a(b-1)$. The endpoint product $(\ell-2)\otimes1=\ell-3$ gives the corresponding terminal recurrence.

For $1\le a\le\ell-3$, balancing gives $s_{a1}=\theta_a^{-1}\theta_1^{-1}(\theta_{a-1}d_{a-1}+\theta_{a+1}d_{a+1})=q^{-(a+2)}d_{a-1}+q^ad_{a+1}$, where $q=e^{it}$. Substituting the sine dimensions and using $e^{-i(a+2)t}\sin(at)+e^{iat}\sin((a+2)t)=\sin(2(a+1)t)$ yields $h_a(1)=2\cos((a+1)t)$. For $a=0$, the single summand in $0\otimes1$ gives $h_0(1)=d_1=2\cos t$. For $a=\ell-2$, the single summand $\ell-3$ gives $s_{a1}=q^{-\ell}d_{\ell-3}=-2\cos t=2\cos((\ell-1)t)d_{\ell-2}$, so the same formula holds at the upper endpoint.

The sequence $g_b=\sin((a+1)(b+1)t)/\sin((a+1)t)$ has $g_0=1$, $g_1=2\cos((a+1)t)$ and satisfies $g_{b+1}=2\cos((a+1)t)g_b-g_{b-1}$ by the sine addition identity. Steps 1.1–2.1 therefore give $h_a(b)=g_b$ for all $0\le b\le\ell-2$ by induction. Multiplying by $d_a$ yields the displayed formula for $s_{ab}$.

By [F2] with its two sine indices equal to $1$, $\sum_{a=0}^{\ell-2}d_a^2=\ell/(2\sin^2t)$; choose the positive square root $D=\sqrt{\ell/2}/\sin t$, which is permitted because $0<t<\pi$ and each $d_a>0$. Dividing $s$ by $D$ gives the displayed $S$. Applying [F2] to rows of $S$ proves $S^2=I$; hence $S$ and $s$ are invertible.

Let $\mathcal C$ be the spherical ribbon fusion category of [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. For simple labels $i,j$,

$$s_{ij}=(\theta_i\theta_j)^{-1}\sum_k N_{ij}^k\theta_kd_k,$$

and, for simple labels $x,i,j$,

$$s_{xi}s_{xj}=d_x\sum_kN_{ij}^ks_{xk}.$$

Also $s_{ij}=s_{ji}$, $s_{i^*j^*}=s_{ij}$, $s_{i0}=d_i$, and $d_{i^*}=d_i$. Consequently $h_x(i)=s_{xi}/d_x$ extends linearly to a unital ring character of the fusion ring.

Let $\mathcal C$ be modular under [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. Let $C$ be the charge-conjugation matrix, $C_{ij}=\delta_{i,j^*}$. Then

$$s^2=D^2C.$$

In particular $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2\ne0$, so either square root $D$ gives an invertible normalized matrix $S=s/D$ with $S^2=C$.
For every simple object $i$ of a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit and pivotal map $j$, its pivotal dimension $d_i=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_i)$ is nonzero.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a rigid monoidal category, let $a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ and $b:Y\to Y^{\vee\vee}$, and suppress the monoidal and chosen-dual comparison maps. For $s\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)$ write $\ell_Z(s)$ and $r_Z(s)$ for its left and right actions on $Z$, transported from $s\otimes1_Z$ and $1_Z\otimes s$ by the unit constraints.

1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.
   If $r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))=\ell_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))$, this becomes
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
   In particular multiplicativity holds when every unit scalar has equal left and right actions on every object. This condition holds in a braided category, and also in a $k$-linear monoidal category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$.
4. For every endomorphism $c:X\to X$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$.

The corresponding right-trace duality, additivity and cyclicity statements hold. For right-trace inputs $p:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$ and $q:Y^{\vee\vee}\to Y$, the general tensor formula is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(q\ell_{Y^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_R(p))).$$

It reduces to multiplicativity under the analogous equality of scalar actions, in particular under either sufficient condition above.

For a multifusion category choose a finite supplied list $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ of
representatives of its simple isomorphism classes. The **fusion rules** are the
nonnegative integers $N_{ij}^k$ determined by

$$[S_i][S_j]=\sum_{k\in I}N_{ij}^k[S_k]$$

in $K_0(\mathcal C)$. Jordan--Hölder makes the multiplicities independent of a
chosen composition series.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) with
chosen left duals ([[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]), braiding $c$
([[def-braiding]]) and twist $\theta$, and let $X\in\mathcal C$. Write
$X_{+1}:=X$ and $X_{-1}:=X^{\vee}$. In a strict model of $\mathcal C$
([[thm-every-braided-monoidal-category-is-monoidally-equivalent-to-a-strict-braided-one]])
there is a unique strict monoidal functor

$$F_X\colon\mathcal T\longrightarrow\mathcal C$$

from the framed oriented tangle category $\mathcal T$ with

$$F_X(+)=X,\qquad F_X(-)=X^{\vee},$$

$$F_X\bigl(X^{+}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=c_{X_\varepsilon,X_{\varepsilon'}},\qquad F_X\bigl(X^{-}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=(c_{X_{\varepsilon'},X_\varepsilon})^{-1},\qquad F_X(\cup_{+1})=\operatorname{coev}_X,\qquad F_X(\cap_{+1})=\operatorname{ev}_X,\qquad F_X(\varphi^{\pm1}_{+1})=\theta_X^{\pm1},$$

where the cup and cap are the coevaluation and evaluation maps attached to the
chosen left duals and the signs are the blackboard conventions of
[[def-the-framed-oriented-tangle-category]]. The remaining elementary tangles
of $\mathcal T$, those carrying a negative sign at a cup, cap or twist, receive
the values forced by these data through the relations. Explicitly put
$j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, with $u$ as in
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Then

$$F_X(\cup_-)=(1_{X^\vee}\otimes j_X^{-1})\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee},\qquad F_X(\cap_-)=\operatorname{ev}_{X^\vee}(j_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}),\qquad F_X(\varphi_-^{\pm1})=\theta_{X^\vee}^{\pm1}.$$

These are the right coevaluation and evaluation on $X$ induced by the ribbon
structure; they need no identification $X^{\vee\vee}=X$ on objects. For a general ribbon
category the same assignment determines a strong monoidal functor, unique up to
the canonical coherence isomorphisms of the strictification. Isotopic framed
tangles are equal morphisms of $\mathcal T$, so $F_X$ is an invariant of framed
tangles. Uniqueness needs no choice.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category with chosen left duals and twist
$\theta$ ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]), let $X\in\mathcal C$, let
$n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, and let $\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the
blackboard-framed closure of $\beta$: the closed framed tangle diagram obtained
from the $(n,n)$-tangle diagram of $\beta$ by joining its top boundary points
to its bottom boundary points by the identity pairing in the blackboard
framing, with every band colored by $X$. Denote by
$F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})$ the value of the tangle evaluation functor
on a word in the elementary generators representing this closed diagram. Then

$$t_n(\beta)=F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

where $t_n$ is the ribbon trace of
[[def-ribbon-evaluation-of-an-x-colored-closed-braid]] and $F_X$ is the tangle
evaluation functor of
[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]].
Consequently $t_n(\beta)$ depends only on the framed isotopy class of
$\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}}$, and the blackboard-framed closure of the positive
stabilization $\iota_n(\beta)\sigma_n$ is the framed closure of $\beta$ with
one positive curl added on a band, while the closure of the negative
stabilization adds one negative curl; with Turaev's convention the positive
curl is the generator $\varphi_X$ with $F_X(\varphi_X)=\theta_X$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category and $X\in\mathcal C$. If $\beta\in B_n$
and $\beta'\in B_{n'}$, with $n,n'\ge1$, are braids whose blackboard-framed $X$-colored closures
are isotopic as framed oriented tangles, then

$$t_n(\beta)=t_{n'}(\beta')$$

in $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)$. More generally, $t$ is an
invariant of framed $X$-colored links: the value $t_n(\beta)$ depends only on
the framed isotopy class of the closure of $\beta$. Ordinary Markov
stabilization is not a framed isotopy: it inserts a curl and is handled only
after writhe normalization.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals, twist $\theta$
([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) and Drinfeld morphism
$u_X\colon X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ of
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Put

$$j_X:=u_X\,\theta_X\ \colon\ X\longrightarrow X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Then $j$ is a natural isomorphism: it is the composite of the natural
isomorphism $u$ with the natural automorphism $\theta$ of the identity. It is
**monoidal** up to the monoidal comparison $d_{X,Y}\colon
X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\to(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$ of the double-dual
functor,

$$j_{X\otimes Y}=d_{X,Y}\circ(j_X\otimes j_Y),$$

which is precisely the statement that $u\theta$ is the pivotal comparison
induced by the ribbon structure; the identity follows from the tensor relation
$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ for
the Drinfeld morphism together with the twist axiom
$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ and
the naturality of $\theta$. Iterating the comparison identifies
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}$ with the corresponding composite of the $j_X$ and the
coherence isomorphisms of the tensor power.

Let $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), and let
$\rho_n\colon B_n\to\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(X^{\otimes n})$ be the
canonical braid action
([[cor-an-object-of-a-braided-category-carries-canonical-braid-actions]]). The
**ribbon evaluation** of the $X$-colored closed braid is the value

$$t_n(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}_L\!\left(j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)\right)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

in the sense of
[[def-the-categorical-trace-of-a-morphism-into-the-double-dual]]: the composite
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)$ is a morphism
$X^{\otimes n}\to(X^{\otimes n})^{\vee\vee}$, which is exactly the input type of
the left categorical trace. When $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)=k$
the value $t_n(\beta)$ is a scalar. For $n=1$ the group $B_1$ is trivial and
$t_1(e)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_X)$, the left dimension of $X$.

For $n=0$ put $t_0(e)=1_{\mathbf 1}$, the evaluation of the empty
closed tangle. This is a separate convention; no generator or dual pairing
is needed for the empty diagram.

The identification of $t_n(\beta)$ with the evaluation
$F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})$ of the blackboard-framed closure of $\beta$
under the functor of
[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]] is
the content of the closure-comparison lemma of this page; it must be proved
before the trace is used as a link evaluation, and it is not assumed here. The
functor $F_X$ is constructed under countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), while the definition of $t_n$ above is choice-free
and uses neither that functor nor that principle; only the comparison, not the
trace, carries the choice cost.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex finite semisimple spherical ribbon category with simple unit and finite simple-label set $I$, with every $d_i\ne0$. Put $\Omega=\sum_i d_i i$ and use the multicolored arbitrary-coupon evaluator of [[lem-multicolored-ribbon-coupon-evaluation]]. The entire graph evaluation is unchanged under a framed band slide of one $\Omega$-colored surgery component over another. It is also unchanged under sliding an open strand of any fixed color, or a strand of an arbitrary coupon-bearing colored graph, over an $\Omega$-colored surgery component, keeping every original color and coupon morphism fixed. All exterior crossings, open boundary factors and coupons are included, not merely a meridian scalar or closed trace. Orientations may be reversed with dual labels; no positivity or unitarity is assumed.

Here is the exact algebraic contract. Let $B=\bigoplus_i i^*\otimes i$ with inclusions $\iota_i$. Define $\iota_X,\Delta,\varepsilon,m$ by the finite formulas in the proof, and put $\Lambda=\sum_i d_i\iota_i b_i^R$. Then

$$m(1_B\otimes\Lambda)=\Lambda\varepsilon,\qquad\Gamma=(1_B\otimes m)(\Delta\otimes1_B),\qquad\Gamma(1_B\otimes\Lambda)=1_B\otimes\Lambda,\qquad\Gamma(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda)=\Lambda\otimes\Lambda.$$

For a fixed object $Y$ the lifted open-strand operator, retaining its entire first tensor factor, is

$$\widehat\Gamma_Y=(1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes m)(1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes\iota_Y\otimes1_B)(1_{Y^*}\otimes b_Y\otimes1_Y\otimes1_B),$$

and it satisfies $\widehat\Gamma_Y(1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes\Lambda)=1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes\Lambda$. Its exterior requires dinaturality only in the surgery-component variable; there is no naturality assumption on an arbitrary family of graph coupons indexed by $Y$. This lemma has no Gauss-sum, Fenn–Rourke, surgery normalization or topological move-completeness premise.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Pivotal trace additivity and tensor multiplicativity give $d_i d_j=\sum_kN_{ij}^kd_k$. Frobenius reciprocity and the change of variable in the fusion sum then give $\sum_i d_iN_{ij}^k=\sum_i d_iN_{k,j^*}^{i}=d_kd_{j^*}=d_kd_j.$ Using the balancing formula from [F1] and summing over $i$ yields $\sum_i\theta_i d_i s_{ij} =\theta_j^{-1}\sum_{i,k}d_iN_{ij}^k\theta_kd_k =\theta_j^{-1}d_jp_+.$

A simple strand $j$ encircled by a zero-framed simple loop $i$ is the scalar $s_{ij}/d_j$ on $j$ by [F5]. Hence the $\Omega$-meridian acts by $\frac1{d_j}\sum_i d_is_{ij} =\frac{(s^2)_{0j}}{d_j} =D^2\delta_{j,0},$ where $d_j\ne0$ by [F3]. Thus $D^{-2}$ times this meridian is the projector onto the unit channel. This proves the projector identity from modular inversion.

Multiply the last identity by $s_{j^*,k}$ and sum over $j$. By [F1]–[F2], $\sum_j s_{ij}s_{j^*,k} =\sum_x s_{i^*,x}s_{xk} =(s^2)_{i^*,k} =D^2\delta_{i,k}.$ Therefore $p_+\sum_j\theta_j^{-1}d_js_{j^*,k}=D^2\theta_kd_k$. Reindexing $j$ by $j^*$ and taking $k=0$ gives $p_+p_-=D^2$; since $p_+p_-=D^2\ne0$, both Gauss sums are nonzero and $\kappa^{-1}=p_-/D$.

By [F4], a $\pm1$-framed $\Omega$ unknot evaluates to $\sum_i d_i\theta_i^{\pm1}d_i=p_\pm$. For a $+1$ blow-up, the normalization changes by $D^{-1}\kappa^{-1}p_+=1$; for a $-1$ blow-up it changes by $D^{-1}\kappa p_-=p_+p_-/D^2=1$. The empty surgery diagram gives $D^{-1}$. By [F5], a zero-framed unknot colored by $\Omega$ evaluates to $\sum_i d_i^2=D^2$, so its one-component normalization is $D^{-2}D^2=1$, the $S^2\times S^1$ value.

Apply [F6] to the full coupon-bearing graph. Its finite coend identity preserves the entire band-slide morphism with every boundary factor and exterior coupon fixed, for either two surgery components or an open colored strand slid over a surgery component. It is independent of the simple-meridian computation of step 1.2. A surgery-component slide changes the linking matrix by the integral basis congruence $B\mapsto P^{\mathsf t}BP$, preserving signature even when $B$ is singular, and preserves the number of surgery components. An open graph-strand slide changes neither surgery matrix nor component count. Therefore every normalization factor is unchanged, proving the full normalized slide identities. Together with step 3.1 this proves all the stated local move identities; it imports no relative topological move-completeness theorem.

By [F2], the right side is $\sum_\ell N_{ij}^{\ell}D^2\delta_{\ell,k}=D^2N_{ij}^k$. Thus $\sum_xs_{xi}s_{xj}s_{x,k^*}/d_x=D^2N_{ij}^k$.
Since $S_{0x}=d_x/D$ and $S=s/D$, dividing step 1.1 by $D^2$ rewrites it as $N_{ij}^k=\sum_xS_{ix}S_{jx}S_{k^*x}/S_{0x}$, using symmetry of $S$ to exchange $S_{xi}$ with $S_{ix}$.

citations.quote: Assume AC. Let $N,M$ be connected nonempty compact oriented smooth three-manifolds, with their boundaries identified with the same oriented surface $\Sigma$ in the bordism convention and with fixed compatible product collars. There is a finite framed link in $\operatorname{int}N$ whose surgery is diffeomorphic to $M$ with the prescribed external boundary parametrization. It may be realized as a four-dimensional two-handle trace with those marked horizontal faces and vertical collar $\Sigma\times[0,1]$. More generally this holds componentwise for a specified common component partition; empty input is treated by the empty union. In particular a fixed connected standard base with the required boundary may be chosen on each component, and a closed component may use $N=S^3$. An explicit connected standard base is the complement in $S^3$ of standard handlebodies placed in pairwise disjoint balls, one for each boundary component with its specified genus, with the given surface parametrizations attached to these boundary copies. This is relative surgery existence, not equivalence or completeness of surgery moves. Decorations may be carried by the resulting actual diffeomorphism; a complete decorated move theorem is a separate assertion.

Assume AC. Let $N$ be a connected nonempty compact oriented three-manifold and let $W_0,W_1$ be connected four-dimensional finite two-handle traces from that same fixed base. Their full common boundary $Y$ and all horizontal, external and corner collar identifications are marked. Suppose a connected compact oriented five-bordism $V$ between them is supplied with its full vertical product collar $Y\times I$ fixed. Then finitely many O3 insertions on each original framed link give two descriptions of the same actual four-dimensional two-handle trace $W_*$ from $N$, with the full marked boundary retained. Here each O3 insertion is a framed knot and its small disk-framed zero meridian, with its actual boundary-relative identification. No condition on any fundamental group is required. In conjunction with the projective-plane stabilization supplier, split signed unit-framed unknot insertions first supply such a $V$ whenever needed. This is a common-middle existence assertion; it does not assert that the two descriptions of $W_*$ are related by a complete O2/O3 movie.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge4$, and let $V$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional bordism with corners, horizontal faces $A_0,A_1$, and vertical face $B\times[0,1]$, with compatible product collar charts fixed. Here $\partial A_i=B\times\{i\}$. There are excellent Morse data with all critical points interior, equal to the specified height $t$ on a fixed smaller vertical product collar, zero and one on the horizontal faces with their prescribed inward collar models. They give a finite handle decomposition whose attaching thickenings lie in the interiors of horizontal levels, away from the fixed vertical collar, retaining the actual outgoing identification. Critical values may be ordered by index while this entire boundary height is fixed. If $V,A_0,A_1$ are connected and $A_0,A_1$ are nonempty, there is such a relative presentation with no handles of index zero or $d$. No fundamental-group assumption or h-cobordism hypothesis is imposed.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(W;M_0,M_1)$ be a compact triad and let $f$ be
an adapted Morse function whose critical points of index $k$ all lie at one
level $c\in(0,1)$, with no critical point of another index at $c$ and no other
critical value in a neighbourhood of $c$. Then the
sublevel just above $c$ is obtained from the sublevel just below $c$ by
attaching disjoint $k$-handles, one for each index-$k$ critical point.
Equivalently, handles of equal index attached at one level may be regarded as
attached simultaneously or successively in any order, the result being the same
up to diffeomorphism fixing the incoming face and respecting the lower sublevel up to homotopy of pairs. On the common attached-stage model, reordering disjoint attachments fixes its entire lower stage. Handles of equal index may
be reordered freely, and attaching embeddings may be changed by isotopy of the
attaching region.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $N$ be compact with $\partial N=\partial_-N\sqcup\partial_+N$, and let $f_N:N\to[0,1]$ be Morse, with $f_N^{-1}(1)=\partial_+N$ and $f_N=1-t$ on a critical-point-free outgoing collar. Attach a $k$-handle along an admissible framed embedding $h:S^{k-1}\times D^{n-k}\to\partial_+N$, obtaining $N'$. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ there is a Morse $f':N'\to[0,1]$, equal to $f_N$ on the part of $N$ outside the outgoing collar strip $t<2\varepsilon$ and near $\partial_-N$, whose old critical points and critical values are unchanged and whose only new critical point has index $k$ and value $1-\varepsilon/2$. Its endpoint fibre at one is the new outgoing face, and $f'=1-t'$ on a smaller outgoing collar. Its handle attachment is the prescribed one, up to compatible collar and corner choices.

The height of the whole old outgoing face must be lowered before the new critical band is glued. Pointwise agreement on that face, or identification of every saddle level with a product attaching tube, is not asserted.

Assume full AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $n$-manifold, $n\ge1$, with fixed product collars, and let $f_0,f_1:W\to[0,1]$ be excellent adapted Morse functions equal to the same noncritical product height on those collars. There is a smooth path $F_s$ joining them, stationary near its parameter endpoints and fixed on smaller boundary collars, with finitely many exceptional parameters. Each exceptional parameter contains exactly one of: a corank-one interior birth/death with nonzero kernel cubic and nonzero parameter unfolding, or a transverse crossing of two nondegenerate critical values. All other critical points are nondegenerate, all other critical values are distinct, no two events share a parameter, and a birth value differs from every other critical value. The critical locus is a compact smooth curve whose parameter projection has only nondegenerate folds. Each fold creates or destroys two critical points of adjacent indices with distinct critical values. By a homotopy supported near each fold, preserving this event list and the endpoints, the path can further be put near that fold in smooth parameter-dependent spatial coordinates into the form

$$F_s=a(s)+b(s)u+c_0u^3+Q(y),\qquad b(0)=0,\quad b'(0)\ne0,\quad c_0>0,$$

where $Q$ is a fixed nondegenerate quadratic form in $n-1$ variables. Empty ends, disconnected $W$, and index $0/n$ pairs are allowed. This is a function-path statement with fixed product height; it has no boundary critical events and asserts no global descending-field or surgery-move theorem.

Assume full AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional collared bordism, $d\ge1$, and let $f_s$ be a path supplied by [[lem-relative-one-parameter-morse-path-with-finite-events]], with the given noncritical height fixed on the spatial collars. Prescribe descending endpoint fields, stationary near the parameter ends, standard near their Morse critical points, and having no trajectories from index $i$ to index $j\ge i$. Morse–Smale endpoint fields suffice. Then there is a smooth descending family $X_s$ with those endpoint and collar values such that:

1. Near every fold it is the negative Euclidean gradient of the exact cubic model. At every regular critical point it has a smooth hyperbolic descending model. Near each same-index passage it may be taken to have the normalized linear Morse model at the destination.
2. No ordinary trajectory increases index. The entire family has finitely many same-index connecting trajectories; each occurs at a distinct parameter away from births and critical-value crossings. Each is a transverse parameter passage: on an incoming section at its destination, the $i-1$ source-sphere tangent directions together with the parameter direction map isomorphically onto the $i$-dimensional normal space of the stable section.
3. A sufficiently small parameter neighborhood of each birth contains no same-index trajectory. Between its two newborn critical points there is exactly the standard cancelling trajectory.
4. In successive one-critical elementary bands, the full framed attaching embeddings and actual outgoing boundary maps vary smoothly on each regular function chamber, including through positive-index-drop tangencies. The existing elementary birth and critical-value-crossing comparisons retain their actual outgoing maps, and their composition retains the terminal boundary parametrization.

Disconnected $W$, empty ends, and index $0/d$ births are allowed. This is an elementary-band assertion: it neither asserts slice-wise Morse–Smale transversality at positive index drops nor supplies parameterwise grouping of arbitrary based handle presentations by index or a global Kirby completeness theorem.

Assume AC. Let $(F_s,X_s)$ be the weak relative descending family of [[lem-relative-descending-path-with-finite-same-index-passages]] on a compact $d$-dimensional collared bordism. Its vertical product height and endpoint fields are fixed. There is a smooth family $g_s$ with the same critical points, indices and exact positive-affine cubic birth models, such that $X_sg_s<0$ off the critical points and all critical heights are ordered by index. The boundary height is unchanged. The family has finitely many simple same-index critical-value crossings, no triple values or simultaneous two crossings, and no such crossing at a same-index trajectory event or at a fold. The only other coincidences are the intended folds. The trajectories, their finite same-index passages, full framed local data and actual terminal identifications are retained. Positive-index-drop tangencies are allowed.

Assume AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth four-dimensional bordism with fixed horizontal faces, fixed vertical product height, and specified all-two-handle endpoint presentations. Apply the finite weak descending-path supplier and its parametric index grouping, with the endpoint fields prescribed from those presentations. Then there is a finite based framed mixed-handle movie joining the given endpoint presentations. Its elementary changes are framed isotopies, same-index handle slides (index3 read as the reverse index1 slide), cancelling adjacent-index births/deaths and commuting critical-value interchanges of disjoint attachments. Older attachments may pass through a birth block; the finite normalizing slides and actual cancellation maps are retained. Every higher attaching embedding and the complete terminal parametrization are carried by the actual outgoing comparisons. All supports fix the vertical boundary collar. No slicewise Morse–Smale condition at positive index drop is required.

Assume AC. Let $N,M$ be connected nonempty compact oriented smooth three-manifolds with their external boundary parametrizations and vertical product collar fixed. Let $W$ be a connected compact oriented four-bordism between them. Suppose two specified all-two-handle presentations of $W$ are joined by the finite index-grouped based mixed-handle movie of [[lem-index-grouped-relative-descending-paths-give-based-framed-handle-movies]], with its actual terminal maps. Their framed links in $N$ are related by finite exterior framed isotopies and $O2/O3$ moves. The cumulative outgoing map is the comparison prescribed by that marked movie, up to isotopy fixed on the protected collar. Here $O2$ is the specified framed component band slide; $O3$ inserts or deletes an arbitrary framed knot and its small disk-zero meridian. Intermediate four-dimensional traces may change by the displayed interior surgeries. No assumption that diffeomorphic four-dimensional two-handlebodies are two-equivalent is made. The construction works componentwise with a fixed matching component partition.

Let $Y$ be a compact oriented smooth three-manifold with prescribed boundary parametrizations and a fixed product collar $C\subset Y$. Surgery links lie in $\operatorname{Int}(Y\setminus C)$. For a framed link $L$, let $Y_L$ be its Dehn filling, with the canonical unchanged collar $C$, and let $E_L=Y\setminus\operatorname{Int}N(L)$ denote its exterior. The meridian of the $i$th filling solid torus is glued to the surgery-framed parallel $\lambda_i$ on $\partial N(L_i)$.

A decoration is a finite properly embedded oriented framed ribbon graph, with fixed abstract coupon set, actual coupon morphisms and band labels, fixed attachment order, and prescribed product ribbons in $C$ meeting only the designated marked boundary intervals. Colored graph isotopies keep all these collars, endpoints and labels fixed. Then:

1. Every decoration in $Y_L$ has a representative in $\operatorname{Int}(E_L)\cup C$, relative to its prescribed collar ribbons.
2. Two such exterior decorations that are isotopic as framed labeled graphs in $Y_L$ are connected by finitely many exterior framed colored graph isotopies and framed slides of open graph strands over the surgery parallels $\lambda_i$. Original coupons and colors remain fixed.
3. Suppose the **marked undecorated relative surgery calculus** holds in $Y$: every required collared bordism has a marked surgery presentation, and every specified orientation-preserving identification of two outputs, fixed pointwise on $C$, is realized up to isotopy relative to $C$ by a finite sequence of the canonical local undecorated moves $O1$ (a separated $\pm1$ unknot), $O2$ (a framed surgery-component band slide), $O3$ (a framed knot plus a small zero-framed meridian), and exterior link isotopies. The canonical move maps are the standard local filling identifications, identity outside their specified local neighborhoods. Under exactly this hypothesis, every marked decorated bordism admits an exterior decorated presentation, and two presentations of the same marked decoration are connected by the corresponding undecorated moves, exterior colored graph isotopies, and the open-colored-strand slides in (2).

The hypothesis in (3) concerns the **specified** output identification, not merely existence of some diffeomorphism. No undecorated completeness theorem is proved or assumed silently here. After surgery components are colored by $\Omega$, all the extra graph moves in this conclusion preserve the complete fixed-coupon evaluation by [[lem-kirby-color-full-band-slide-and-coupon-identity]]; the usual local $O1/O2/O3$ normalization identities are separate algebraic suppliers. Connectedness is not required.

derivations.claim: **Marked surgery existence in the fixed base.** On one connected component apply [F1] to the actual $N$ and $M$ with their given boundary parametrizations. Its marked closed-cap filling, interior one/three-handle trades and full framed-link consolidation give a four-dimensional two-handle trace $W$ from $N$ and a finite link $L\subset\operatorname{int}N$ with the specified outgoing identification $N_L\to M$. This does not identify three-dimensional surface handle attachments with four-dimensional link handles: the dimension-changing bridge is the actual four-bordism and disk-factor construction inside [F1]. The standard-complement base in the Statement exists by placing the standard handlebodies in disjoint balls of $S^3$ and keeping their explicit boundary parametrizations; its complement is connected. For a closed component use $S^3$. Pull the actual ribbon graph back by the given output identification; the independent exterior-representative part of [F6] moves its finite framed spine off the filling cores and radially out of the filling tori, with its endpoint ribbons and coupons retained. This gives the stated decorated presentation and all its markings.

**The common actual trace with the prescribed output map.** First disregard the graph, and let $L_0,L_1$ be two link presentations with the specified comparison of their output three-manifolds fixed pointwise on the external collar. Form their four-dimensional two-handle traces $W_0,W_1$ from the same $N$. Their entire three-boundary is $Y=(-N)\cup(\partial N\times I)\cup M$, with the given output comparison used on its $M$ face and the identity on the incoming $N$ face. Thus $Y$ is an actual marked common boundary, not merely a common diffeomorphism type. By [F2], first add split signed unit-framed unknots as needed for the signature correction and then finite $O3$ pairs from the two ends. The resulting links describe the same actual middle trace $W_*$ with this entire marked boundary. Every move has its boundary-relative local identification, so the original prescribed output map is retained in the two descriptions.

**A finite based movie on that trace.** Construct the endpoint data from each supplied two-handle presentation of $W_*$ as follows. Use [F3]'s common simultaneous attached-stage model, with its disjoint actual framed attaching tubes. On each tube use its quadratic two-handle band $Q(x,y)=-|x|^2+|y|^2$, normalized to have the same critical height $c$; glue their side product coordinates to the unchanged regular complement. This is the explicit parallel version of the local band construction in [F3]: its angular coordinates and $y$ disk factor give exactly the prescribed attaching tube and its full framing. All these local bands lie off the protected vertical collar, where the complement keeps the given height. The resulting Morse function $H$ has only index2 critical points, all at $c$. Choose its descending field $X$ standard near every quadratic origin, using the displayed quadratic flow and its regular side-height field, and patch them in the regular complement by positive descending combinations. Thus $dH(X)<0$ away from the critical points and the prescribed vertical product field is retained. There is no $2\to2$ trajectory: a nonconstant descending orbit strictly lowers $H$, while both endpoint critical values would be $c$. Choose disjoint bumps $\rho_j$ supported in the critical blocks, equal to one near their origins, and put $F=H+\sum_j\delta_j\rho_j$ with distinct sufficiently small constants $\delta_j$. On each transition annulus the compact support has a positive minimum of $-dH(X)$ and a finite bound for $|d\rho_j(X)|$; choose the constants so $\sum_j|\delta_jd\rho_j(X)|<-dH(X)/2$ there. Near each critical origin the bump is constant, so its Hessian and the field model are unchanged. Hence $X$ remains descending for the excellent endpoint function $F$, with the SAME trajectories as for $H$, and still has no same-index orbit. There is no index-increasing orbit because there are no critical points of another index. With no handles use the regular product data. The actual band gluing and unchanged flow carry the endpoint framed attaching data and outgoing map from the given presentation; changing the local critical values inserts only its recorded regular-level comparisons. Extend these endpoint pairs constantly on small parameter-end neighborhoods. Use the fixed corner/vertical face convention of [F3]. The finite generic function path and the actual weak descending-path supplier give finitely many function events and finitely many isolated equal-index trajectory events, with exact local birth models and the complete elementary outgoing maps. Apply [F4] to order index heights while keeping that field and the vertical height. Its finite height-jet construction ensures that all new same-index value crossings are finite, simple and separated from the trajectory events. Its based-movie bridge transports the full unstable thickenings to the common cuts in uniformly finite time, isolates the unique equal-index passage, uses the reversed index1 calculation for index3, and includes the necessary slides of older attachments through a cancelling birth block. All later attaching embeddings and terminal maps are carried by those actual comparisons. Hence the precise finite based mixed-handle movie required by [F5] has been proved, rather than inferred from function genericity.

**Marked undecorated completeness.** Apply [F5] to the movie in step 3.1. Rooted-tree collapse, dual three-handle trades, forward one-handle trades and every change of arc or flattening produce the stated finite $O2/O3$ moves, retaining their actual cumulative output map. Its four-dimensional levels may change by interior framed circle surgeries; no assertion that arbitrary diffeomorphic two-handlebodies are two-equivalent is being used. Compose with the $O1/O3$ sequences from step 2.1, reversing the sequence from the second end. The resulting finite $O1/O2/O3$ and isotopy sequence begins at $L_0$, ends at $L_1$, and realizes exactly the specified output identification up to isotopy fixed on the external collar. This proves the marked undecorated calculus required in [F6], for arbitrary compact connected oriented $N$ and arbitrary fundamental-group classes.

**Decorations and actual coupon data.** Invoke the decorated lifting conclusion of [F6] only after step 4.1 has discharged its hypothesis. At each canonical local $O1/O2/O3$ map it gives a finite exterior graph preparation and carries the resulting graph through that very map. The final transported graph is isotopic in the filled output to the prescribed final graph, since the cumulative output identification is the specified one. Its independent graph/core crossing argument converts that isotopy to finite exterior colored framed graph isotopies and slides over the actual surgery longitudes. All original coupons remain the same morphisms, with their attachment order, orientations, colors and complete framings; all collar ribbons and endpoints are fixed. This proves the full decorated statement. No scalar evaluation or variable-coupon naturality is substituted for graph-move completeness.

**Components and external weighted data.** Compactness gives finitely many connected components. Perform step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1 separately on the fixed matching component partition and take their finite disjoint union. Surgery and all the local moves preserve this partition. An empty bordism uses the empty link and empty move sequence; an empty incoming or outgoing surface merely removes that boundary face, while a closed component still has its nonempty fixed base $S^3$. The collars used throughout are noncritical product heights, so no boundary critical-point event or reparametrization of a fixed cap has been introduced. Every external boundary handlebody, its parametrization and its marked cap ribbons remain the chosen ones. Any integer weight and object Lagrangians are carried unchanged because the theorem compares geometric presentations of the same weighted morphism; the anomaly and evaluation identities are separate consumer results. This proves every stated case.

citations.quote:
A **multifusion category** is a finite semisimple multitensor category. A
**fusion category** is a finite semisimple tensor category. In particular the
unit of a fusion category is simple, whereas a multifusion unit may split.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a rigid monoidal category, let $a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ and $b:Y\to Y^{\vee\vee}$, and suppress the monoidal and chosen-dual comparison maps. For $s\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)$ write $\ell_Z(s)$ and $r_Z(s)$ for its left and right actions on $Z$, transported from $s\otimes1_Z$ and $1_Z\otimes s$ by the unit constraints.

1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.
   If $r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))=\ell_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))$, this becomes
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
   In particular multiplicativity holds when every unit scalar has equal left and right actions on every object. This condition holds in a braided category, and also in a $k$-linear monoidal category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$.
4. For every endomorphism $c:X\to X$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$.

The corresponding right-trace duality, additivity and cyclicity statements hold. For right-trace inputs $p:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$ and $q:Y^{\vee\vee}\to Y$, the general tensor formula is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(q\ell_{Y^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_R(p))).$$

It reduces to multiplicativity under the analogous equality of scalar actions, in particular under either sufficient condition above.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a spherical tensor category over an algebraically closed field $k$, with spherical structure $a$.
For every object $X$ and every endomorphism $x:X\to X$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}_L(a_Xx)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(xa_X^{-1}).$$

Let $\mathcal C$ be the spherical ribbon fusion category of [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. For simple labels $i,j$,

$$s_{ij}=(\theta_i\theta_j)^{-1}\sum_k N_{ij}^k\theta_kd_k,$$

and, for simple labels $x,i,j$,

$$s_{xi}s_{xj}=d_x\sum_kN_{ij}^ks_{xk}.$$

Also $s_{ij}=s_{ji}$, $s_{i^*j^*}=s_{ij}$, $s_{i0}=d_i$, and $d_{i^*}=d_i$. Consequently $h_x(i)=s_{xi}/d_x$ extends linearly to a unital ring character of the fusion ring.

Assume full AC. Let $M:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ be any compact oriented smooth three-bordism with its fixed product collars, boundary parametrizations and a properly embedded finite colored framed ribbon graph with actual coupon morphisms and the prescribed labeled boundary ribbons. For each connected component of $M$, fix a connected standard base $N$ with exactly that parametrized external boundary: for example the complement in $S^3$ of disjoint standard handlebodies, one of the prescribed genus for each boundary component. Keep these boundary handlebodies, their attaching parametrizations and their marked cap ribbons fixed. A closed component uses $N=S^3$. Take the finite disjoint union with this specified component partition. More generally, any fixed connected compact oriented base with the same marked boundary is allowed on each component.

There is a finite framed link $L\subset\operatorname{int}N$, off the protected boundary collar, an exterior representative of the given colored ribbon graph with all original coupons, and a specified orientation-preserving output identification $N_L\to M$ retaining every boundary parametrization and collar ribbon. Here $N_L$ is the framed Dehn filling of the link exterior. For any two such presentations, the **specified** identification of their outputs is realized up to isotopy fixed on the protected collar by a finite sequence of exterior framed isotopies and the following relative moves:

1. $O1$: insert or delete a split $+1$ or $-1$ framed unknot in an interior ball, with the actual filled-ball identification.
2. $O2$: the specified framed band slide of one surgery component over another, with the full band framing and canonical local filling comparison.
3. $O3$: insert or delete an arbitrary integer-framed knot $K$ and its small meridian $U$ with the disk framing zero; the induced filling identification is the identity outside its solid-torus support.
4. Exterior framed colored graph isotopy and framed slides of open graph strands over the specified surgery-framed longitudes. Every original graph label, coupon morphism, attachment order, boundary ribbon and endpoint remains fixed or is transported by the recorded move map.

Thus the cumulative move map, with its transported graph, realizes the given marked decorated bordism, including its specified output identification. No hypothesis on any fundamental group is imposed. $O3$ is essential in this general fixed-base scope and is not silently replaced by a split Hopf pair or by $O1/O2$ alone. All supports fix the given external collars; no unproved variable-boundary slicing move list is required. Disconnected bordisms, empty input/output surfaces, closed components, empty graphs and the empty bordism are allowed, with the fixed component partition. Any integer weight and object Lagrangians of the weighted ribbon-bordism definition are retained as part of the external data; this is a presentation and move theorem, independently of the later evaluation and anomaly formulas.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals. Consider finite oriented framed ribbon graphs with boundary collars, bands colored by arbitrary objects of $\mathcal C$, and coupons colored by arbitrary morphisms between the tensor products of their incident signed objects. There is a unique monoidal evaluation assigning each coupon its declared morphism, crossings the braiding or its correctly typed inverse, cups/caps the chosen duality maps and their ribbon-induced opposite variants, and full twists $\theta^{\pm1}$. It is invariant under every boundary-relative framed graph isotopy and preserves composition, tensor product and the empty graph. In a strict model it is strict monoidal; transport gives the corresponding strong monoidal evaluation in $\mathcal C$.

More precisely, for a signed list $A=(Y_1^{\epsilon_1},\ldots,Y_p^{\epsilon_p})$, put $|A|=\bigotimes_sY_s^{\epsilon_s}$, with $Y^-=Y^*$. For a coupon $f:|A|\to|B|$, its strand passages and full rotation are the complete composites

$$c_{|B|,Z}(f\otimes1_Z)=(1_Z\otimes f)c_{|A|,Z},\qquad c_{Z,|B|}(1_Z\otimes f)=(f\otimes1_Z)c_{Z,|A|},\qquad\theta_{|B|}f\theta_{|A|}^{-1}=f.$$

Their tensor-list expansions, all inverse-crossing versions and the explicit dual-mate formulas supply every coupon move; the claim includes zero-input/output coupons and all band orientations. No assumption that all colors are tensor powers of one object is imposed.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex finite semisimple spherical ribbon category with simple unit and finite simple-label set $I$, with every $d_i\ne0$. Put $\Omega=\sum_i d_i i$ and use the multicolored arbitrary-coupon evaluator of [[lem-multicolored-ribbon-coupon-evaluation]]. The entire graph evaluation is unchanged under a framed band slide of one $\Omega$-colored surgery component over another. It is also unchanged under sliding an open strand of any fixed color, or a strand of an arbitrary coupon-bearing colored graph, over an $\Omega$-colored surgery component, keeping every original color and coupon morphism fixed. All exterior crossings, open boundary factors and coupons are included, not merely a meridian scalar or closed trace. Orientations may be reversed with dual labels; no positivity or unitarity is assumed.

Here is the exact algebraic contract. Let $B=\bigoplus_i i^*\otimes i$ with inclusions $\iota_i$. Define $\iota_X,\Delta,\varepsilon,m$ by the finite formulas in the proof, and put $\Lambda=\sum_i d_i\iota_i b_i^R$. Then

$$m(1_B\otimes\Lambda)=\Lambda\varepsilon,\qquad\Gamma=(1_B\otimes m)(\Delta\otimes1_B),\qquad\Gamma(1_B\otimes\Lambda)=1_B\otimes\Lambda,\qquad\Gamma(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda)=\Lambda\otimes\Lambda.$$

For a fixed object $Y$ the lifted open-strand operator, retaining its entire first tensor factor, is

$$\widehat\Gamma_Y=(1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes m)(1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes\iota_Y\otimes1_B)(1_{Y^*}\otimes b_Y\otimes1_Y\otimes1_B),$$

and it satisfies $\widehat\Gamma_Y(1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes\Lambda)=1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes\Lambda$. Its exterior requires dinaturality only in the surgery-component variable; there is no naturality assumption on an arbitrary family of graph coupons indexed by $Y$. This lemma has no Gauss-sum, Fenn–Rourke, surgery normalization or topological move-completeness premise.

Let $\mathcal C$ be modular with $p_\pm=\sum_i\theta_i^{\pm1}d_i^2$, $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2$, and $\kappa=p_+/D$. Then

$$p_+p_-=D^2,\qquad \kappa^{-1}=p_-/D.$$

The formal Kirby color is $\Omega=\sum_i d_i\,i$. A zero-framed $\Omega$ meridian around a simple strand $j$ acts by $D^2\delta_{j,0}$ times the identity, and a $\pm1$-framed $\Omega$ unknot evaluates to $p_\pm$. Hence the surgery normalization

$$\tau(M_L)=D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F(L_\Omega)$$

is invariant under adding/removing a disjoint $\pm1$-framed $\Omega$ unknot; it gives $\tau(S^3)=D^{-1}$ and $\tau(S^2\times S^1)=1$. The same normalized graph evaluation is invariant under full framed surgery-component handle slides and colored-strand slides over surgery components, with all arbitrary exterior graph coupons retained. A topological theorem asserting completeness of these and relative moves is a separate supplier.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex modular spherical ribbon fusion category. Put $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2$, choose $D\ne0$, let $p_\pm=\sum_i\theta_i^{\pm1}d_i^2$, $\kappa=p_+/D$, and $\Omega=\sum_i d_i i$. Write $b_X:\mathbf1\to X\otimes X^*$ and $e_X:X^*\otimes X\to\mathbf1$ for left duality, $r_X=e_{X^*}(j_X\otimes1)$ for right evaluation, and $b_X^R=(1\otimes j_X^{-1})b_{X^*}$ for right coevaluation. For $a:X\otimes Z\to Y\otimes Z$ define

$$\operatorname{ptr}_Z(a)=(1_Y\otimes r_Z)(a\otimes1_{Z^*})(1_X\otimes b_Z),\qquad M_{X,Z}=c_{Z,X}c_{X,Z}.$$

Then $p_+p_-=D^2$, and the following are identities of complete morphisms, valid with arbitrary exterior tensor factors and coupons:

$$K_\pm(X):=\sum_i d_i\theta_i^{\pm1}\operatorname{ptr}_i(M_{X,i}^{\pm1})=p_\pm\theta_X^{\mp1}.$$

The zero-framed meridian operator $E_X=\sum_i d_i\operatorname{ptr}_i(M_{X,i})$ equals $D^2P_X$, where $P_X$ is the projection onto the full unit-isotypic summand. For $a\in\operatorname{End}(i^*\otimes j)$ define

$$R_{ij}(a)=(r_i\otimes1_j\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes a\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes1_{i^*}\otimes b_j).$$

The paired-handle/coupon contraction is

$$R_{ij}(E_{i^*\otimes j})=\delta_{ij}\frac{D^2}{d_i}1_{i\otimes i^*}.$$

Thus the normalized graph evaluation $D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F$ is unchanged under a signed generalized Fenn–Rourke twist-surgery move or circumcision adding a framed knot and its small zero-framed meridian. These are local algebraic identities; a complete presentation/move theorem is a separate topological assertion. No positivity, unitary conjugation, or anomaly cancellation is assumed.

Use the category, $D,d_i,\kappa$ and dualities of [[lem-colored-fr-surgery-and-coupon-cancellation]]. For a connected standard genus-$g$ marked surface $t$, put

$$X_{t,i}=W_1^{\epsilon_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes W_n^{\epsilon_n}\otimes\bigotimes_{r=1}^g(i_r\otimes i_r^*),\qquad V_t=\bigoplus_{i\in I^g}\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X_{t,i}),\qquad d(i)=\prod_r d_{i_r}.$$

For disjoint surfaces take tensor products and set $V_\varnothing=\mathbb C$. Opposite raw coupon coordinates are $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_{t,i},\mathbf1)$, with composition pairing. With the standard spine handlebody caps and their reflected opposite caps, the normalized capped-cylinder Gram pairing is

$$Q_t(y_j,x_i)=\delta_{ij}D^{g-1}d(i)^{-1}y_ix_i.$$

Its inverse correction is $N_t|_i=D^{1-g}d(i)1$, extended multiplicatively across surface components. For a fixed special surgery graph $\Omega$ representing a connected parametrized graph bordism $M$, let $m$ and $B$ be its surgery-component count and linking matrix. Define $A_M$ by the raw testing-coupon functional $y(A_Mx)=D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F(\Omega;y,x)$, with finite surgery-color sum understood, and set $Z_\alpha(M)=N_{\Sigma_{\rm out}}A_M$. Then

$$Z_\alpha(M)^j_i=\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}D^{-m-1+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)F_0(\Omega;i,j).$$

Here $\alpha$ denotes the actual reference cap meridians and $F_0$ includes the exact tensor-Hom projections defined below. These fixed-presentation operators satisfy the cylinder, ball, empty and disjoint-union laws. For stacked presentations of composable bordisms,

$$Z_\alpha(M_2M_1)=\kappa^{\sigma(B_1)+\sigma(B_2)-\sigma(B_{\rm comp})}Z_\alpha(M_2)Z_\alpha(M_1).$$

The signatures here are the actual matrices, including the indicated added annuli. No Maslov identification is assumed in this lemma. For disconnected $M$, use the product over its connected components, equivalently the exponent $-m-b_0(M)+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2$. Independence under a complete relative presentation calculus is a separate theorem; this result proves the exact normalization and algebra of its local cap/stacking models. No unweighted anomaly-free functor is asserted.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Decompose $X$ as $\mathbf1^{\oplus r}\oplus\bigoplus_{i\ne0}i^{\oplus r_i}$ using [F1]. The unit-copy inclusions $x_a$ and projections $y^a$ satisfy $y^ax_b=\delta_{ab}$ and identify the two Hom spaces with $\mathbb C^r$ and its full dual. Every other simple summand contributes zero. Thus composition is perfect, including $r=0$. Trace additivity, multiplicativity and $d_{i^*}=d_i$ give $\operatorname{tr}(1_{i\otimes i^*})=d_i^2$ and $\operatorname{tr}(1_H)=D^2$. This is a categorical closed trace; it does not identify a geometric opposite-cap pairing with that trace.

By [F2] choose an actual presentation of each connected component with its fixed boundary handlebodies and testing coupons. The finite evaluation [F3] is linear in each coupon. Perfectness from step 1.1 therefore determines a unique raw operator from its testing functional. The tensor-Hom inclusions and unit-channel projections of [F5] retain exactly the tensor product of connected state spaces at a disconnected boundary. The calculation of [F5] gives $Q,N$ as displayed: its full meridian identity kills unmatched handle tuples and contributes $D^{2g}/d(i)$ on a matched tuple; its cylinder has $g$ zero-framed surgery annuli, hence multiplying by $D^{-g-1}$ gives $Q$. All $D,d_i$ are nonzero. Applying the inverse $N$ produces the unique normalized map and not merely a scalar class of maps.

Test two presentations against the same arbitrary incoming and outgoing coupons. By [F2], their specified marked identification is a finite sequence of the actual moves listed there. An O1 move adds $m\mapsto m+1$, $\sigma\mapsto\sigma+\epsilon$ and evaluation factor $p_\epsilon=D\kappa^\epsilon$, so its normalized multiplier is $D^{-1}\kappa^{-\epsilon}p_\epsilon=1$. O2 changes the linking matrix by an integral unimodular band congruence, hence keeps signature and $m$; its complete coupon-bearing evaluation is unchanged by [F3]. For O3 the added $K_f,U_0$ block has linking form $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}f&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ after separating its two core directions from the old form by completing squares. That block has determinant $-1$ and signature zero; the count increases by two. The full circumcision identity [F4] multiplies evaluation by $D^2$, canceling $D^{-2}$. This identity applies to the arbitrary knot and to every exterior color/coupon in the actual support. Exterior isotopy is [F3]; an open strand over a surgery longitude is precisely its lifted open-strand/coupon identity after bending the fixed strand and applying the actual exterior coupons. It is not an assumption that arbitrary coupon families are dinatural. Thus every allowed move preserves every tested normalized functional.

[F2] retains the complete output identification, all collar ribbons and fixed caps, so the comparison in step 3.1 applies to these exact testing states, with no unnoticed boundary mapping class. It follows by perfectness that the operators agree. Changing a computational coupon basis replaces $x_a$ by $\sum_bx_bA_{ba}$ and $y^a$ by $\sum_b(A^{-1})_{ab}y^b$; the complete finite identity resolution $\sum_ax_ay^a$ is unchanged. Object simple-summand resolutions are unchanged by the same matrix calculation. Actual coupon morphisms remain fixed. Therefore all auxiliary decompositions used in the computation give the same map. This establishes existence, uniqueness and the asserted full presentation independence.

Apply [F5] to a cylinder and to the two empty-graph balls: the cylinder word $D^{2g}/d(i)$ multiplied by $D^{-2g}d(i)$ is the identity on every multiplicity block, the outgoing ball is $1\in\mathbb C$, the incoming ball is multiplication by $D^{-1}$, and their glued sphere is $\tau(S^3)=D^{-1}$. Empty bordism gives $1$ and disjoint union tensors all factors. These are now laws of the well-defined operators, since step 4.1 allows their local models as presentations of any such bordism.

Likewise choose the actual stacked presentations in [F5] for arbitrary composable bordisms. Their cap-annulus, disconnected-family projectors and all $N$ factors prove $Z_\alpha(M_2M_1)=\kappa^{\sigma(B_1)+\sigma(B_2)-\sigma(B_{\rm comp})}Z_\alpha(M_2)Z_\alpha(M_1)$. Replacing any of these presentations preserves both sides by step 4.1; thus this is a law for the constructed maps. [F5] includes disconnected incidence components, empty surfaces and singular linking matrices, so no connectedness, positivity or nonsingularity restriction is introduced. This proves every stated assertion while leaving only the separately specified signature-to-Maslov identification to its actual supplier.

An object is a closed oriented surface $\Sigma$ with a fixed finite collection of marked points carrying simple labels of the complex modular ribbon fusion category, together with a Lagrangian subspace $\lambda\subset H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb R)$ for the signed intersection form. An elementary morphism is an oriented compact smooth 3-bordism $M:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ with product collars and fixed boundary parametrizations, a properly embedded colored ribbon graph whose ends match the marked labels, and an integer weight $n\in\mathbb Z$. Reversing a boundary orientation dualizes its labels.

For any closed oriented surface $\Sigma$, the intersection convention is $\omega_\Sigma([\alpha],[\beta])=$ the signed intersection number in which the tangent to $\alpha$ followed by the tangent to $\beta$ gives the surface orientation. For a bordism $M:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$, write $j_r$ for the inclusion maps into $H_1(M;\mathbb R)$ and set

$$\Lambda_M=\{(x_0,x_1)\in H_1(\Sigma_0;\mathbb R)\oplus H_1(\Sigma_1;\mathbb R):j_0x_0=j_1x_1\}.$$

Give the product the form $-\omega_{\Sigma_0}\oplus\omega_{\Sigma_1}$. The boundary-kernel lemma applied to $\partial M$ gives the relation with $j_0x_0=-j_1x_1$; changing the sign of the second coordinate is symplectic and gives exactly $\Lambda_M$. Hence $\Lambda_M$ is Lagrangian ([[lem-3-manifold-boundary-kernel-is-lagrangian]]).

For composable bordisms $M_1:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ and $M_2:\Sigma_1\to\Sigma_2$, put $A=\Lambda_{M_1}$ and $B=\Lambda_{M_2}$. For a relation $R\subseteq\overline V\oplus W$, write $R(L)=\{w:\exists v\in L,(v,w)\in R\}$ and $R^t(Q)=\{v:\exists w\in Q,(v,w)\in R\}$. These use the inclusion maps into each individual bordism. The three Lagrangians for composition lie in the middle surface:

$$K_1=A(\lambda_0),\qquad K_0=\lambda_1,\qquad K_2=B^t(\lambda_2)\quad\subseteq H_1(\Sigma_1;\mathbb R).$$

They are Lagrangian by [[lem-lagrangian-relation-sends-lagrangian-to-lagrangian]], applied also to the transposed relation. With the Wall-form sign fixed in [[lem-maslov-index-four-lagrangian-cocycle]], define

$$n(M_2\circ M_1)=n_2+n_1+\mu(K_1,K_0,K_2).$$

For mapping cylinders of symplectic maps $f_1,f_2$, the index is $\mu(f_1\lambda_0,\lambda_1,f_2^{-1}\lambda_2)=\mu(f_2f_1\lambda_0,f_2\lambda_1,\lambda_2)$. This is Walker's prescribed sign and order. For arbitrary bordisms, replacing the individual relations by homology maps into the glued manifold is not part of the definition.

Identity bordisms are cylinders with weight zero. Disjoint union takes the disjoint union of geometric data, the direct sum of the surface Lagrangians, and the sum of weights. The empty surface is the monoidal unit. Bordisms are identified by orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms respecting collars, parametrizations, ribbon data and weights; smoothing glued collars is understood up to these identifications. Associativity and the weight, unit and disjoint-union laws follow from the relation identity in [[lem-maslov-correction-composes-for-lagrangian-relations]] and the proof below. This defines the weighted category before any RT functor is asserted. The equality between its correction and a surgery-signature defect remains a separate obligation of [[thm-weighted-rt-tqft-and-factorization]]; no unweighted TQFT is asserted.

Assume full AC. Let $M:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ be any compact oriented smooth three-bordism with its fixed product collars, boundary parametrizations and a properly embedded finite colored framed ribbon graph with actual coupon morphisms and the prescribed labeled boundary ribbons. For each connected component of $M$, fix a connected standard base $N$ with exactly that parametrized external boundary: for example the complement in $S^3$ of disjoint standard handlebodies, one of the prescribed genus for each boundary component. Keep these boundary handlebodies, their attaching parametrizations and their marked cap ribbons fixed. A closed component uses $N=S^3$. Take the finite disjoint union with this specified component partition. More generally, any fixed connected compact oriented base with the same marked boundary is allowed on each component.

There is a finite framed link $L\subset\operatorname{int}N$, off the protected boundary collar, an exterior representative of the given colored ribbon graph with all original coupons, and a specified orientation-preserving output identification $N_L\to M$ retaining every boundary parametrization and collar ribbon. Here $N_L$ is the framed Dehn filling of the link exterior. For any two such presentations, the **specified** identification of their outputs is realized up to isotopy fixed on the protected collar by a finite sequence of exterior framed isotopies and the following relative moves:

1. $O1$: insert or delete a split $+1$ or $-1$ framed unknot in an interior ball, with the actual filled-ball identification.
2. $O2$: the specified framed band slide of one surgery component over another, with the full band framing and canonical local filling comparison.
3. $O3$: insert or delete an arbitrary integer-framed knot $K$ and its small meridian $U$ with the disk framing zero; the induced filling identification is the identity outside its solid-torus support.
4. Exterior framed colored graph isotopy and framed slides of open graph strands over the specified surgery-framed longitudes. Every original graph label, coupon morphism, attachment order, boundary ribbon and endpoint remains fixed or is transported by the recorded move map.

Thus the cumulative move map, with its transported graph, realizes the given marked decorated bordism, including its specified output identification. No hypothesis on any fundamental group is imposed. $O3$ is essential in this general fixed-base scope and is not silently replaced by a split Hopf pair or by $O1/O2$ alone. All supports fix the given external collars; no unproved variable-boundary slicing move list is required. Disconnected bordisms, empty input/output surfaces, closed components, empty graphs and the empty bordism are allowed, with the fixed component partition. Any integer weight and object Lagrangians of the weighted ribbon-bordism definition are retained as part of the external data; this is a presentation and move theorem, independently of the later evaluation and anomaly formulas.

Fix a complex modular ribbon fusion category as in [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]], with finite simple-label set $I$, tensor unit $\mathbf1$, and dual label $i^*$ for each $i$. Define the **handle object**

$$H=\bigoplus_{i\in I}i\otimes i^*.$$

For an oriented marked surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g$ with ordered marked points labeled by objects $W_1,\ldots,W_n$, fix a parametrization and the standard handle decomposition used to read its labels. The associated algebraic state space is

$$V(\Sigma;W_1,\ldots,W_n)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}\!\left(\mathbf1,\, W_1\otimes\cdots\otimes W_n\otimes H^{\otimes g}\right).$$

The empty tensor product is $\mathbf1$ and $H^{\otimes0}=\mathbf1$. Reversing the orientation of a marked boundary circle replaces its label $W$ by the left dual $W^*$. This formula defines a vector space only; mapping-class operators, bordism maps, independence of parametrization, and gluing are not asserted here.

Assume full AC and its inherited countable-choice consequences. For the state spaces of [[def-rt-state-spaces]], composition is a perfect pairing

$$\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X)\times\operatorname{Hom}(X,\mathbf1)\longrightarrow\mathbb C,\qquad(v,w)\longmapsto wv.$$

The categorical trace of $1_{i\otimes i^*}$ is $d_i^2$, and $\operatorname{tr}(1_H)=\sum_i d_i^2=D^2$ for $H=\bigoplus_i i\otimes i^*$. Distinguish that trace from the actual standard-cap geometric Gram form on a connected genus-$g$ surface:

$$Q_t(y_j,x_i)=\delta_{ij}D^{g-1}d(i)^{-1}y_ix_i,\qquad N_t|_i=Q_t^{-1}|_i=D^{1-g}d(i)1.$$

Here $i$ is the full handle-color tuple, $d(i)=\prod_r d_{i_r}$, and the inverse is in composition-dual coordinates. For disconnected surfaces take tensor products and empty value $\mathbb C$.

For every compact parametrized colored ribbon bordism, capping against all testing states, taking the surgery-color sum with closed normalization $D^{-m-b_0(M)}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}$, and applying $N_{\rm out}$ defines a unique linear map $Z_\alpha(M)$. It is independent of the marked surgery presentation, all auxiliary coupon bases and their complete identity resolutions. It retains the prescribed boundary caps, parametrizations, colors and actual coupon morphisms. These maps satisfy the cylinder, ball, empty and disjoint-union laws, and the actual stacked-presentation law of [[lem-rt-capped-operator-normalization-and-composition]]. The identification of its signature defect with the Maslov correction is a separate supplier.

Use the category, $D,d_i,\kappa$ and dualities of [[lem-colored-fr-surgery-and-coupon-cancellation]]. For a connected standard genus-$g$ marked surface $t$, put

$$X_{t,i}=W_1^{\epsilon_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes W_n^{\epsilon_n}\otimes\bigotimes_{r=1}^g(i_r\otimes i_r^*),\qquad V_t=\bigoplus_{i\in I^g}\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X_{t,i}),\qquad d(i)=\prod_r d_{i_r}.$$

For disjoint surfaces take tensor products and set $V_\varnothing=\mathbb C$. Opposite raw coupon coordinates are $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_{t,i},\mathbf1)$, with composition pairing. With the standard spine handlebody caps and their reflected opposite caps, the normalized capped-cylinder Gram pairing is

$$Q_t(y_j,x_i)=\delta_{ij}D^{g-1}d(i)^{-1}y_ix_i.$$

Its inverse correction is $N_t|_i=D^{1-g}d(i)1$, extended multiplicatively across surface components. For a fixed special surgery graph $\Omega$ representing a connected parametrized graph bordism $M$, let $m$ and $B$ be its surgery-component count and linking matrix. Define $A_M$ by the raw testing-coupon functional $y(A_Mx)=D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F(\Omega;y,x)$, with finite surgery-color sum understood, and set $Z_\alpha(M)=N_{\Sigma_{\rm out}}A_M$. Then

$$Z_\alpha(M)^j_i=\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}D^{-m-1+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)F_0(\Omega;i,j).$$

Here $\alpha$ denotes the actual reference cap meridians and $F_0$ includes the exact tensor-Hom projections defined below. These fixed-presentation operators satisfy the cylinder, ball, empty and disjoint-union laws. For stacked presentations of composable bordisms,

$$Z_\alpha(M_2M_1)=\kappa^{\sigma(B_1)+\sigma(B_2)-\sigma(B_{\rm comp})}Z_\alpha(M_2)Z_\alpha(M_1).$$

The signatures here are the actual matrices, including the indicated added annuli. No Maslov identification is assumed in this lemma. For disconnected $M$, use the product over its connected components, equivalently the exponent $-m-b_0(M)+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2$. Independence under a complete relative presentation calculus is a separate theorem; this result proves the exact normalization and algebra of its local cap/stacking models. No unweighted anomaly-free functor is asserted.

Assume AC, carried through Poincaré–Lefschetz duality. Use outward-normal-first boundary orientations and the Walker Maslov form: on triples $a_1+a_2+a_3=0$, $a_i\in L_i$, it is $\psi(a,a')=\omega(a_1,a_2')$, with signature $\mu_W(L_1,L_2,L_3)$ after removing the radical.

If an oriented four-manifold is decomposed as $W=W_1\cup_{M_0}W_2$, with

$$\partial W_1=M_0\cup(-M_1),\qquad\partial W_2=(-M_0)\cup M_2,\qquad\Sigma=\partial M_0=\partial M_1=\partial M_2,$$

put $K_i=\ker[H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb R)\to H_1(M_i;\mathbb R)]$. Then

$$\sigma(W)=\sigma(W_1)+\sigma(W_2)-\mu_W(K_1,K_0,K_2).$$

For the actual standard-cap special-graph stacking presentations of [[lem-rt-capped-operator-normalization-and-composition]], let $\alpha_q$ be the meridian Lagrangians of the chosen reference caps and $R_q$ the individual bordism homology relations. With the canonical middle-object orientation, the actual surgery signatures satisfy

$$\Delta\sigma:=\sigma(B_{\rm comp})-\sigma(B_1)-\sigma(B_2)=\mu_W(R_1\alpha_0,\alpha_1,R_2^t\alpha_2)=:\mu_\alpha.$$

For arbitrary real object Lagrangians $\lambda_q$, define the actual cap-reference integer

$$a(R;\lambda,\alpha)=-\mu_W(\lambda_0,\alpha_0,R^t\alpha_1)-\mu_W(R\lambda_0,\alpha_1,\lambda_1).$$

It satisfies $a(BA)-a(B)-a(A)=\mu_\alpha-\mu_\lambda$, where $\mu_\lambda=\mu_W(A\lambda_0,\lambda_1,B^t\lambda_2)$. Consequently the correctly weighted operators are

$$Z(M,n;\lambda)=\kappa^{n+a(R_M;\lambda,\alpha)}Z_\alpha(M),\qquad n_{\rm comp}=n_2+n_1+\mu_\lambda.$$

They compose strictly, preserve the identity and tensor laws, and a unit increase of weight acts by $\kappa$. In particular the action $\kappa^{-n}$ is incompatible with this prescribed $+\mu_W$ composition and the fixed surgery normalization $\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}$. These are normalization/signature claims for the indicated presentations; the full relative surgery/Cerf completeness theorem remains separate.

Fix a complex modular ribbon fusion category and its state-space convention in [[def-rt-state-spaces]], with $H=\bigoplus_i i\otimes i^*$ and $S=s/D$. On a disconnected surface take the tensor product of the connected Hom state spaces, with empty value $\mathbb C$. Write $r_i:i\otimes i^*\to\mathbf1$ and $b_i^R:\mathbf1\to i^*\otimes i$ for the corresponding right evaluation and coevaluation. With fixed tensor order and parametrizations, separating sewing is the isomorphism

$$G:\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X\otimes i)\otimes\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,i^*\otimes Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X\otimes Y),\qquad G_i(f\otimes k)=(1_X\otimes r_i\otimes1_Y)(f\otimes k).$$

For any simple-summand inclusions $g_{i\alpha}:i^*\to X$ and composition-dual projections $p_{i\alpha}:X\to i^*$, its inverse is

$$F(z)=\sum_{i,\alpha}((g_{i\alpha}\otimes1_i)b_i^R)\otimes((p_{i\alpha}\otimes1_Y)z).$$

For nonseparating sewing the direct-sum inclusions/projections $u_i:i\otimes i^*\to H$, $v_i:H\to i\otimes i^*$ give mutually inverse maps

$$G((z_i)_i)=\sum_i(1_X\otimes u_i)z_i,\qquad F(z)=((1_X\otimes v_i)z)_i.$$

These maps retain every multiplicity coordinate, are independent of auxiliary bases, are natural on uncut factors, and commute for disjoint cut pairs with fixed compatible tensor order. Thus iterated algebraic sewing has the explicit reverse cutting inverse. For simple marked labels,

$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,i_1\otimes\cdots\otimes i_n\otimes H^{\otimes g})=\sum_x S_{0x}^{\,2-2g-n}\prod_{r=1}^n S_{i_rx}.$$

These are algebraic state-space identities. Identification with presentation-independent bordism sewing requires the separately constructed RT functor; no surgery move theorem is a hypothesis or conclusion here.

$$\operatorname{ptr}_Z(a)=(1_Y\otimes r_Z)(a\otimes1_{Z^*})(1_X\otimes b_Z),\qquad M_{X,Z}=c_{Z,X}c_{X,Z}.$$

$$K_\pm(X):=\sum_i d_i\theta_i^{\pm1}\operatorname{ptr}_i(M_{X,i}^{\pm1})=p_\pm\theta_X^{\mp1}.$$

$$R_{ij}(a)=(r_i\otimes1_j\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes a\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes1_{i^*}\otimes b_j).$$

The paired-handle/coupon contraction is

$$R_{ij}(E_{i^*\otimes j})=\delta_{ij}\frac{D^2}{d_i}1_{i\otimes i^*}.$$

Thus the normalized graph evaluation $D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F$ is unchanged under a signed generalized Fenn–Rourke twist-surgery move or circumcision adding a framed knot and its small zero-framed meridian. These are local algebraic identities; a complete presentation/move theorem is a separate topological assertion. No positivity, unitary conjugation, or anomaly cancellation is assumed.

derivations.claim: [F1] presents every specified decorated bordism, componentwise and with its actual boundary maps. [F2] constructs a unique presentation-independent operator $Z_\alpha(M)$ from all capped tests and applies $N_{\rm out}$. Its outgoing block is exactly $\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}D^{-m-b_0(M)+\chi_{\rm out}/2}d(j)F_0$. Multiply by $\kappa^{n+a(R_M;\lambda,\alpha)}$ to obtain the displayed formula. The relation $R_M$ and the chosen real Lagrangians depend only on the actual bordism and its marked boundary, so the extra factor has no presentation dependence. It is defined even when no handlebody realizes $\lambda$; only the actual reference $\alpha$ is represented by the caps. Write $A=R_{M_1}$ and $B=R_{M_2}$. The stacked law is $Z_\alpha(M_2M_1)=\kappa^{-\mu_\alpha}Z_\alpha(M_2)Z_\alpha(M_1)$ by [F2,F3]. The composite weight is $n_2+n_1+\mu_\lambda$. This proves strict composition for all individual relations, including noninjective ones and closed components of the composite. The identity relation has $a=0$; [F2]'s cylinder is the identity, so identities are preserved. No whole-composite kernel is substituted for either individual relation.

Fix the standard separating tube connecting the two new dual boundary circles, keeping their tensor order. In the capped graph put all unrelated handle annuli in their standard disk products. Applying [F5] to each annulus gives $D^2/d_i$ on its matched color channel and zero on unmatched channels. The complete product is precisely the Gram factor $Q$ computed by [F2]; its outgoing correction $N=Q^{-1}$ cancels it. Consequently its actual normalized map is $G_i(f\otimes k)=(1_X\otimes r_i\otimes1_Y)(f\otimes k)$, with the parentheses and dualities of [F4]. For a nonseparating tube the two added legs are one handle summand, so the remaining word is its actual inclusion $u_i:i\otimes i^*\to H$; summing gives $G((z_i))=\sum_i(1_X\otimes u_i)z_i$. All other outgoing $d$ factors have already been canceled by $N$ above. This is an identification with the geometric tube operator, not only an algebraic possible sewing map.

For disjoint union [F2] tensors state spaces, caps, complete unit-channel projections and graph evaluations, with exponent $-m-b_0(M)+\chi_{\rm out}/2$. The Maslov form and $a$ add on symplectic direct sums by [F3], and weights add in [F1]. Increasing $n$ by one multiplies the formula by $\kappa$, including for an empty underlying weighted bordism.

The explicit inverses are those of [F4]: for separating sewing, $F(z)=\sum_{i,\alpha}((g_{i\alpha}\otimes1_i)b_i^R)\otimes((p_{i\alpha}\otimes1_Y)z)$, where $g:i^*\to X$, $p:X\to i^*$ are complete simple-summand composition-dual maps. Thus each local comparison has a repeated pair in its Maslov triple and weight correction zero, so the calculations in step 2.2 have exactly the stated weight-zero normalization. This transports the same sewing maps through the corresponding weighted reference-change cylinders, rather than assuming arbitrary real Lagrangians are geometric caps.

The oppositely oriented labeled surface is the categorical dual object in the bordism category: the bent product cylinder gives evaluation and coevaluation with the actual reversed boundary labels.
