Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit $\mathbf 1$ and a finite set $I$ of isomorphism classes of simple objects. Fix a braiding $c$ and a ribbon twist $\theta$. The induced pivotal map is $j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, where $u$ is the Drinfeld morphism of [[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Throughout this pair we use the associated spherical pivotal structure: $j$ is part of the data, and sphericality means $\dim_j(X)=\dim_j(X^\vee)$ for every object, as in [[def-spherical-structure]]. Its trace is $\operatorname{tr}_j(f)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_Xf)$ for $f\in\operatorname{End}(X)$.

Write $0$ for the unit label and $i^*$ for the dual of $i$. Put $N_{ij}^k=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}(k,i\otimes j)$, $d_i=\operatorname{tr}_j(1_i)$, and $s_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}_j(c_{j,i}c_{i,j})$. Define $D^2=\sum_{i\in I}d_i^2$. The unnormalized Hopf-link matrix is $s=(s_{ij})$. The ribbon fusion category is **modular** when $s$ is invertible. When $D^2\ne0$, either square root $D$ defines the normalized matrix $S=s/D$; for a modular category, [[lem-modular-hopf-matrix-squared]] proves this nonvanishing. No positivity of the general $d_i$ or of $D$ is assumed.

Let $\mathcal C$ be modular under [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. Let $C$ be the charge-conjugation matrix, $C_{ij}=\delta_{i,j^*}$. Then

$$s^2=D^2C.$$

In particular $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2\ne0$, so either square root $D$ gives an invertible normalized matrix $S=s/D$ with $S^2=C$.

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, written additively. A normalized **abelian 3-cocycle** is a pair of functions $\omega:G^3\to\mathbb C^\times$ and $r:G^2\to\mathbb C^\times$, equal to $1$ whenever one of their arguments is $0$, satisfying the pentagon equation

$$\omega(a,b,c)\omega(a,b+c,d)\omega(b,c,d)=\omega(a+b,c,d)\omega(a,b,c+d)$$

and the two braided hexagon equations

$$\omega(b,c,a)\omega(a,b,c)r(a,b+c)=r(a,b)r(a,c)\omega(b,a,c),$$

$$r(a+b,c)=\omega(a,b,c)\omega(c,a,b)\omega(a,c,b)^{-1}r(a,c)r(b,c).$$

The associated pointed category has one simple object $g$ in each grade $g\in G$, tensor product $g\otimes h=g+h$, associator $\alpha_{g,h,k}:(g\otimes h)\otimes k\to g\otimes(h\otimes k)$ given by scalar $\omega(g,h,k)$, and braiding $c_{g,h}:g\otimes h\to h\otimes g$ given by scalar $r(g,h)$. For the left dual $g^\vee=-g$, take evaluation $g^\vee\otimes g\to0$ to have scalar $1$ and coevaluation $0\to g\otimes g^\vee$ to have scalar $\omega(g,-g,g)^{-1}$. The first snake is the identity by this choice; the second is the identity because the normalized pentagon at $(g,-g,g,-g)$ gives $\omega(g,-g,g)\omega(-g,g,-g)=1$. A ribbon twist is a function $q:G\to\mathbb C^\times$ with $q(0)=1$, $q(-g)=q(g)$, and

$$q(g+h)=r(g,h)r(h,g)q(g)q(h).$$

Write $b(g,h)=r(g,h)r(h,g)$ for the double-braiding scalar. The pointed ribbon category data include a compatible pivotal structure whose twist is $q$ and whose simple dimensions are $1$; this convention is an explicit input, not a consequence of the quadratic function alone. [[thm-pointed-metric-group-is-modular-iff-radical-trivial]] proves from the two hexagons that $b$ is a symmetric bicharacter and that the Hopf-link matrix has entries $s_{gh}=b(g,h)$. A quadratic function alone is not the category data: the associator, both hexagons, duality maps, and the stated pivotal convention are part of the definition.

Let $(G,\omega,r,q)$ be pointed ribbon data as in [[def-pointed-metric-group-ribbon-category]], and let $b(g,h)=r(g,h)r(h,g)$. The associated pointed ribbon fusion category is modular if and only if

$$\operatorname{rad}(b)=\{g\in G:b(g,h)=1\text{ for every }h\in G\}=\{0\}.$$

Fix a complex modular ribbon fusion category and its state-space convention in [[def-rt-state-spaces]], with $H=\bigoplus_i i\otimes i^*$ and $S=s/D$. On a disconnected surface take the tensor product of the connected Hom state spaces, with empty value $\mathbb C$. Write $r_i:i\otimes i^*\to\mathbf1$ and $b_i^R:\mathbf1\to i^*\otimes i$ for the corresponding right evaluation and coevaluation. With fixed tensor order and parametrizations, separating sewing is the isomorphism

$$G:\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X\otimes i)\otimes\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,i^*\otimes Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X\otimes Y),\qquad G_i(f\otimes k)=(1_X\otimes r_i\otimes1_Y)(f\otimes k).$$

For any simple-summand inclusions $g_{i\alpha}:i^*\to X$ and composition-dual projections $p_{i\alpha}:X\to i^*$, its inverse is

$$F(z)=\sum_{i,\alpha}((g_{i\alpha}\otimes1_i)b_i^R)\otimes((p_{i\alpha}\otimes1_Y)z).$$

For nonseparating sewing the direct-sum inclusions/projections $u_i:i\otimes i^*\to H$, $v_i:H\to i\otimes i^*$ give mutually inverse maps

$$G((z_i)_i)=\sum_i(1_X\otimes u_i)z_i,\qquad F(z)=((1_X\otimes v_i)z)_i.$$

These maps retain every multiplicity coordinate, are independent of auxiliary bases, are natural on uncut factors, and commute for disjoint cut pairs with fixed compatible tensor order. Thus iterated algebraic sewing has the explicit reverse cutting inverse. For simple marked labels,

$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,i_1\otimes\cdots\otimes i_n\otimes H^{\otimes g})=\sum_x S_{0x}^{\,2-2g-n}\prod_{r=1}^n S_{i_rx}.$$

These are algebraic state-space identities. Identification with presentation-independent bordism sewing requires the separately constructed RT functor; no surgery move theorem is a hypothesis or conclusion here.

Assume full AC and its inherited countable-choice consequences. Let $\mathcal C$ be any complex modular ribbon fusion category, with fixed $D\ne0$, $\kappa=p_+/D$, the state spaces of [[def-rt-state-spaces]] and the weighted collared ribbon-bordism category of [[def-weighted-lagrangian-ribbon-bordism]]. No unitarity, positivity or anomaly-cancellation hypothesis is imposed. For each parametrized connected boundary surface choose its standard spine caps, with meridian Lagrangian $\alpha$; the object may carry any real Lagrangian $\lambda$. Use the Walker Maslov convention and actual cap-reference correction $a(R;\lambda,\alpha)$ of [[lem-wall-signature-and-rt-cap-reference-correction]].

A connected surgery presentation with $m$ surgery components, linking matrix $B$ and integer bordism weight $n$ has the exact outgoing color-block operator

$$Z(M,n;\lambda)^j_i=\kappa^{n+a(R_M;\lambda,\alpha)-\sigma(B)}D^{-m-1+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)F_0(\Omega;i,j).$$

Here $F_0$ is the finite colored graph operator with the disconnected-boundary unit-channel projections of [[lem-rt-capped-operator-normalization-and-composition]], and $d(j)$ is the product of outgoing handle-color dimensions. For disconnected $M$ use the product over its connected components, equivalently replace $-m-1$ by $-m-b_0(M)$; the external weight contributes the single factor $\kappa^n$. The empty value is $\mathbb C$.

These maps are independent of all marked surgery presentations and auxiliary coupon bases and define a symmetric monoidal functor on the full specified weighted category, including actual colored coupons, disconnected bordisms and empty ends. The functor preserves duality. A unit increase of weight acts by $\kappa$. No ordinary anomaly-free functor is asserted without cancellation of this anomaly.

For every compatible circle cut there is a natural factorization isomorphism

$$V(\Sigma_{\rm glued};\vec W)\cong\bigoplus_{i\in I}V(\Sigma_{\rm cut};\vec W,i,i^*).$$

The sewing map from right to left is the actual normalized tube map; its inverse is the complete composition-dual cutting resolution. Both separating and nonseparating cuts, all multiplicities, commuting disjoint cuts and iterated gluing are included. Markings, tensor order and the Lagrangian identifications of the cut are retained; a change of parametrization is represented by its weighted mapping cylinder.

Use the category, $D,d_i,\kappa$ and dualities of [[lem-colored-fr-surgery-and-coupon-cancellation]]. For a connected standard genus-$g$ marked surface $t$, put

$$X_{t,i}=W_1^{\epsilon_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes W_n^{\epsilon_n}\otimes\bigotimes_{r=1}^g(i_r\otimes i_r^*),\qquad V_t=\bigoplus_{i\in I^g}\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X_{t,i}),\qquad d(i)=\prod_r d_{i_r}.$$

For disjoint surfaces take tensor products and set $V_\varnothing=\mathbb C$. Opposite raw coupon coordinates are $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_{t,i},\mathbf1)$, with composition pairing. With the standard spine handlebody caps and their reflected opposite caps, the normalized capped-cylinder Gram pairing is

$$Q_t(y_j,x_i)=\delta_{ij}D^{g-1}d(i)^{-1}y_ix_i.$$

Its inverse correction is $N_t|_i=D^{1-g}d(i)1$, extended multiplicatively across surface components. For a fixed special surgery graph $\Omega$ representing a connected parametrized graph bordism $M$, let $m$ and $B$ be its surgery-component count and linking matrix. Define $A_M$ by the raw testing-coupon functional $y(A_Mx)=D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F(\Omega;y,x)$, with finite surgery-color sum understood, and set $Z_\alpha(M)=N_{\Sigma_{\rm out}}A_M$. Then

$$Z_\alpha(M)^j_i=\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}D^{-m-1+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)F_0(\Omega;i,j).$$

Here $\alpha$ denotes the actual reference cap meridians and $F_0$ includes the exact tensor-Hom projections defined below. These fixed-presentation operators satisfy the cylinder, ball, empty and disjoint-union laws. For stacked presentations of composable bordisms,

$$Z_\alpha(M_2M_1)=\kappa^{\sigma(B_1)+\sigma(B_2)-\sigma(B_{\rm comp})}Z_\alpha(M_2)Z_\alpha(M_1).$$

The signatures here are the actual matrices, including the indicated added annuli. No Maslov identification is assumed in this lemma. For disconnected $M$, use the product over its connected components, equivalently the exponent $-m-b_0(M)+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2$. Independence under a complete relative presentation calculus is a separate theorem; this result proves the exact normalization and algebra of its local cap/stacking models. No unweighted anomaly-free functor is asserted.

Assume AC, carried through Poincaré–Lefschetz duality. Use outward-normal-first boundary orientations and the Walker Maslov form: on triples $a_1+a_2+a_3=0$, $a_i\in L_i$, it is $\psi(a,a')=\omega(a_1,a_2')$, with signature $\mu_W(L_1,L_2,L_3)$ after removing the radical.

If an oriented four-manifold is decomposed as $W=W_1\cup_{M_0}W_2$, with

$$\partial W_1=M_0\cup(-M_1),\qquad\partial W_2=(-M_0)\cup M_2,\qquad\Sigma=\partial M_0=\partial M_1=\partial M_2,$$

put $K_i=\ker[H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb R)\to H_1(M_i;\mathbb R)]$. Then

$$\sigma(W)=\sigma(W_1)+\sigma(W_2)-\mu_W(K_1,K_0,K_2).$$

For the actual standard-cap special-graph stacking presentations of [[lem-rt-capped-operator-normalization-and-composition]], let $\alpha_q$ be the meridian Lagrangians of the chosen reference caps and $R_q$ the individual bordism homology relations. With the canonical middle-object orientation, the actual surgery signatures satisfy

$$\Delta\sigma:=\sigma(B_{\rm comp})-\sigma(B_1)-\sigma(B_2)=\mu_W(R_1\alpha_0,\alpha_1,R_2^t\alpha_2)=:\mu_\alpha.$$

For arbitrary real object Lagrangians $\lambda_q$, define the actual cap-reference integer

$$a(R;\lambda,\alpha)=-\mu_W(\lambda_0,\alpha_0,R^t\alpha_1)-\mu_W(R\lambda_0,\alpha_1,\lambda_1).$$

It satisfies $a(BA)-a(B)-a(A)=\mu_\alpha-\mu_\lambda$, where $\mu_\lambda=\mu_W(A\lambda_0,\lambda_1,B^t\lambda_2)$. Consequently the correctly weighted operators are

$$Z(M,n;\lambda)=\kappa^{n+a(R_M;\lambda,\alpha)}Z_\alpha(M),\qquad n_{\rm comp}=n_2+n_1+\mu_\lambda.$$

They compose strictly, preserve the identity and tensor laws, and a unit increase of weight acts by $\kappa$. In particular the action $\kappa^{-n}$ is incompatible with this prescribed $+\mu_W$ composition and the fixed surgery normalization $\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}$. These are normalization/signature claims for the indicated presentations; the full relative surgery/Cerf completeness theorem remains separate.

Let $(V,\omega)$ be a finite-dimensional real symplectic vector space and let $L_1,L_2,L_3$ be Lagrangian subspaces. Put

$$U_{123}=\frac{L_1\cap(L_2+L_3)}{(L_1\cap L_2)+(L_1\cap L_3)}.$$

For $a\in L_1\cap(L_2+L_3)$ write $a+b+c=0$ with $b\in L_2,c\in L_3$. The form

$$\psi_{123}([a],[a'])=\omega(a,b')$$

is well-defined, symmetric, and nondegenerate. Define $\mu(L_1,L_2,L_3)=\operatorname{sign}(\psi_{123})$. For any four Lagrangians,

$$\mu(L_1,L_2,L_3)+\mu(L_1,L_3,L_4)=\mu(L_1,L_2,L_4)+\mu(L_2,L_3,L_4).$$

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Fix the standard oriented solid torus $D^2\times S^1$, with $m$ the positive disk-boundary and $l$ the core direction. Its boundary orientation is $(m,l)$. The reference opposite-cap reflection acts on this basis by $r=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$. The positive Hopf gluing exchanges the meridian of one cap with the longitude of the other; its two disk-core orientations give the exchange matrix $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. Removing the fixed opposite reflection gives the stated $s_+$, since $rs_+$ is that exchange matrix. This fixes which Hopf generator is meant and its linking orientation. In particular $m\mapsto-l$, $l\mapsto m$, rather than the inverse convention. In the capped matrix coefficient use the composition-dual test $y_j=r_j/d_j$ because $r_jb_j=d_j$. The positive Hopf graph with these two coupons evaluates to $s_{ji}/d_j$. Its closed empty-surgery normalization is $D^{-1}$ and its outgoing torus correction from [F3] is $d_j$, giving exactly $S_{ji}=s_{ji}/D$. The positive core twist is the actual solid-torus map $(z,e^{i\phi})\mapsto(e^{i\phi}z,e^{i\phi})$, so $m\mapsto m$, $l\mapsto l+m$ and its core normal disk makes one positive full rotation. Put $A=s_+t=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\-1&-1\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. Direct multiplication gives $A^3=I$ and $s_+^2=-I$. Composing the weight-zero $s_+,t$ lifts introduces no weight because $t^{-1}\alpha=\alpha$, so its Maslov triple has a repeated argument. Thus $ST$ is the weight-zero lift of $A$. For its square the middle triple is $(A\alpha,\alpha,A^{-1}\alpha)=(\mathbb Rl,\mathbb Rm,\mathbb R(l-m))$. A sum-zero vector is $(-c l,c m,c(l-m))$, and its Walker form is $\omega(-c l,c'm)=cc'$, so this Maslov index is $+1$. For its third power the first and third lines coincide: $A^2\alpha=A^{-1}\alpha$. The next correction is zero. The weight-zero inverse lift of $s_+$ is $s_-=s_+^{-1}$: its inverse-composition correction has repeated first and third lines, so is zero. Its operator is consequently $S^{-1}$ by functoriality. Its cubed operator is therefore $\kappa Z(-I,0)=\kappa C$, proving the asserted inverse-generator alternative. Let $\ell\ge3$, $t=\pi/\ell$, and suppose a spherical ribbon fusion category has simple labels $a=0,\ldots,\ell-2$ with

$$N_{ab}^c=1\quad\text{for }c=|a-b|,|a-b|+2,\ldots,\min(a+b,2\ell-4-a-b),$$

and all other $N_{ab}^c=0$, with $d_a=\sin((a+1)t)/\sin t$ and $\theta_a=e^{it\,a(a+2)/2}$. Then

$$s_{ab}=\frac{\sin((a+1)(b+1)t)}{\sin t},\qquad D^2=\frac{\ell}{2\sin^2t},\qquad S_{ab}=\sqrt{\frac2\ell}\sin((a+1)(b+1)t).$$

The sine matrix is invertible and $S^2=I$. This is a conditional calculation from the displayed category data; it does not assert that a particular tilting quotient has those data.

Fix an integer $\ell\ge3$ and set $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, so the multiplicative order of $q^2$ is $\ell$. Use the divided-power integral form of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] from [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], specialized by $v\mapsto q$ to $\mathbb C$. In type $A_1$, write $K=K_h$ and $E,F$ for the rank-one generators. The convention is

$$KEK^{-1}=q^2E,\qquad KFK^{-1}=q^{-2}F,\qquad [E,F]=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}},$$

$$\Delta(K)=K\otimes K,\qquad \Delta(E)=E\otimes K+1\otimes E,\qquad \Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K^{-1}\otimes F.$$

This is the Sawin coproduct, rather than the inverse-$K$ coproduct in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Its counit is $\varepsilon(K)=1$, $\varepsilon(E)=\varepsilon(F)=0$ and its antipode is $S(E)=-EK^{-1}$, $S(F)=-KF$, $S(K)=K^{-1}$. The exact integral transport is from the library algebra with opposite coproduct, by $E_{\rm target}=KE_{\rm lib}$, $F_{\rm target}=F_{\rm lib}K^{-1}$ and $K_{\rm target}=K_{\rm lib}$. Substituting these generators gives the displayed coproduct and unchanged mixed relation. On divided powers the formulas are $E_{\rm target}^{(r)}=v^{-r(r-1)}K^rE_{\rm lib}^{(r)}$ and $F_{\rm target}^{(r)}=v^{r(r-1)}F_{\rm lib}^{(r)}K^{-r}$; the inverse formulas also have Laurent-monomial coefficients, so the integral lattice and toral generators are preserved.

The Lusztig specialization includes all divided powers $E^{(r)},F^{(r)}$ and the toral quantum binomials; this is the divided-power form, not the small quantum group. A finite-dimensional module is **type 1** when it carries its integral-weight grading $M=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}M_m$ with $K|_{M_m}=q^m$, the full toral character $T_{c,t}|_{M_m}=\begin{bmatrix}m+c\\t\end{bmatrix}_q I$ for every $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$, and $E^{(r)}M_m\subseteq M_{m+2r}$, $F^{(r)}M_m\subseteq M_{m-2r}$. The binomial is its Laurent-polynomial specialization, including negative upper indices. The grading is part of the data and is not collapsed when distinct weights have the same $K$ eigenvalue. Every module intertwiner preserves it: for $m<n$, $T_{-m,n-m}$ has eigenvalues $0$ and $1$ on weights $m$ and $n$.

For $a\ge0$, the Weyl module $\Delta(a)$ has basis $v_0,\ldots,v_a$ and actions

$$Kv_j=q^{a-2j}v_j,\qquad E^{(r)}v_j=\begin{bmatrix}a-j+r\\r\end{bmatrix}_qv_{j-r},\qquad F^{(r)}v_j=\begin{bmatrix}j+r\\r\end{bmatrix}_qv_{j+r},$$

where the Gaussian binomials are the Laurent-polynomial specializations of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]], and $v_j=0$ outside $0\le j\le a$. Its dual is the dual Weyl module $\nabla(a)=\Delta(a)^\vee$. A **Weyl filtration** (respectively dual-Weyl filtration) is a finite submodule filtration whose successive quotients are modules $\Delta(a)$ (respectively $\nabla(a)$). A **tilting module** is a module with both filtrations.

Take $s=e^{\pi i/(2\ell)}$, so $s^2=q$. The ribbon category is the full weight-lattice extension $\mathcal U_s^\dagger(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ of this Lusztig form, not its root-lattice restriction. Its toral factor is the completed function algebra on the weight lattice $P=\mathbb Z\omega$, acting on each weight space by its weight character. Before specialization, the rank-one universal $R$-matrix is the Sawin weight-lattice expression

$R=D\sum_{r\ge0}q^{r(r+1)/2}(1-q^{-2})^r[r]_q!E^{(r)}\otimes F^{(r)},\qquad D|_{M_m\otimes N_n}=s^{mn}.$

interpreted in the completed tensor product; at the root it means the image of the integral completed form, not termwise division by a vanishing $[r]_q!$. In ordinary powers the coefficient is $q^{r(r-1)/2}(q-q^{-1})^r/[r]_q!$; changing to two divided powers multiplies that coefficient by $([r]_q!)^2$. Thus the displayed divided-power coefficient is Laurent integral and vanishes for $r\ge\ell$ after specialization. The toral factor is the weight pairing, fixed explicitly by $D$ above. The pivotal map is $j_M(x)(\varphi)=\varphi(Kx)$ and the twist is $\theta=u^{-1}j$ for the Drinfeld map $u$. The object class of this page is the full subcategory of finite-dimensional integrable type-1 tilting modules for this weight-lattice ribbon extension. No assertion about semisimplicity or the trace radical is part of this definition.

Use the full integral-weight divided-power category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]], with $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$ and every $\ell\ge3$. The displayed strings define $\Delta(a)$, and $\nabla(a)=\Delta(a)^\vee$. For all $a,b\ge0$,

$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta(a),\nabla(b))=\delta_{ab},\qquad \operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta(a),\nabla(b))=0.$$

Here Ext vanishing means that every short exact sequence in the finite-dimensional full-weight category with those end terms splits. The tensor product $\Delta(a)\otimes\Delta(b)$ has one Weyl factor of each label $a+b,a+b-2,\ldots,|a-b|$, and the analogous dual-Weyl assertion holds. Both filtration classes are closed under direct summands. Thus tiltings are closed under tensor products, duals and direct summands. For every $a\ge0$ there is exactly one indecomposable tilting $T(a)$ of highest weight $a$; its weight-$a$ space is one-dimensional, and it occurs as a summand of $V^{\otimes a}$, where $V=\Delta(1)$. Every finite tilting is a finite direct sum of these $T(a)$, so the additive idempotent-complete tensor category generated by $V$ is the entire tilting category.

Let $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, and use the full-weight category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]]. Write $T(m)$ for the indecomposable tilting of highest weight $m$ and $\chi(m)=\sum_{j=0}^m e^{m-2j}$. For $a\ge1$ and $0\le b\le\ell-2$,

$$\operatorname{ch}T(a\ell+b)=\chi(a\ell+b)+\chi(a\ell-b-2),\qquad \operatorname{ch}T(a\ell-1)=\chi(a\ell-1).$$

Also $T(m)=\Delta(m)=\nabla(m)$ for $0\le m<\ell$. With the positive $K$ pivotal map, the dimension on a Weyl character is $[m+1]_q$. Consequently every $T(m)$ with $m\ge\ell-1$ has zero pivotal trace on **every** endomorphism, so its identity is negligible. In the retained range $0\le m\le\ell-2$, $T(m)$ is simple of nonzero pivotal dimension $[m+1]_q$.

For every $\ell\ge3$, let $\mathcal T_\ell$ be the full finite-dimensional integrable type-1 tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]], and $\mathcal N_\ell$ its negligible ideal. The quotient with the same objects and morphism spaces $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\ell}(X,Y)/\mathcal N_\ell(X,Y)$ is a finite semisimple ribbon category. Its simple objects are exactly $T(0),\ldots,T(\ell-2)$, of pivotal dimensions $[a+1]_q$, and

$$[T(a)][T(b)]=\sum_{\substack{|a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,2\ell-4-a-b)\\c\equiv a+b\ (2)}}[T(c)]\qquad(0\le a,b\le\ell-2).$$

Here a fusion category means a $\mathbb C$-linear rigid semisimple monoidal category with simple unit and finitely many simple isomorphism classes. The quotient is spherical with the specified positive pivotal dimensions and inherits the full ribbon structure, including even $\ell$.

For every $\ell\ge3$, the full tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]] is rigid and braided by $c_{M,N}=\operatorname{flip}\circ R_{M,N}$, where

$$R_{M,N}=D\sum_{r\ge0}q^{r(r+1)/2}(1-q^{-2})^r[r]_q!E_M^{(r)}\otimes F_N^{(r)},\qquad D|_{M_m\otimes N_n}=s^{mn}.$$

The sum is finite on every pair of objects. Its pivotal map is $j_M(x)(\varphi)=\varphi(Kx)$ and its ribbon twist is $\theta_M=u_M^{-1}j_M$, with $u$ the Drinfeld map. For $V=\Delta(1)$, the self-dual cup and cap are

$$w=v_+\otimes v_- -q^{-1}v_-\otimes v_+,\qquad b(v_+\otimes v_-)=-q,\quad b(v_-\otimes v_+)=1,$$

with $b(v_\pm\otimes v_\pm)=0$. They obey both snakes, $b(w)=-\delta$ and Frobenius–Schur sign $-1$ for $j$. Nevertheless $\dim_j V=\delta$. If $U=-wb$, then $U^2=\delta U$, the adjacent TL relations hold, and

$$c_{V,V}=sI-s^{-1}U,\qquad T=qU-I=-s\,c_{V,V}^{-1}.$$

The $\Delta(2)$ and trivial channels have crossing eigenvalues $s,-s^{-3}$ and Hecke eigenvalues $-1,q^2$, respectively. Their twists are $s^8,1$; $\theta_V=s^3I$. The $\Delta(2)$ channel is removed in the negligible quotient when $\ell=3$. More generally $\theta_{\Delta(a)}=s^{a(a+2)}I$ for $0\le a\le\ell-1$. These assertions include even $\ell$ and use no small-quantum-group substitution.

Use all $\ell\ge3$, $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $s=e^{\pi i/(2\ell)}$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$ and the full tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]]. Put $V=\Delta(1)$ and let $P_0$ be its trivial-channel projector in $V\otimes V=\Delta(2)\oplus\Delta(0)$. The maps

$$\rho_n:\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal T_\ell}(V^{\otimes n}),\qquad U_i\longmapsto\delta P_{0,i,i+1}$$

are well defined. Their composite with the negligible quotient has kernel exactly the embedded boundary ideal $I_n=(p_{\ell-1})$ and induces

$$\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)/I_n\ \cong\ \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal T_\ell/\mathcal N_\ell}(V^{\otimes n}).$$

Equivalently the target is the full centralizer on a chosen sum of the retained tilting summands. The unreduced map does **not** kill $p_{\ell-1}$: its image is the nonzero simple $\Delta(\ell-1)$.

The precise categorical comparison is with the additive Karoubi negligible quotient of $\mathrm{TL}(-\delta)$, equipped with its ordinary diagram braiding $c=s1+s^{-1}e$ and with planar pivotal structure multiplied by tensor parity $(-1)^n$. This is ribbon-equivalent to $\mathcal T_\ell/\mathcal N_\ell$. Its endomorphism algebras are identified with positive-loop TL algebras by $U_i=-e_i$. Its pivotal dimensions are $[a+1]_q$, and its twists on retained labels are $s^{a(a+2)}$. The quantum self-duality cup/cap have loop $-\delta$ and Frobenius–Schur sign $-1$, whereas the parity-corrected pivotal closure has value $+\delta$ on $V$. Thus no equivalence of the unmodified positive-loop unoriented **pivotal** TL category is asserted.

On the highest-weight-$2$ and trivial prequotient channels, the quantum crossing eigenvalues are $s,-s^{-3}$; the Hecke element $T_i=qU_i-1=-s c_i^{-1}$ has eigenvalues $-1,q^2$. The highest-weight-$2$ channel is retained only when $\ell\ge4$. Pivotal traces, twists and all framed ribbon closures agree under the stated corrected comparison. Assume countable choice only when invoking the cited free framed-tangle evaluation theorem; the local matrix and path arguments use no choice axiom.

For generic $q$, or whenever the quantum integers needed for $p_r,p_s,p_t$ are units, the unnormalized trivalent theta pairing satisfies

$$\Theta(r,s,t)=\frac{[m]![n']![p]![m+n'+p+1]!}{[m+n']![n'+p]![m+p]!},$$

where $m=(r+s-t)/2$, $n'=(s+t-r)/2$, $p=(t+r-s)/2$ are nonnegative integers. The vertices and exact unit domain are those of [[lem-temperley-lieb-general-theta-net-evaluation]]. At $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, and $0\le r,s,t\le\ell-2$, the pairing is positive when the triangle/parity conditions hold and $r+s+t\le2\ell-4$; it is zero for a triangle/parity triple above that level. A triple requiring an undefined root JW projector is not implicitly included.

Put $k=\ell-2$ and quotient the diagram category by the tensor ideal generated by $p_{k+1}$. A retained path of length $n$ is $a=(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$ with $a_0=0$, $0\le a_i\le k$ and $|a_i-a_{i-1}|=1$. There are inclusions $i_a:p_{a_n}\to n$ and retractions $r_a:n\to p_{a_n}$ such that $r_ai_b=0$ for distinct paths, $r_ai_a=p_{a_n}$, and $\sum_a i_ar_a=1_n$. Consequently the $E_{a,b}=i_ar_b$ at a common endpoint form complete matrix units, with

$$E_{a,b}E_{c,d}=\delta_{b,c}E_{a,d},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(E_{a,b})=\delta_{a,b}[a_n+1]_q.$$

Their pairing is nondegenerate. The endpoint $p_{k+1}$ is deleted before normalization; no denominator $[\ell]$ is used.

Let $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$ and $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. Put

$$\operatorname{Rad}(\tau_n)=\{x\in\mathrm{TL}_n:\tau_n(xy)=0\text{ for every }y\in\mathrm{TL}_n\}.$$

Let $I_n$ be the two-sided ideal generated by $p_{\ell-1}\otimes1_{n-\ell+1}$ for $n\ge\ell-1$, and $I_n=0$ below that rank. Then $I_n=\operatorname{Rad}(\tau_n)$, and $\mathrm{TL}_n/I_n$ is the direct sum of full matrix algebras with multiplicities given by length-$n$ paths from $0$ of heights $0,\ldots,\ell-2$. The additive idempotent-complete negligible quotient has simple labels $0,\ldots,\ell-2$, represented by $p_a$, and

$$a\otimes b\cong\bigoplus_{\substack{|a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,2\ell-4-a-b)\\c\equiv a+b\ (2)}}c.$$

At $n=\ell-1$ the unreduced algebra is semisimple, while its trace radical is the nonzero one-dimensional block generated by $p_{\ell-1}$. Trace radical and Jacobson radical are therefore distinct at this first boundary.

derivations.claim: By [F2], the full actual tilting category has its semisimple quotient with exactly the simple labels $0,\ldots,\ell-2$ and the complete truncated fusion multiplicities in [F1]. The all-endomorphism trace calculation kills every excluded indecomposable, not just its identity trace. Thus the quotient here is the actual category in the Statement, rather than a fusion ring substituted for it.

By [F3], its full braiding and ribbon structure descend from the integral finite R-series, and the pivotal conversion gives $d_a=[a+1]_q=\sin((a+1)\pi/\ell)/\sin(\pi/\ell)$ and $\theta_a=s^{a(a+2)}=q^{a(a+2)/2}$ with $s=e^{\pi i/(2\ell)}$. The self-dual cup/cap loop is $-\delta$ and the positive pivotal trace uses the proved parity conversion; no equivalence with unmodified positive-loop pivotal diagrams is assumed. The actual category therefore satisfies every hypothesis of [F1], for all $\ell\ge3$, including even $\ell$.

Apply [F1] to this actual spherical ribbon fusion category. It gives $s_{ab}=\sin((a+1)(b+1)\pi/\ell)/\sin(\pi/\ell)$ and $D^2=\ell/(2\sin^2(\pi/\ell))$. Choose its positive square root $D=\sqrt{\ell/2}/\sin(\pi/\ell)$; division gives exactly the displayed normalized $S$. Finite sine orthogonality gives $S^2=I$, so $S$ and $s$ are invertible. This establishes modularity of the actual quotient and all its stated data, without a source-only category premise or a TQFT assumption.

A **multifusion category** is a finite semisimple multitensor category. A
**fusion category** is a finite semisimple tensor category. In particular the
unit of a fusion category is simple, whereas a multifusion unit may split.

category ([[def-monoidal-category]]).

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit $\mathbf 1$ and a finite set $I$ of isomorphism classes of simple objects. Fix a braiding $c$ and a ribbon twist $\theta$. The induced pivotal map is $j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, where $u$ is the Drinfeld morphism of [[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Throughout this pair we use the associated spherical pivotal structure: $j$ is part of the data, and sphericality means $\dim_j(X)=\dim_j(X^\vee)$ for every object, as in [[def-spherical-structure]]. Its trace is $\operatorname{tr}_j(f)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_Xf)$ for $f\in\operatorname{End}(X)$.

derivations.claim:
By [F2], for any simple labels $i,j$, $s_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}(1_{i\otimes j})=d_i d_j=1$. In the ordered basis $(1,\varepsilon)$ this gives
$s=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.$
The two rows coincide, and $\det(s)=1\cdot1-1\cdot1=0$. Therefore $s$ is not invertible and the category is not modular. This shows why nondegeneracy must be a hypothesis or separately proved.

citations.quote: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, written additively. A normalized **abelian 3-cocycle** is a pair of functions $\omega:G^3\to\mathbb C^\times$ and $r:G^2\to\mathbb C^\times$, equal to $1$ whenever one of their arguments is $0$, satisfying the pentagon equation
Let $(G,\omega,r,q)$ be pointed ribbon data as in [[def-pointed-metric-group-ribbon-category]], and let $b(g,h)=r(g,h)r(h,g)$. The associated pointed ribbon fusion category is modular if and only if

derivations.claim:
Normalization holds because every exponent vanishes if any argument is $0$. For bits, $b+c$ in the cocycle equations is reduced modulo $2$. The pentagon signs have exponents
$abc+a(b+c)d+bcd=acd+bcd+abc+abd\pmod2,$
so its two sides agree. For the first hexagon, the ratio of the $r$-terms is $i^{-2abc}=(-1)^{abc}$, which is exactly the ratio of the $\omega$-terms. For the second hexagon, the ratio of the $r$-terms is again $i^{-2abc}=(-1)^{abc}$, equal to $\omega(a,b,c)\omega(c,a,b)\omega(a,c,b)^{-1}=(-1)^{abc}$. The twist equation is trivial if either bit is zero; at $(1,1)$ its right side is $r(1,1)^2q(1)^2=i^2i^2=1=q(0)$. Also $q(-g)=q(g)$. Thus all specified cocycle and twist identities hold.

The double-braiding values are $b(0,g)=b(g,0)=1$ and $b(1,1)=i^2=-1$. Hence
$s=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.$
The only nonzero element $1$ is not in the radical because $b(1,1)=-1\ne1$, so $\operatorname{rad}(b)=\{0\}$. By [F2] the category is modular; directly, $\det(s)=-2$ and $D^2=2$.

Let $\ell\ge3$, $t=\pi/\ell$, and suppose a spherical ribbon fusion category has simple labels $a=0,\ldots,\ell-2$ with

$$N_{ab}^c=1\quad\text{for }c=|a-b|,|a-b|+2,\ldots,\min(a+b,2\ell-4-a-b),$$

and all other $N_{ab}^c=0$, with $d_a=\sin((a+1)t)/\sin t$ and $\theta_a=e^{it\,a(a+2)/2}$. Then

$$s_{ab}=\frac{\sin((a+1)(b+1)t)}{\sin t},\qquad D^2=\frac{\ell}{2\sin^2t},\qquad S_{ab}=\sqrt{\frac2\ell}\sin((a+1)(b+1)t).$$

The sine matrix is invertible and $S^2=I$. This is a conditional calculation from the displayed category data; it does not assert that a particular tilting quotient has those data.

Let $\mathcal C$ be modular with $p_\pm=\sum_i\theta_i^{\pm1}d_i^2$, $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2$, and $\kappa=p_+/D$. Then

$$p_+p_-=D^2,\qquad \kappa^{-1}=p_-/D.$$

The formal Kirby color is $\Omega=\sum_i d_i\,i$. A zero-framed $\Omega$ meridian around a simple strand $j$ acts by $D^2\delta_{j,0}$ times the identity, and a $\pm1$-framed $\Omega$ unknot evaluates to $p_\pm$. Hence the surgery normalization

$$\tau(M_L)=D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F(L_\Omega)$$

is invariant under adding/removing a disjoint $\pm1$-framed $\Omega$ unknot; it gives $\tau(S^3)=D^{-1}$ and $\tau(S^2\times S^1)=1$. The same normalized graph evaluation is invariant under full framed surgery-component handle slides and colored-strand slides over surgery components, with all arbitrary exterior graph coupons retained. A topological theorem asserting completeness of these and relative moves is a separate supplier.

Let $\ell\ge3$, $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, and let $\mathcal C_\ell$ be the standard ribbon semisimplification of finite-dimensional integrable type-1 tilting modules for Lusztig's divided-power $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, using the positive-trace quantum ribbon convention. Then $\mathcal C_\ell$ is modular, with simples $a=0,\ldots,\ell-2$, dimensions $d_a=\sin((a+1)\pi/\ell)/\sin(\pi/\ell)$, twists $\theta_a=q^{a(a+2)/2}$, and

$$s_{ab}=\frac{\sin((a+1)(b+1)\pi/\ell)}{\sin(\pi/\ell)},\qquad S_{ab}=\sqrt{\frac2\ell}\sin\frac{(a+1)(b+1)\pi}{\ell}.$$

Assume full AC and its inherited countable-choice consequences. Let $\mathcal C$ be any complex modular ribbon fusion category, with fixed $D\ne0$, $\kappa=p_+/D$, the state spaces of [[def-rt-state-spaces]] and the weighted collared ribbon-bordism category of [[def-weighted-lagrangian-ribbon-bordism]]. No unitarity, positivity or anomaly-cancellation hypothesis is imposed. For each parametrized connected boundary surface choose its standard spine caps, with meridian Lagrangian $\alpha$; the object may carry any real Lagrangian $\lambda$. Use the Walker Maslov convention and actual cap-reference correction $a(R;\lambda,\alpha)$ of [[lem-wall-signature-and-rt-cap-reference-correction]].

A connected surgery presentation with $m$ surgery components, linking matrix $B$ and integer bordism weight $n$ has the exact outgoing color-block operator

$$Z(M,n;\lambda)^j_i=\kappa^{n+a(R_M;\lambda,\alpha)-\sigma(B)}D^{-m-1+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)F_0(\Omega;i,j).$$

Here $F_0$ is the finite colored graph operator with the disconnected-boundary unit-channel projections of [[lem-rt-capped-operator-normalization-and-composition]], and $d(j)$ is the product of outgoing handle-color dimensions. For disconnected $M$ use the product over its connected components, equivalently replace $-m-1$ by $-m-b_0(M)$; the external weight contributes the single factor $\kappa^n$. The empty value is $\mathbb C$.

These maps are independent of all marked surgery presentations and auxiliary coupon bases and define a symmetric monoidal functor on the full specified weighted category, including actual colored coupons, disconnected bordisms and empty ends. The functor preserves duality. A unit increase of weight acts by $\kappa$. No ordinary anomaly-free functor is asserted without cancellation of this anomaly.

For every compatible circle cut there is a natural factorization isomorphism

$$V(\Sigma_{\rm glued};\vec W)\cong\bigoplus_{i\in I}V(\Sigma_{\rm cut};\vec W,i,i^*).$$

The sewing map from right to left is the actual normalized tube map; its inverse is the complete composition-dual cutting resolution. Both separating and nonseparating cuts, all multiplicities, commuting disjoint cuts and iterated gluing are included. Markings, tensor order and the Lagrangian identifications of the cut are retained; a change of parametrization is represented by its weighted mapping cylinder.

derivations.claim: The labels are $0,1$. The dimension formula gives $d_0=d_1=1$. The twist formula gives $\theta_0=1$ and $\theta_1=q^{3/2}=e^{\pi i/2}=i$. Thus $D^2=1+1=2$ and choose $D=\sqrt2$. The Gauss sums are $p_+=1+i,\qquad p_-=1-i,\qquad \kappa=\frac{1+i}{\sqrt2}=e^{\pi i/4}.$ In particular $\kappa\ne1$.

A positive blow-up multiplies the surgery link value by $p_+$ and changes $(m,\sigma)$ to $(m+1,\sigma+1)$, so its normalized ratio is $D^{-1}\kappa^{-1}p_+=D^{-1}\frac{D}{p_+}p_+=1.$ A negative blow-up has ratio $D^{-1}\kappa p_-=D^{-1}\frac{p_+p_-}{D}=1$ by [F2]. citations.quote:
Let $(V,\omega)$ be a finite-dimensional real symplectic vector space and let $L_1,L_2,L_3$ be Lagrangian subspaces. Put

$$U_{123}=\frac{L_1\cap(L_2+L_3)}{(L_1\cap L_2)+(L_1\cap L_3)}.$$

For $a\in L_1\cap(L_2+L_3)$ write $a+b+c=0$ with $b\in L_2,c\in L_3$. The form

$$\psi_{123}([a],[a'])=\omega(a,b')$$

is well-defined, symmetric, and nondegenerate. Define $\mu(L_1,L_2,L_3)=\operatorname{sign}(\psi_{123})$. For any four Lagrangians,

$$\mu(L_1,L_2,L_3)+\mu(L_1,L_3,L_4)=\mu(L_1,L_2,L_4)+\mu(L_2,L_3,L_4).$$

Let $(V,\omega_V)$ and $(W,\omega_W)$ be finite-dimensional real symplectic vector spaces of dimensions $2n$ and $2m$. Give $\overline V\oplus W$ the form $-\omega_V\oplus\omega_W$. If $\Lambda\subseteq\overline V\oplus W$ is Lagrangian and $L\subseteq V$ is Lagrangian, then

$$R_\Lambda(L)=\{y\in W:\text{there is }x\in L\text{ with }(x,y)\in\Lambda\}$$

is Lagrangian in $W$.

Let $W$ be a subspace of a symplectic vector space $(V,\omega)$, with
[[def-symplectic-orthogonal-complement|symplectic orthogonal]] $W^\omega$.
Then $W$ is

- **isotropic** when $W\subseteq W^\omega$, equivalently $\omega|_{W\times W}=0$;
- **coisotropic** when $W^\omega\subseteq W$;
- **symplectic** when $\omega|_{W\times W}$ is nondegenerate, equivalently
  $W\cap W^\omega=0$; and
- **Lagrangian** when $W=W^\omega$.

The zero subspace is isotropic (and Lagrangian only when $V=0$), while $V$ is
coisotropic and symplectic.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map of vector spaces over $F$, with $V$
finite-dimensional. Then

$$\dim_F V=\operatorname{nullity}T+\operatorname{rank}T.$$

Equivalently,

$$\dim_F V=\dim_F(\ker T)+\dim_F(\operatorname{im}T).$$

derivations.claim: The Wall form in [F1] is unchanged by a symplectic isomorphism: the isomorphism carries its numerator and denominator to the corresponding subspaces and preserves $\omega(a,b')$. The cyclic map $[a]\mapsto[b]$, with $a+b+c=0$, is a well-defined isomorphism between the cyclic Wall quotients: changing a decomposition adds an adjacent intersection, and its inverse is obtained by solving the same sum-zero equation. It preserves the form because $\omega(b,c')=-\omega(b,a')=\omega(a',b)=\omega(a,b')$. Hence $\mu$ is cyclically invariant. If the first two Lagrangians agree, its numerator and denominator are both that Lagrangian, so the quotient is zero. Cyclic invariance therefore shows that $\mu$ vanishes whenever any two arguments agree. Orthogonal direct sums give orthogonal direct sums of Wall quotients and forms, so their signatures add.

Set $K=\{v:(v,0)\in B\}$ and $K'=\{w:(0,w)\in B\}$. Both are isotropic. A vector $x$ annihilates $\pi_VB$ exactly when $(x,0)$ annihilates $B$, hence belongs to $B=B^\perp$. Thus $(\pi_VB)^\perp=K$ and $\pi_VB=K^\perp$; likewise $\pi_WB=K'^\perp$. A pair $(v,w)\in B$ defines an isomorphism $\phi:K^\perp/K\to K'^\perp/K'$. Changing $w$ adds precisely $K'$, and changing $v$ adds $K$; the two projections are onto and these are their kernels. Isotropy of $B$ gives $\omega_W(w,w')=\omega_V(v,v')$, so $\phi$ is symplectic.

Choose a Lagrangian $N_0$ containing $K$. This finite construction needs no transversality: extend a basis $e_i$ of $K$ to hyperbolic pairs by choosing vectors $f_j$ with $\omega(e_i,f_j)=\delta_{ij}$, possible by nondegeneracy. Replace $f_i$ by $f_i-\frac12\sum_j\omega(f_i,f_j)e_j$ to make their pairings zero. Their span is symplectic. In its symplectic orthogonal complement, repeatedly choose a nonzero vector and a vector pairing to $1$, splitting off a symplectic plane each time. Adjoining one vector from each such plane to the $e_i$ spans the required Lagrangian. The construction ends by finite dimension.

For a Lagrangian $L\subseteq V$, put $L_K=((L\cap K^\perp)+K)/K$. It is Lagrangian in $K^\perp/K$: the inverse image $P_L=(L\cap K^\perp)+K$ is isotropic, and $P_L^\perp=(L+K)\cap K^\perp=(L\cap K^\perp)+K=P_L$. The last equality follows by writing $x=l+k$ and observing that $x,k\in K^\perp$ force $l\in K^\perp$. Here $(U\cap T)^\perp=U^\perp+T^\perp$ follows from inclusion and equal dimensions by [F3]. The relation normal form in step 1.2 gives $B(L)/K'=\phi(L_K)$ and $B^t(Q)/K=\phi^{-1}(Q_{K'})$. These are equalities of the actual subspaces containing $K'$ or $K$, not an assumption that relation images are injective.

Suppose $N_0,N\subseteq V$ both contain $K$. We prove $\mu_V(L,N_0,N)=\mu_{K^\perp/K}(L_K,N_0/K,N/K)$ by identifying their complete Wall forms. The left numerator $L\cap(N_0+N)$ lies in $K^\perp$. It projects onto the right numerator: if a representative $l+k$, with $l\in L\cap K^\perp$, lies in the sum of the two reduced spaces, then $l\in N_0+N$, since that sum contains $K$. The image of $(L\cap N_0)+(L\cap N)$ is precisely the right denominator: $l+k\in N_0$ is equivalent to $l\in N_0$, and likewise for $N$. The projection kernel $L\cap K$ is already in this denominator. Hence the Wall quotient spaces are isomorphic. A decomposition $a+b+c=0$ projects to the corresponding decomposition, and $\omega(a,b')$ descends to the quotient form because both entries lie in $K^\perp$. The isomorphism is an isometry, proving equality of signatures. By step 1.1 the same reduction holds when any two arguments contain $K$.

For arbitrary $L,P$ and $N$ containing $K$, the four-Lagrangian identity gives $\mu(L,P,N)-\mu(L,P,N_0)=\mu(L,N_0,N)-\mu(P,N_0,N)$. Reduce the two right-hand terms by step 3.1 and apply that same identity in $K^\perp/K$. Thus $\mu_V(L,P,N)=\mu_{K^\perp/K}(L_K,P_K,N/K)+\eta_K(L,P)$, where $\eta_K(L,P)=\mu_V(L,P,N_0)-\mu_{K^\perp/K}(L_K,P_K,N_0/K)$. In particular the defect is independent of $N$. The auxiliary $N_0$ disappears from the differences used below.

In step 4.1 take $N=B^t(Q)$. By step 2.1 and symplectic invariance, its reduced triple transports by $\phi$ to $(B(L)/K',B(P)/K',Q_{K'})$. Since $B(L)$ and $B(P)$ both contain $K'$, step 3.1 applied in $W$ identifies this reduced signature with $\mu_W(B(L),B(P),Q)$. Therefore $\mu_V(L,P,B^t(Q))-\mu_W(B(L),B(P),Q)=\eta_K(L,P)$, independent of $Q$. Subtract the equations for $Q$ and $R$ and use the four-Lagrangian identity on $(B(L),B(P),Q,R)$ in $W$. This yields exactly the first identity in the Statement.

Relational composition obeys $(BA)(\lambda_0)=B(A(\lambda_0))$ and $(CB)^t(\lambda_3)=B^t(C^t(\lambda_3))$ by the defining existential equations. Substitute $L=A(\lambda_0)$, $P=\lambda_1$, $Q=\lambda_2$, $R=C^t(\lambda_3)$ into step 5.1. All these spaces are Lagrangian by [F2], including inverse images by applying it to transposed relations. The resulting equality is precisely $m(B,A)+m(C,BA)=m(C,B)+m(CB,A)$. Thus adding these integer corrections gives associative weights.

For an identity relation on either side, its image or inverse image is the specified middle Lagrangian, so two arguments of $\mu$ agree and the correction is zero by step 1.1. Direct sums add corrections by that same step, including the zero-dimensional empty space. For graphs of symplectic isomorphisms the correction is $\mu(f_1\lambda_0,\lambda_1,f_2^{-1}\lambda_2)$. Transporting all three arguments by $f_2$ gives $\mu(f_2f_1\lambda_0,f_2\lambda_1,\lambda_2)$ with precisely the stated sign and order. These prove the remaining conclusions.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every subset of a manifold null set is
null, and every countable union of manifold null sets is null.

Let $M$ be a positive-dimensional smooth manifold, let $\mathcal A$ be a smooth
atlas on $M$, and let $E\subseteq M$ be $\mathcal A$-null in the sense of
[[def-null-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold]]. Then $M\setminus E$ is dense in $M$.
In particular, under Countable Choice the conclusion holds for any manifold-null
set $E$.

Let $k,m,n\ge1$ and $p\in\mathbb N$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+n+p}$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^k$. Suppose $F(a,b,\lambda_0)=0$ and $D_yF(a,b,\lambda_0)$ is invertible. Then there are neighbourhoods and a unique $C^k$ map $\varphi$ solving $F(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda)=0$. More precisely, on suitable open neighbourhoods $P$ of $(a,\lambda_0)$ and $Q$ of $b$,

$$F(x,y,\lambda)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y=\varphi(x,\lambda),$$

and

$$D\varphi(x,\lambda)=-D_yF(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda)^{-1}D_{(x,\lambda)}F(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda).$$

When no parameter block is present, this is the ordinary $C^k$ implicit function theorem.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be
$C^1$, and let $a\in U$.  If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open sets
$V,W\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that
$f|_V:V\to W$ is bijective.  Its inverse $g:W\to V$ is $C^1$, and

$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$

Thus $f$ is a local diffeomorphism at $a$.

Let $m\ge 0$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^m$ be open around
$(0,0)$, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth with

$$F(0,0)=0,\qquad \frac{\partial F}{\partial u}(0,0)=0,\qquad \frac{\partial^2F}{\partial u^2}(0,0)\ne0.$$

Then, after shrinking $U$, there are a sign $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}$, a smooth
function $H$ of the parameter variable, and a smooth local coordinate
change $(u,y)\mapsto (u',y)$ fixing $(0,0)$ such that

$$F(u,y)=H(y)+\varepsilon (u')^2.$$

Let $F$ be smooth near $(0,0)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^m$, assume
$dF_{(0,0)}=0$, and suppose there is a smooth local coordinate system $(s,y)$
centered at $(0,0)$, obtained from $(u,y)$ by a change of variables of the
form $(u,y)\mapsto(s,y)$, together with a smooth function $H$ near
$0\in\mathbb R^m$ such that, in these coordinates,

$$\widetilde F(s,y):=F(u(s,y),y)=F(0,0)+\varepsilon s^2+H(y), \qquad \varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}.$$

Then $0$ is a critical point of $H$, the Hessian of $H$ at $0$ is the
restriction of the Hessian of $F$ at $(0,0)$ to the $y$-coordinate subspace in
the $(s,y)$ chart, and if $\operatorname{Hess}_{(0,0)}(F)$ is nondegenerate
then so is $\operatorname{Hess}_0(H)$.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $K\subseteq M$ be compact, and let $W\subseteq M$ be open with $K\subseteq W$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:M\to [0,1]$ that equals $1$ on an open neighbourhood of $K$ and satisfies $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq W$.
Under countable choice, every smooth manifold, also with boundary, admits a Riemannian metric.

Boundary charts are allowed here; extend their smooth coordinates to open sets across the boundary. The finite vector $E(x)=(\chi_\alpha(x),\chi_\alpha(x)x_\alpha^1(x),\ldots,\chi_\alpha(x)x_\alpha^n(x))_\alpha\in\mathbb R^N$ is a smooth embedding. Indeed, if $E(x)=E(x')$, choose $\alpha$ with $\chi_\alpha(x)>0$. Equality of its first component implies $\chi_\alpha(x')>0$; equality of its remaining components then gives $x_\alpha(x)=x_\alpha(x')$, hence $x=x'$. Its differential is injective because on $\{\chi_\alpha>0\}$ one recovers $dx_\alpha^i=(d(\chi_\alpha x_\alpha^i)-x_\alpha^i d\chi_\alpha)/\chi_\alpha$. Compactness makes the continuous injection a homeomorphism onto its image. This constructs the needed embedding without invoking a separate embedding theorem. Let $\mathcal P$ be the finite-dimensional vector space of real polynomials on $\mathbb R^N$ of total degree at most $15$. For any $1\le k\le4$ and any distinct interior points $p_1,\ldots,p_k$, the map $\mathcal P\longrightarrow igoplus_{i=1}^k J^3_{p_i}(W,\mathbb R),\qquad P\longmapsto (j^3_{p_i}(P\circ E))_i$ is onto. Here a spatial 3-jet is the finite list of the value and all spatial derivatives of orders one through three; its coordinate changes are the usual smooth invertible chain-rule changes. To prove surjectivity, choose for every $i
e j$ an affine linear function $\ell_{ij}$ with $\ell_{ij}(E(p_j))=0$ and $\ell_{ij}(E(p_i))
e0$. Put $Q_i=\prod_{j

e i$. At $p_i$, some $n$ components of $E$ have independent differentials; they are local coordinates by the inverse function theorem. Polynomials of degree at most three in those components realize arbitrary spatial 3-jets at $p_i$. Since multiplication by a jet with nonzero constant term is invertible in the finite Taylor algebra, choose such a polynomial $R_i$ whose 3-jet, multiplied by that of $Q_i\circ E$, is the desired jet at $p_i$. Then $P=\sum_i Q_iR_i$ realizes all prescribed jets. Its degree is at most $4(k-1)+3\le15$. The separating linear forms and the coefficients depend on the chosen points, but they are used only to prove surjectivity of this **one fixed finite polynomial space**; no varying family of perturbation spaces is needed. Begin with the affine path between $f_0,f_1$, reparametrized to be stationary on parameter intervals $[0,2\delta]$ and $[1-2\delta,1]$. Call it $H_s$. Choose a spatial bump $\gamma$, zero near the boundary, positive on an open set containing the possible critical points, and equal to one on the complement of a slightly larger product collar. Choose $ eta(s)$ zero for $s\le\delta$ and $s\ge1-\delta$, and positive for $\delta<s<1-\delta$. Fix a basis $P_1,\ldots,P_m$ of $\mathcal P$ and consider $H_{s,z}(x)=H_s(x)+ eta(s)\gamma(x)\sum_{
u=1}^m z_
u P_
u(E(x)).$ For every $s$ with $ eta(s)>0$ and every configuration of at most four distinct points where $\gamma>0$, parameter differentiation in $z$ maps onto all their spatial 3-jets simultaneously: multiplication by the nonzero smooth scalar $ eta(s)\gamma$ is invertible on each finite Taylor algebra, so the preceding interpolation applies. Restrict $z$ to a sufficiently small open ball. On the fixed product collar $H_{s,z}$ is unchanged; on its transition region the original spatial differential has a uniform positive lower bound, so no critical points appear there. On the compact perturbation support the original $H_s$ has a positive margin from $0,1$, so the range and the endpoint fibers are retained. By openness of Morse nondegeneracy and of the finitely many distinct endpoint critical values, the stationary parameter ends remain excellent even on the portions where $ eta$ begins to be positive. Thus every relevant exceptional event occurs where $ eta\gamma>0$ and the jet evaluation is submersive.

**The jet strata, their smoothness, and their codimensions.** Write a jet as $(v,d,A,T)$: value, gradient covector, symmetric Hessian matrix, and symmetric third derivative. At $d=0$, $A$ is intrinsic. At $d=0$ and $A$ of corank one, $T$ restricted to the kernel line is also intrinsic: the extra third-derivative chain-rule terms contain either $d$ or $A$ paired with a kernel vector, and vanish. Consequently the following conditions define well-defined smooth strata in the appropriate spatial jet bundles. The locus of symmetric matrices of corank exactly $r$ is smooth of codimension $r(r+1)/2$. For a direct proof choose an invertible $(n-r)\times(n-r)$ principal block $A_0$ and write the matrix in blocks $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}A_0&B\\B^t&C\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. Its rank is $n-r$ precisely when the symmetric Schur complement $C-B^tA_0^{-1}B$ is zero. Its $r(r+1)/2$ entries are independent equations because differentiating with respect to $C$ gives the identity. Such charts cover the rank stratum (after a fixed linear change of basis where necessary). Hence the stratum $B_r$ defined by $d=0$ and Hessian corank $r$ has codimension $n+r(r+1)/2$. The corank-one sub-stratum $B_{1,0}$ adding $T|_{\ker A}^{\otimes3}=0$ has codimension $n+2$: choose a smooth local nonzero kernel vector and vary its cubic coefficient independently. The sign of that vector does not affect the zero condition. For simultaneous jets at distinct spatial points at one parameter, the conditions below have the stated codimensions. Gradient conditions at the different points are independent, and value equalities are independent of all gradient/Hessian/third-derivative coordinates. The codimension/source-dimension cases are: One $B_1$; $n+1$; $n+1$. One $B_r$, $r\ge2$; $n+r(r+1)/2\ge n+3$; $n+1$. One $B_{1,0}$; $n+2$; $n+1$. Two Morse critical points of equal value; $2n+1$; $2n+1$. One $B_1$ and another critical point, equal values; $2n+2$; $2n+1$. Two $B_1$ points at one parameter; $2n+2$; $2n+1$. Three critical points with one common value; $3n+2$; $3n+1$. One $B_1$ and an equal-value pair at two other points; $3n+2$; $3n+1$. Two equal-value pairs at four distinct points; $4n+2$; $4n+1$. In the last three rows no Hessian restrictions on the ordinary critical points are needed. One may partition into fixed corank strata if a condition is already expressed on a corank locus; there are finitely many possibilities. The first equal-value row is restricted to invertible Hessians, an open condition, so it is an embedded submanifold as written. The $B_1$ rows use the smooth corank-one stratum, not the singular closed determinantal variety.

**Application of the actual finite-dimensional transversality theorem.** For each row and each relevant $k$, the source is the smooth manifold $\{s:\beta(s)>0\}\times\operatorname{Conf}_k(\{x:\gamma(x)>0\}),$ of dimension $kn+1$. The target is the product spatial 3-jet bundle over that source. The evaluation map also depending on $z$ is a submersion in every vertical jet direction by step 1.1, and covers the identity on the spatial base; hence it is transverse to each displayed stratum. Apply [F1] to each of these finitely many maps/strata. The union of their exceptional parameter subsets is null, so its complement meets every parameter ball. Pick one $z$ in that complement and set $F_s=H_{s,z}$. If a target stratum has codimension greater than its configuration source dimension, its transverse inverse image is empty: at a point of the inverse image the differential would have to surject onto a normal space of strictly larger dimension. Thus all the high-codimension rows are avoided. The $B_1$ inverse image and the Morse equal-value-pair inverse image are zero-dimensional smooth submanifolds. This is an application of a supplied finite-dimensional theorem to explicit submersive families, not an application of an unproved infinite-dimensional or multijet version. At a $B_1$ point choose coordinates with Hessian kernel spanned by $u$ and invertible Hessian block in $y$. Let $b=\partial_s d_xF$ and $c=\partial_u^3F$. To see exactly what transversality says, project the linearization of the gradient onto its kernel covector: its spatial columns vanish there and its parameter column is $b(u)$. In the remaining $n-1$ gradient directions the Hessian is invertible. The differential of the corank equation in the remaining kernel spatial direction is $c$ (terms from differentiating the kernel vector vanish because $Au=0$). Therefore the determinant of the normal derivative to $B_1$ is, up to a nonzero factor, $b(u)c$. Its invertibility implies $b(u)\ne0$ and $c\ne0$. The separate avoidance of $B_{1,0}$ is compatible with, and corroborates, this calculation. At an equal-value pair with invertible Hessians, eliminate the spatial normal directions using the two Hessian blocks. The remaining derivative is the derivative of the difference of the two critical values along the parameter. Thus transversality is exactly nonzero crossing speed. The three- and four-point exclusions ensure that there is only one pair at a crossing parameter. The two-$B_1$ and $B_1$-plus-pair exclusions ensure that no birth coincides with another birth or crossing. The $B_1$-plus-equal-value exclusion ensures that a birth value is distinct from every other critical value.

**Finiteness, including exclusion of diagonal accumulation.** The critical curve is closed in the compact parameter/manifold product and is disjoint from a fixed boundary collar. Thus it is compact, with the ordinary endpoint critical points as its only boundary. The degenerate subset is closed in it, since it is the zero set of the Hessian determinant. It is discrete by transverse $B_1$ intersection and has no higher-corank limit by step 3.1; compactness therefore makes it finite. The equal-value-pair set is discrete but initially lies in a noncompact configuration space, so discreteness alone does **not** establish finiteness. Suppose infinitely many crossings existed. By compactness of $[0,1]\times W^2$, take an accumulation point $(s,p,q)$. If $p\ne q$, continuity makes both limiting points critical with equal values. Neither can be degenerate by the $B_1$-plus-equal-value exclusion, and then the equal-value transverse inverse image is locally discrete, a contradiction. If $p=q$ and this point is Morse, the parameter implicit function theorem gives a unique nearby critical branch, so two distinct critical points cannot converge to it. If $p=q$ and it is a fold, step 4.1 gives exactly the two nearby critical branches and proves that their values are unequal. This also contradicts crossing accumulation. Hence there are only finitely many crossings. The stationary endpoint neighborhoods exclude endpoint accumulation. Together with the simultaneous-event exclusions in step 3.1, this proves the stated genericity and finiteness conclusions.

**An explicit homotopy making the elementary cubic path.** Use the split-and-shifted coordinates of step 4.1. Write $c_0=C(0,0)>0$ and $D(s,u)=u^3(C(s,u)-c_0)$. Let $\alpha$ be a smooth scalar bump equal to one on $[-1/2,1/2]$ and zero outside $(-1,1)$, and choose a radial spatial bump $\rho(y/r)$ equal to one near zero and zero for $|y|\ge r$. Put $g_{\theta,s}(u,y)=a(s)+b(s)u+u^3C(s,u)+Q(y)-\theta\alpha(s/r^2)\alpha(u/r)\rho(y/r)D(s,u),\quad 0\le\theta\le1.$ Extend this family by the original path outside the coordinate box. The bump factors make this a smooth compactly supported change; it is supported in $|s|<r^2$, $|u|<r$, $|y|<r$, and hence leaves the endpoint functions untouched. At $\theta=1$ it has constant cubic coefficient $c_0$ in a smaller box. Here are the derivative estimates ensuring that this is a homotopy through the same generic event, rather than a possibly singular interpolation. Smoothness gives $|C(s,u)-c_0|\le K(|s|+|u|)$ on a fixed box, while the derivatives of $C$ of each fixed finite order are bounded there. On the shrinking box this gives $D=O(r^4)$, $D_u=O(r^3)$, $D_{uu}=O(r^2)$, $D_{uuu}=O(r)$, and $D_s=O(r^3)$. Differentiating the $s/r^2$ cutoff once and the $u/r$ cutoff once therefore gives a mixed $(s,u)$ derivative bounded by $O(r)$; three spatial derivatives likewise give $O(r)$. A first $y$ derivative of the correction is $O(r^3)$ and a second is $O(r^2)$, uniformly in $\theta$. All critical points in the support have $y=0$. Indeed, on the region where the $y$ cutoff varies, $|y|$ is bounded below by a positive constant times $r$, so $|d_yQ|$ is bounded below by a positive constant times $r$, whereas the correction's $y$ derivative is $O(r^3)$. These cannot cancel for small $r$. Where the cutoff equals one or zero its $y$ derivative vanishes and $d_yQ=0$ exactly when $y=0$. The transverse Hessian at $y=0$ remains the nondegenerate Hessian of $Q$. On $y=0$, the reduced function still has $g_{\theta,uu}(s,0)=0$ and $g_{\theta,u}(s,0)=b(s)$, because the correction has a factor $u^3$ and the $u$ cutoff is constant near zero. Its third $u$ derivative is positive by the uniform $O(r)$ estimate and the lower bound in step 4.1. Thus $g_{\theta,uu}(s,u)$ has its only zero at $u=0$, and a degenerate critical point requires $b(s)=0$, hence $s=0$. The fold stays at the origin, with the same nonzero cubic and mixed derivatives; each nearby slice has exactly the root pattern of step 4.1. No new birth can occur anywhere in the support. Outside the support nothing changed. Choose the initial neighborhood to isolate this event from the finitely many other event parameters and from the other critical values at its parameter. The correction has size $O(r^4)$, so it retains a strict gap from all those other critical values after shrinking. The two local critical values remain distinct by the strict-minimum argument in step 4.1 for every $\theta$. Thus no crossing is created or destroyed. This proves the stated supported cubic normalization, with all boundary collars fixed.

Assume full AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $n$-manifold, $n\ge1$, with fixed product collars, and let $f_0,f_1:W\to[0,1]$ be excellent adapted Morse functions equal to the same noncritical product height on those collars. There is a smooth path $F_s$ joining them, stationary near its parameter endpoints and fixed on smaller boundary collars, with finitely many exceptional parameters. Each exceptional parameter contains exactly one of: a corank-one interior birth/death with nonzero kernel cubic and nonzero parameter unfolding, or a transverse crossing of two nondegenerate critical values. All other critical points are nondegenerate, all other critical values are distinct, no two events share a parameter, and a birth value differs from every other critical value. The critical locus is a compact smooth curve whose parameter projection has only nondegenerate folds. Each fold creates or destroys two critical points of adjacent indices with distinct critical values. By a homotopy supported near each fold, preserving this event list and the endpoints, the path can further be put near that fold in smooth parameter-dependent spatial coordinates into the form

$$F_s=a(s)+b(s)u+c_0u^3+Q(y),\qquad b(0)=0,\quad b'(0)\ne0,\quad c_0>0,$$

where $Q$ is a fixed nondegenerate quadratic form in $n-1$ variables. Empty ends, disconnected $W$, and index $0/n$ pairs are allowed. This is a function-path statement with fixed product height; it has no boundary critical events and asserts no global descending-field or surgery-move theorem.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. For each $p\in M$, let
$\gamma_p:I_p\to M$ be the maximal integral curve through $p$, and set

$$ \mathcal D:=\{(t,p)\in\mathbb R\times M:t\in I_p\}, \qquad \Phi(t,p):=\gamma_p(t). $$

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.

Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a compact interval, and let $X_t$ be a smooth
time-dependent vector field on $M$ such that

$$ \bigcup_{t\in J}\operatorname{supp}(X_t) $$

is contained in a compact subset $K\subseteq M$. Then there is a global evolution
