citations.quote: Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F:M\to N$ be continuous, let $A\subseteq M$ be closed, and suppose $F$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood of $A$. Then there exist a smooth map $\widetilde F:M\to N$ and an open neighbourhood $W$ of $A$ such that $\widetilde F=F$ on $W$ and $F$ is homotopic to $\widetilde F$ by a homotopy fixed on $W$, hence relative to $A$. No compactness of $A$ or its neighbourhood is assumed.
Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F:M\to N$ be a continuous map between smooth manifolds. Then there exists a smooth map $\widetilde F:M\to N$ homotopic to $F$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold without
boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold, and let
$F\colon M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy such that $F_t:=F(\cdot,t)$ is an
embedding for every $t\in I$. Suppose $F$ is constant near the ends of $I$:
there is $\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac12)$ with $F(x,t)=F(x,0)$ for $t\le\varepsilon$
and $F(x,t)=F(x,1)$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon$ and all $x\in M$. Then for every
open neighbourhood $W$ of the image $F(M\times I)$ there is an ambient isotopy
$H\colon N\times I\to N$ such that

$$H_t\circ F_0=F_t\quad\text{for every }t\in I,$$

$H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, each $H_t$ is a diffeomorphism of $N$, and $H_t$ is the
identity outside $W$ for every $t$. Moreover $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\in[0,\tfrac{\varepsilon}{2}]$ and
$H_t=H_1$ for $t\in[1-\tfrac{\varepsilon}{2},1]$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V$ be a compact
smooth $n$-manifold with boundary and let $N$ be a smooth $n$-manifold without
boundary ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $F:V\times I\to N$ be a smooth map such
that $F_t:=F(\cdot,t)$ is a smooth embedding for every $t\in I$
([[def-smooth-embedding]]), and suppose $F$ is constant near the ends: for some
$\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac12)$ one has $F(x,t)=F(x,0)$ for $t\le\varepsilon$ and
$F(x,t)=F(x,1)$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon$, for all $x\in V$.

Then for every open neighbourhood $W\subseteq N$ of the compact image
$F(V\times I)$ there is a smooth map $H:N\times I\to N$ such that
$H_0=\operatorname{id}_N$, every $H_t$ is a diffeomorphism of $N$
([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]),
$$H_t\circ F_0=F_t\quad\text{for every }t\in I,$$
$H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, $H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$
for $t\le\varepsilon/2$, and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.

Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a compact interval, and let $X_t$ be a smooth
time-dependent vector field on $M$ such that

$$ \bigcup_{t\in J}\operatorname{supp}(X_t) $$

is contained in a compact subset $K\subseteq M$. Then there is a global evolution
operator $\Psi_{t,s}:M\to M$ for all $s,t\in J$.

Let $X=U\cup V$, where $U$ and $V$ are open path-connected subsets of $X$, let $U\cap V$ be path-connected, and fix $x_0\in U\cap V$. For the inclusion-induced maps in the diagram

$$\pi_1(U,x_0)\longleftarrow\pi_1(U\cap V,x_0)\longrightarrow\pi_1(V,x_0),$$

the group $\pi_1(X,x_0)$, together with the two inclusion-induced homomorphisms, is a pushout ([[def-pushout-of-group-homomorphisms]]). Equivalently, the canonical homomorphism from any pushout $P$ of the displayed diagram to $\pi_1(X,x_0)$ is an isomorphism. No injectivity of either map from the overlap group is assumed.

Assume Countable Choice. For N > r >= 2, the standard block inclusion SO(r) into SO(N) is surjective on fundamental groups. Hence a loop discrepancy of a total normal frame can be killed by a loop supported in a single rank-r orthogonal summand, leaving its subspace and designated corner values fixed.
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar.

derivations.claim: First take embedded endpoint circles in a $d$-manifold, $d\ge4$, and a continuous free homotopy with compact image in a prescribed relatively compact open set $O$. Reparametrize it to be constant near both endpoints, extend constantly to an open parameter interval, and apply [F1] there relative to closed endpoint neighborhoods. Restriction gives a smooth homotopy $H:[0,1]\times S^1\to O$ with the specified stationary ends. Write $j:O\to\mathbb R^a$ and $R:U\to j(O)$ for the embedding and retraction constructed in [F1]. Along the compact image, $dR$ has rank $d$ because $R$ fixes $j(O)$; retain a uniform neighborhood with that rank.

The zero-velocity stratum of the curve one-jet bundle has codimension $d$ on the two-dimensional source $(s,t)$. The diagonal of $O\times O$ has codimension $d$ on the three-dimensional same-parameter source $(s,t,t')$, $t\ne t'$. By [F2] one small parameter avoids both strata: their transverse inverse images have negative dimension, since $d\ge4$. The noncompact off-diagonal source is permitted by [F2]; it need not be replaced by a compact configuration space. Endpoint neighborhoods are stationary. Compact-circle embedding is open in the $C^1$ topology: finitely many coordinate intervals give a positive local derivative bound and injectivity on shorter intervals, and pairs outside those intervals have positive image separation. Smallness retains the endpoint embedding condition in transition collars. Every slice is thus injective and immersive; compactness makes it an embedding. Its compact track lies in $O$, so [F3] gives an ambient isotopy supported in a compact subset of $O$.

Without the homotopy parameter the same family proves the three-dimensional assertion. Smooth the continuous loop by [F1]. The nonimmersion source now has dimension one and the double-point source dimension two, both below the respective codimension three. To avoid a finite old link add the evaluation transversality condition to each component: its codimension is two and the loop source has dimension one. The value-submersive family in step 2.1 handles all finitely many conditions simultaneously. One small parameter therefore gives an embedded representative of the original free class disjoint from that link.

For a single two-handle use open thickenings of the old stage and the handle. Their overlap retracts onto $S^1\times D^2$ and is connected, whereas the handle thickening is contractible. By [F4] the new fundamental group is the old group modulo the normal closure of the attaching-circle class. Finite induction gives a surjection $\pi_1(N)\to\pi_1(W)$. Hence the given interior circle is freely homotopic to a loop in a pushed-in base copy. step 3.2 gives an embedded representative there avoiding the old attaching link. This uses the arbitrary group class, not nullhomotopy.

The auxiliary homotopy may be pushed off the protected external collar while keeping its endpoints. If that strip has inward coordinate $r\le a$, choose $\delta>0$ so both endpoint loops avoid $r\le a+2\delta$. On $[0,a+2\delta]$ use an increasing smooth map into $[a+\delta,a+2\delta]$ agreeing with identity near its upper end, and extend by identity beyond. Its composition with the homotopy changes only that auxiliary map, not $W$ or its prescribed collars. The image is compact and misses the protected strip. Choose a relatively compact open neighborhood of this image outside the strip and apply step 3.1. This gives the required supported ambient isotopy. Without the stated endpoint-avoidance hypothesis it only guarantees avoidance of a sufficiently small boundary strip, so that hypothesis is retained in the Statement.

Transport the prescribed rank-three normal frame by the ambient isotopy. At the base circle its normal bundle splits into the oriented rank-two normal bundle in $N$ and the level-normal line. An oriented bundle on a circle is trivial: transport a frame around a cut interval and correct endpoint holonomy by a path in the orientation-preserving linear group, using orthonormalization and plane rotations. Choose an initial level frame. Its rank-three extension differs from the prescribed frame by a loop in $GL^+(3,\mathbb R)$, which polar orthonormalization retracts to $SO(3)$. By [F5] its class comes from $SO(2)$. Modify the level frame by that loop; this is an integral twist, and its rank-three extension is now homotopic to the prescribed frame. This retains both possible rank-three framing classes rather than equating them.

A smooth homotopy of the frames gives an isotopy of sufficiently small tubular product embeddings. In a fixed normal chart apply the invertible frame maps to the disk coordinates; compactness of the parameter-circle product gives one radius on which all are embedded. The full-dimensional compact-source version of [F3], applied in the boundaryless interior after stationary endpoint reparametrization, extends this isotopy while fixing the external collar. Thus the conclusion retains the whole framed attaching embedding and not merely its unframed core. Together with step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1 this proves every clause.

Then for every open neighbourhood $W\subseteq N$ of the compact image

For fixed attaching and product-collar data, two compatible smooth monotone roundings of a handle attachment are diffeomorphic by an isotopy supported in that collar. The diffeomorphism is the identity outside the collar.

Assume AC. Let $N$ be a connected nonempty compact smooth oriented three-manifold, and let $W$ be a finite four-dimensional two-handle trace from $N$, with its full external boundary collar fixed. Every smooth framed circle in $\operatorname{int}W$ avoiding that protected collar is ambiently isotopic, with compact support outside it, to a circle in a pushed-in copy of $N$. The target circle may avoid the old finite attaching link. Its prescribed oriented rank-three normal framing is represented, up to homotopy and isotopy of its small tubular attaching embedding, by an integral rank-two framing in $N$ plus the level-normal line. No condition on $\pi_1(N)$ or on the circle's class is imposed. More generally, freely homotopic embedded circles in a smooth manifold of dimension $d\ge4$ are isotopic whenever their homotopy lies in a prescribed relatively compact open set; the isotopy may be supported in that set. Every loop class in a three-manifold has an embedded representative avoiding a prescribed finite link.

Assume full AC. Let $N\cong D^2\times S^1$ be an oriented solid torus in the interior of an oriented smooth 3-manifold, let $K$ be its core with any integral framing, and let $U$ be a small meridian of $K$ with the zero framing given by its meridian disk. Simultaneous framed surgery on $K$ and $U$ returns a solid torus diffeomorphic to $N$ by a diffeomorphism equal to the original identification on $\partial N$. Thus inserting or removing this pair preserves the ambient manifold relative to the complement of $N$, including external collars and boundary parametrizations. An embedded colored ribbon graph avoiding $N$ is fixed. No assertion is made that a graph traversing $N$ is fixed, or that this operation belongs to a complete relative move list.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $N$ be a connected smooth $n$-manifold with
nonempty boundary and let $D\subseteq\partial N$ be an embedded closed disk.
Then the boundary connected sum $N\natural D^n$, obtained by gluing an $n$-disk
along $D$, is diffeomorphic to $N$ by a diffeomorphism equal to the identity
outside a collar neighbourhood of $D$.

derivations.claim: Join the feet of the one-handle by an embedded arc in the connected lower stage, with interior away from the feet, and thicken it. Along with the handle core this gives a standard ball-plus-tube neighborhood $S^1\times D^{d-1}$, with a designated $(d-1)$-ball on its boundary in the lower stage. Concretely thicken the joining arc to a disk tube, use the foot disks as its ends, and join the second tube supplied by the handle. Match their endpoint normal coordinates to obtain exactly this product, and push the core circle into its interior.

For the four-dimensional bridge choose coordinates $S^1\times D^3$ about the level circle, with $D^2_{\mathrm{eq}}$ the level equator and lower/upper half-balls $D^3_-,D^3_+$. Remove this tube and insert $D^2_a\times S^2$, using its given full rank-three framing. Split $S^2=S^2_-\cup_{S^1_{\mathrm{eq}}}S^2_+$. The lower product with $S^1\times D^3_-$ removed is a product collar with an indented outgoing face: in the normal coordinates the half-ball removal moves the old upper face to an inward rounded graph. A smooth increasing interval map on each normal line, fixed at the lower end, carries that face to the graph; these maps are identity outside the tube and the seam rounding is in a smaller collar. The upper half has the same product description. Thus the surgery is a product, the two inserted pieces, and an absorbable outgoing product.

Interior surgery replaces a smaller $S^1\times D^{d-1}$ by $D^2\times S^{d-2}$. The remaining shell of the original product is $S^1\times S^{d-2}\times I$, so it is a retained boundary collar. Split the sphere into its two hemispheres. The first $D^2\times D^{d-2}_+$ is a ball. The second, read with core factor $D^{d-2}_-$, is a $(d-2)$-handle with attaching region $D^2\times S^{d-3}$ and outgoing region $S^1\times D^{d-2}_-$. Place the designated lower-stage boundary ball in $S^1\times\operatorname{int}D^{d-2}_+$, which is on the first ball's boundary. Absorb that ball into the lower collar by [F4]. The remaining handle has index $d-2$. The outer collar is unchanged point by point; every later attachment is carried by that boundary identification. This is an interior modification, not a cancellation of the original ambient manifold. For $d=4$ it trades index one for two, and for $d=5$ one for three; reversing dimension five gives index four to two.

The first piece $D^2_a\times S^2_-$ is a two-handle with core $D^2_a$, normal disk $S^2_-$ and attaching region $S^1_a\times S^2_-$. On the old level this is the knot $K$ with its prescribed level framing. Its outgoing region is $D^2_a\times S^1_{\mathrm{eq}}$. The second piece $D^2_a\times S^2_+$ is also a two-handle, but its disk factors are interchanged: core $S^2_+$, normal disk $D^2_a$, attaching region $D^2_a\times S^1_{\mathrm{eq}}$. This is exactly the outgoing region of the first handle; using the same core factor for both would give a different attaching region.

The second attaching circle is $\{p\}\times S^1_{\mathrm{eq}}$ for an interior point $p\in D^2_a$. Move $p$ along a radial arc toward $S^1_a$, first shrinking its normal thickening uniformly. This is a compact isotopy of the actual attaching product embedding in the boundary after the first handle. At the seam its product corner rotation carries it to the old level, where it is a small meridian of $K$. Its tangential $S^1_a$ direction is a constant push direction around this meridian and its other normal direction is the complementary radial direction in $D^2_{\mathrm{eq}}$. Thus its framing has no turn relative to the meridian disk, so is zero. Its other boundary piece $S^1_a\times S^2_+$ is where the indented upper product attaches. Absorbing that product retains the original upper boundary map. By [F1] these product isotopies compare the full handle attachments, not just their cores.

For an arbitrary prescribed rank-three frame on a circle in a two-handle trace, [F2] first moves the circle to the base and realizes its framing by an integral level frame. Its framing homotopy is realized by an isotopy of small tubular embeddings, so step 1.2, step 2.2, step 3.1 apply to the prescribed surgery relative to the whole ambient boundary. By [F3] the resulting pair has the O3 boundary-relative identification on its small solid torus; old attaching links outside that torus and external base collars are fixed. This proves the bridge for every framing, without identifying the two rank-three parity classes, as well as the existence trade in step 1.1, step 2.1.

Here **adapted complete** has the collar-extension meaning of [[def-morse-function-adapted-to-a-cobordism]]: $X$ is the restriction of a complete smooth field on a boundaryless collar extension of $W$; a trajectory is followed in $W$ only until it exits a face.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $K\subseteq M$ be compact, and let $W\subseteq M$ be open with $K\subseteq W$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:M\to [0,1]$ that equals $1$ on an open neighbourhood of $K$ and satisfies $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq W$.

Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a compact interval, and let $X_t$ be a smooth
time-dependent vector field on $M$ such that

$$ \bigcup_{t\in J}\operatorname{supp}(X_t) $$

is contained in a compact subset $K\subseteq M$. Then there is a global evolution
operator $\Psi_{t,s}:M\to M$ for all $s,t\in J$.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. For each $p\in M$, let
$\gamma_p:I_p\to M$ be the maximal integral curve through $p$, and set

$$ \mathcal D:=\{(t,p)\in\mathbb R\times M:t\in I_p\}, \qquad \Phi(t,p):=\gamma_p(t). $$

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(W;M_0,M_1)$ be a compact triad and let $f$ be
an adapted Morse function whose critical points of index $k$ all lie at one
level $c\in(0,1)$, with no critical point of another index at $c$ and no other
critical value in a neighbourhood of $c$. Then the
sublevel just above $c$ is obtained from the sublevel just below $c$ by
attaching disjoint $k$-handles, one for each index-$k$ critical point.
Equivalently, handles of equal index attached at one level may be regarded as
attached simultaneously or successively in any order, the result being the same
up to diffeomorphism fixing the incoming face and respecting the lower sublevel up to homotopy of pairs. On the common attached-stage model, reordering disjoint attachments fixes its entire lower stage. Handles of equal index may
be reordered freely, and attaching embeddings may be changed by isotopy of the
attaching region.

For fixed attaching and product-collar data, two compatible smooth monotone roundings of a handle attachment are diffeomorphic by an isotopy supported in that collar. The diffeomorphism is the identity outside the collar.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $f$ be adapted on a compact triad with adapted
field $X$, and let $P$ (value $c$) and $Q$ (value $c'>c$) be consecutive
critical levels such that $\operatorname{ind}(p)\ge\operatorname{ind}(q)$ for
all $p\in P$, $q\in Q$. Let $U$ be a prescribed neighbourhood of a regular level
$f^{-1}(v)$ with $c<v<c'$. Then there is a complete adapted downward
gradient-like field $X'$ for $f$, equal to $X$ outside $U$, such that for all
$q\in Q$ and $p\in P$ the crossing spheres $A_q$ and $B_p$ of the previous
lemma are pairwise disjoint.

Consequently no trajectory of $X'$ has one limit in $P$ and the other in $Q$,
and the corresponding compact trajectory sets are disjoint. The field change may be chosen arbitrarily small in $C^\infty$ on $W$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(f,X)$ be adapted on a compact triad, and choose regular $0<u<c<c'<v<1$ such that the critical set in $K=f^{-1}[u,v]$ consists exactly of finite clusters $P,Q$ at values $c,c'$. Suppose there is no $X$-trajectory from a point of $Q$ to a point of $P$. Then for any $a,a'\in(u,v)$, including $a>a'$ or $a=a'$, there is an adapted Morse $g$ with the same critical points and indices as $f$, $g=a$ on $P$, $g=a'$ on $Q$, and $X$ still downward gradient-like for $g$. The function is $f$ outside the interior of $K$ and near its two end levels, and is $f$ plus a constant near every critical point. On a triad with just these two critical clusters, one may also use its face levels as $u,v$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(W;M_0,M_1)$ be a nonempty compact connected triad with
$M_0\ne\varnothing$ connected. Then $W$ admits a handle decomposition relative
to $M_0$ with no $0$-handles. If $M_0$ has $k$ components the same argument
leaves no $0$-handles and begins with $k-1$ connecting $1$-handles; if
$M_0=\varnothing$, exactly the $0$-handles needed to create the components of
$W$ remain, one per component.

nonempty boundary and let $D\subseteq\partial N$ be an embedded closed disk.
Then the boundary connected sum $N\natural D^n$, obtained by gluing an $n$-disk
along $D$, is diffeomorphic to $N$ by a diffeomorphism equal to the identity

derivations.claim: In the fixed corner and face charts extend the boundary height by the inward horizontal collar coordinate near $A_0$, one minus that coordinate near $A_1$, and $t$ on the vertical collar. These agree in the specified product corner charts: the horizontal inward coordinate there is exactly $t$ or $1-t$. Patch only beyond smaller common collars using [F2], blending with $1/2$ in the compact interior. At a corner use restrictions of ordinary Euclidean bumps to its product quadrant; a finite cover and division by their positive sum give the required partition there. Thus the same finite patching proof applies directly to these corner charts, rather than presuming that a boundary-only partition statement already covers corners. The resulting smooth $h:V\to[0,1]$ has exactly the endpoint fibers $A_0,A_1$, is strictly between zero and one elsewhere, and has nonzero differential near every boundary face and corner. Thus the possible critical set lies in a compact subset of the ordinary interior.

On that compact set choose finitely many nested interior coordinate charts and bump-supported linear coordinate functions, as in the actual proof of [F1]. Their differential evaluations span the cotangent fiber wherever a critical point is possible. The finite-dimensional evaluation is therefore transverse to the zero section. By [F1] choose an arbitrarily small parameter whose differential is transverse to zero. Compactness and nondegeneracy give finitely many critical points. Independent constant bumps separate their values without changing their Hessians, and the positive value margin on the perturbation support retains the range and endpoint fibers. The result is an excellent Morse function equal to the original height on all protected collars.

Choose the metric $dt^2+dr^2+g_B$ on the vertical collar, where $r$ is its inward normal coordinate, and Euclidean metrics on smaller disjoint critical charts; patch elsewhere by [F2]. The negative gradient is tangent to the vertical face and equals $-\partial_t$ there. It has the standard linear Morse model at each critical point and the required horizontal entry and exit signs. Extend it over signed face collars in the product models and cut it off on an ambient carrier. Its spatial modifications have compact support, so [F2] gives complete evolution. An interior trajectory cannot first hit the vertical face in finite time: the unique solution through a hypothetical first-hit point would lie in that boundary face backwards as well, contradicting its interior starting point.

Transport framed local unstable disks across the regular bands by this boundary-tangent field. Their compact sphere sections lie away from the vertical collar. Outside small Morse blocks strict descent has a uniform positive lower bound on each compact band. In the blocks the exact exponential Morse flow accounts for infinite-time limits, which can occur only at critical points, never at the noncritical vertical model. Consequently every finite regular transport of a compact attaching thickening stays in a compact subset of the interior of a horizontal level. The local construction in [F3], with its product complement transported by the regular flow, therefore gives the finite relative handle decomposition. All handles attach away from the vertical collar, and the composed outgoing identification is retained. This proves the cornered interface directly; the ordinary closed-face theorem is not invoked outside its hypotheses.

For an inverted adjacent critical pair, the compact unstable and stable sphere sections in a regular $(d-1)$-level have dimensions summing to at most $d-2$. The moving-off construction in [F4] uses product tubes and arbitrarily small translations of these compact sections, avoiding the finite projected lower-dimensional sets simultaneously. Choose these tubes inside that level's interior. Its regular-band field shear thus separates the sections with support disjoint from the vertical collar. The resulting no-connection condition gives compact disjoint critical-trajectory closures, by the exact Morse-block argument of [F4]: any noncompact limiting travel would break at a critical point, which would give an excluded connecting trajectory. The interior field change extends by zero on the protected collar.

The value-change step needs an additional orbit cutoff because the vertical height is not constant. In addition to the orbit-constant separating function $\beta$ of [F4], choose an orbit-constant $\alpha$ equal to one near both compact critical-trajectory sets and zero near the vertical product trajectories. Construct it on the lower exit level by a bump one near the compact critical exits and zero near its boundary, and extend it along regular trajectories. Near each critical-trajectory set extend it constantly as one. This is smooth by the same exit-continuity argument in the full proof of [F4]: close regular trajectories have exits near the compact critical exits, so the bump is already constant in a neighborhood. A local minimum has an attracting neighborhood with no lower through-exit, where the constant-one extension applies; reverse the argument for a maximum. Thus $d\alpha(X)=d\beta(X)=0$, with $\alpha=0$ on a neighborhood of the fixed vertical collar.

If the ordinary interchange formula in [F4] is $G(f,\beta)$, use $g=(1-\alpha)f+\alpha G(f,\beta)$ instead. Away from critical points, $dg(X)=(1-\alpha+\alpha\partial_1G(f,\beta))df(X)<0$. Near the critical sets $\alpha=1$, so this is precisely the desired value interchange and a constant change in each critical chart. Near the vertical face $\alpha=0$, so it is exactly $f$. Band-end identities make it smooth when extended by the old function. Finite adjacent exchanges sort the critical values by index; their inversion number strictly decreases. The boundary height, the field's product model and all endpoint maps are retained throughout.

Assume now that the total bordism and both nonempty horizontal ends are connected. In index order the initial zero/one-handle graph has vertices the incoming component and new balls, and edges the one-handles. It is connected because handles of index at least two have connected attaching regions and cannot connect components. Root a spanning tree at the incoming vertex. Process its edges outward, absorbing each new ball with its incident one-handle by the local disk comparison of [F5]; carry every other attaching map through the resulting stage diffeomorphism. All attaching disks, arcs and comparison collars are compact in horizontal interiors, so the vertical collar is fixed. This removes all zero-handles.

Reverse the presentation relative to the connected nonempty outgoing end and perform the same rooted-tree procedure. It deletes only index $d$ and paired index $d-1$ handles in the original direction and transports the rest, so it does not reintroduce removed zero-handles. The face charts and height reverse by $t\mapsto1-t$ during the construction and return to the prescribed ones afterward. This gives the claimed presentation without zero or top handles, retaining the full horizontal and vertical parametrizations. step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1 already establish the existence and rearrangement assertions without the connectivity assumptions used only for this deletion phase.

citations.quote:
Assume AC. Every compact closed oriented smooth three-manifold $X$ admits a compact oriented smooth four-manifold $W$ and an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $j:\partial W\to X$. Disconnected and empty manifolds are included. Consequently $\Omega_3^{SO}=0$ integrally, with a single copy of each input manifold.

More precisely, if $X=M\cup C$ is an actual closed manifold obtained by attaching specified smooth caps $C$ to a compact oriented three-manifold $M$ along specified collared boundary parametrizations, the identification $j$ retains these marked submanifolds, their parametrizations and any decorations by pullback. No extension of a boundary diffeomorphism across a cap or filling is required. The assertion is existence; a simultaneous choice of fillings for a set of inputs may use AC and is not asserted canonical.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge4$, and let $V$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional bordism with corners, horizontal faces $A_0,A_1$, and vertical face $B\times[0,1]$, with compatible product collar charts fixed. Here $\partial A_i=B\times\{i\}$. There are excellent Morse data with all critical points interior, equal to the specified height $t$ on a fixed smaller vertical product collar, zero and one on the horizontal faces with their prescribed inward collar models. They give a finite handle decomposition whose attaching thickenings lie in the interiors of horizontal levels, away from the fixed vertical collar, retaining the actual outgoing identification. Critical values may be ordered by index while this entire boundary height is fixed. If $V,A_0,A_1$ are connected and $A_0,A_1$ are nonempty, there is such a relative presentation with no handles of index zero or $d$. No fundamental-group assumption or h-cobordism hypothesis is imposed.

Assume AC. In dimension $d\ge4$, a one-handle whose feet lie in the same connected lower stage can be replaced, by an interior framed circle surgery, with one $(d-2)$-handle. The resulting manifold may change, but its entire boundary, specified collar and every later attaching map are identified with the old ones. The framing for this existence trade is the displayed product framing. Separately, surgery on a prescribed rank-three-framed circle lying in a product three-dimensional level of an oriented four-manifold, with its framing homotopic to a level rank-two framing plus the level-normal line, is represented relative to the unaffected boundary by adjoining two four-dimensional two-handles on that framed knot $K$ and a small disk-framed zero meridian $U$. The statement retains the integral framing of $K$. In a two-handle trace every interior framed circle can be put in this form by the preceding circle lemma. The pair's boundary identification is the boundary-relative local O3 identification.

Assume AC. Let $N$ be a connected nonempty compact smooth oriented three-manifold, and let $W$ be a finite four-dimensional two-handle trace from $N$, with its full external boundary collar fixed. Every smooth framed circle in $\operatorname{int}W$ avoiding that protected collar is ambiently isotopic, with compact support outside it, to a circle in a pushed-in copy of $N$. The target circle may avoid the old finite attaching link. Its prescribed oriented rank-three normal framing is represented, up to homotopy and isotopy of its small tubular attaching embedding, by an integral rank-two framing in $N$ plus the level-normal line. No condition on $\pi_1(N)$ or on the circle's class is imposed. More generally, freely homotopic embedded circles in a smooth manifold of dimension $d\ge4$ are isotopic whenever their homotopy lies in a prescribed relatively compact open set; the isotopy may be supported in that set. Every loop class in a three-manifold has an embedded representative avoiding a prescribed finite link.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V$ be a compact
smooth $n$-manifold with boundary and let $N$ be a smooth $n$-manifold without
boundary ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $F:V\times I\to N$ be a smooth map such
that $F_t:=F(\cdot,t)$ is a smooth embedding for every $t\in I$
([[def-smooth-embedding]]), and suppose $F$ is constant near the ends: for some
$\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac12)$ one has $F(x,t)=F(x,0)$ for $t\le\varepsilon$ and
$F(x,t)=F(x,1)$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon$, for all $x\in V$.

Then for every open neighbourhood $W\subseteq N$ of the compact image
$F(V\times I)$ there is a smooth map $H:N\times I\to N$ such that
$H_0=\operatorname{id}_N$, every $H_t$ is a diffeomorphism of $N$
([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]),
$$H_t\circ F_0=F_t\quad\text{for every }t\in I,$$
$H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, $H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$
for $t\le\varepsilon/2$, and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar.

For fixed attaching and product-collar data, two compatible smooth monotone roundings of a handle attachment are diffeomorphic by an isotopy supported in that collar. The diffeomorphism is the identity outside the collar.

derivations.claim: Glue $-N$ to $M$ along the actual given boundary map and collars, obtaining a closed oriented three-manifold $X$ with a marked seam $\Sigma$. By [F1] choose $U$ with $\partial U\cong X$ and pull back this marking. Discard filling components without boundary. If necessary join the remaining finitely many components by interior connected sums: remove two interior four-balls and join their oriented sphere boundaries by $S^3\times I$, using product annulus charts. These operations preserve every old boundary collar and make $U$ connected. Its boundary is nonempty, even when the seam is empty, since $N,M$ are nonempty.

Near the marked seam the filling has coordinates $\Sigma\times(-2\epsilon,2\epsilon)_u\times[0,2\epsilon)_v$, with $v$ inward. Remove a small notch along $u=v=0$: in this half-plane replace a small boundary interval by an inward compact arc with quadrant corners at its endpoints, unchanged outside a small rectangle. Its product with $\Sigma$ is the vertical face $\Sigma\times I$. Identify the shortened horizontal collars with the original ones by smooth increasing interval maps, identity near their far ends, and keep the identity on every $\Sigma$ point. Product quadrant charts retain the prescribed parametrizations at both corners. The notch does not disconnect the interior: each remaining local point joins the unchanged interior region. Thus this is a connected boundary-marked four-bordism from $N$ to $M$ with precisely the given vertical product collar. For empty $\Sigma$ no notch is needed.

Apply [F2] in dimension four to remove zero and four handles. Starting at connected $N$, trade every one-handle by its interior circle construction for a two-handle. Its feet lie in the same connected lower stage and the trade preserves connectedness as well as the whole boundary. Order handles by index using the fixed-height construction. Reverse from connected $M$ and trade the reversed one-handles, which were original three-handles, to two-handles. Reversing back leaves only two-handles. The modified four-manifold need not equal the original filling; its entire marked boundary does. Denote its resulting successive two-handle trace by $W'$.

Record this successive trace by one link in the original $N$. Inductively suppose preceding handles are represented by a framed link $L\subset N$. The next attaching circle lies in the surgered outgoing three-manifold. Apply the explicit curve family in [F3] to perturb it off the finitely many belt-core circles of the filling solid tori: each core has codimension two whereas the curve source has dimension one. The perturbation is an attaching isotopy and carries its full normal thickening. Its compact intersection with each filling product $D^2\times S^1$ now has radial coordinate bounded below by some $\epsilon>0$.

In each such product choose a smooth increasing radial reparametrization, identity near zero and outside a slightly larger seam collar, which sends every radius at least $\epsilon$ beyond the old filling-torus boundary. This exists by choosing its strictly positive derivative with the required integral and fixed end intervals. It is a radial ambient isotopy, stationary at its parameter ends. Thus the circle is pushed into the old exterior $N\setminus\nu L$. Carry its full attaching thickening by the derivative, shrinking it uniformly first if needed. By [F3] the isotopy extends over a collar of the existing trace, fixed at the incoming face and external boundary. Hence the total trace agrees with the prescribed successive one, retaining the outgoing comparison. The new circle is now an additional framed component in the original $N$. Finite induction produces a single link.

The outgoing boundary of a four-dimensional two-handle removes $S^1\times\operatorname{int}D^2$ and inserts $D^2\times S^1$ in its product attaching coordinates, exactly the stated framed surgery. Therefore the final link yields $M$ with the original external parametrization. For disconnected manifolds run the construction independently on each prescribed pair of connected components, using that pair's fixed base, and take their finite disjoint union. For empty inputs take the empty union. The common partition is essential: surgery never changes the number of ambient components. No nullhomotopy of attaching circles, fundamental-group restriction, Kirby completeness or decorated move completeness has been used.

Assume full AC. Let $N\cong D^2\times S^1$ be an oriented solid torus in the interior of an oriented smooth 3-manifold, let $K$ be its core with any integral framing, and let $U$ be a small meridian of $K$ with the zero framing given by its meridian disk. Simultaneous framed surgery on $K$ and $U$ returns a solid torus diffeomorphic to $N$ by a diffeomorphism equal to the original identification on $\partial N$. Thus inserting or removing this pair preserves the ambient manifold relative to the complement of $N$, including external collars and boundary parametrizations. An embedded colored ribbon graph avoiding $N$ is fixed. No assertion is made that a graph traversing $N$ is fixed, or that this operation belongs to a complete relative move list.

Assume AC. Let $Y$ be a closed oriented smooth three-manifold and let $W_0,W_1$ be compact oriented smooth four-manifolds, with $W_0$ nonempty, with fixed collars and orientation-preserving parametrizations $\phi_i:\partial W_i\to Y$. Form the actual closed seam $M=(-W_0)\cup_YW_1$ using $\phi_1^{-1}\phi_0$, and put $s=\sigma(M)$. Let $W_0'$ be its interior connected sum with $s$ complex-oriented projective planes for $s\ge0$, or $-s$ oppositely oriented projective planes for $s<0$, using balls away from its boundary collar. Then there is a compact oriented smooth five-manifold with corners $V$ whose identified faces are
$$\partial V=(-W_0')\cup(Y\times[0,1])\cup W_1,$$
with exactly the original parametrizations on both corner copies of $Y$ and fixed product collars. The five-manifold $V$ may be chosen connected whenever its nonempty boundary is prescribed; in particular it is connected for the connected nonempty trace case. No condition on any fundamental group is imposed. For two nonempty four-dimensional zero/two-handle traces these connected sums are the split $+1$ or $-1$ framed-unknot insertions in the trace diagram. The theorem asserts existence of this relative five-bordism; it asserts no ordering or cancellation of its handles.

derivations.claim: Apply [F1] to the supplied $V$ in dimension five, keeping the full marked vertical collar. Remove its zero and five handles. Trade each one-handle to a three-handle by [F2], using a joining arc in the connected lower stage. Reorder, reverse, and trade each reversed one-handle to a three-handle there; in the original direction these are trades of index four to index two. No zero, one, four or five handle is reintroduced. Sort the remaining two- and three-handles by the fixed-height construction [F1]. Choose the regular middle four-manifold $W_*$ after the two-handles and before the three-handles.

From $W_0$ to $W_*$ only five-dimensional two-handles occur. From $W_1$ the reversed three-handles have complementary index $5-3=2$, so the same is true. Every such handle changes its four-dimensional level by interior framed circle surgery. Interior surgery preserves connectedness: the tube boundary $S^1\times S^2$ is connected, so gluing the old tube back could not join different components of its complement; since the old level is connected, that complement is connected, and the replacement attaches along the same connected interface. Thus every level in this construction stays connected, as required to iterate the base-circle argument.

Start with either original link presentation of $W_i$. By [F3] move the first five-dimensional handle's attaching circle to the fixed base, retaining its rank-three framing through an integral level frame. Its base representative avoids the old link, so choose its small tube disjoint from every old attaching thickening. By [F2] the actual four-dimensional surgery is two added two-handles on the corresponding $K$ and disk-framed zero meridian $U$. By [F4] its induced O3 boundary map is identity on the old link and the external base collar. Hence every previous handle and both end parametrizations are carried correctly. The new level again has a finite two-handle presentation from the same base.

Repeat step 3.1 for the finitely many five-dimensional two-handles from each end. At every stage the preceding conclusion gives exactly the hypothesis needed for [F3], so there is no circular assumption that an arbitrary four-manifold already has such a presentation. Both finite sequences terminate at the same actual level $W_*$ chosen in step 1.1, with its original full marked boundary, and give the stated two link descriptions. If no handles occur, the empty sequence is allowed.

If an actual five-bordism was not initially supplied, [F4] first corrects the signature seam by interior connected sums with signed projective planes, represented by split $+1$ or $-1$ framed unknot insertions. It produces the required connected fixed-collar $V$, without a fundamental-group hypothesis. Apply step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1 to these corrected traces. This adds precisely the asserted O1 preparation to the O3 common-middle construction. The conclusion leaves two descriptions of $W_*$; comparing them by an unrestricted trace-changing movie is a further theorem and is not inferred from their common diffeomorphism type.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $n$-manifold with collared boundary $\partial W=\partial_0W\sqcup\partial_1W$, let $\varphi:S^{k-1}\times D^{n-k}\to\partial_1W$ be an attaching embedding of a $k$-handle and let $\psi:S^k\times D^{n-k-1}\to\partial_1(W\cup_\varphi h^k)$ be an attaching embedding of a $(k+1)$-handle attached after it, where $0\le k\le n-1$. If the attaching sphere of $h^{k+1}$ meets the belt sphere of $h^k$ transversely in exactly one point, then $W\cup_\varphi h^k\cup_\psi h^{k+1}$ is diffeomorphic to $W$ relative to $\partial_0W$. Consequently a geometrically cancelling consecutive pair may be deleted from, or added to, any handle presentation of the same manifold; the diffeomorphism may be taken to act only in a collar of the affected boundary disc and in the two handles, so the attaching data of all later handles are carried along.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $h_1,h_2$ be $k$-handles attached to $M\subseteq\partial_+W$ as in the slide definition, with $1\le k\le n-2$, and let $h_1'$ be a slide of $h_1$ over $h_2$ (the slid handle attached to $M$ by the band move). Then $W\cup_{f_1}h_1\cup_{f_2}h_2$ and $W\cup_{f_1'}h_1'\cup_{f_2}h_2$ are diffeomorphic relative to $\partial_0W$; more precisely there is a diffeomorphism supported in a neighbourhood of the two handles and the band region carrying the first presentation to the second. Consequently a handle slide does not change the diffeomorphism type of the presented manifold and may be performed on any of two equal-index handles.

be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

boundary ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $F:V\times I\to N$ be a smooth map such
that $F_t:=F(\cdot,t)$ is a smooth embedding for every $t\in I$
([[def-smooth-embedding]]), and suppose $F$ is constant near the ends: for some
$\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac12)$ one has $F(x,t)=F(x,0)$ for $t\le\varepsilon$ and
$F(x,t)=F(x,1)$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon$, for all $x\in V$.

Then for every open neighbourhood $W\subseteq N$ of the compact image

derivations.claim: **Exact movie input and the retained marking.** Let N be a compact oriented smooth three-manifold with a protected boundary collar. Consider a four-dimensional relative handle presentation based on N×I. A distinguished one-handle h=I×D³ attaches at two disjoint parametrized balls in int(N). Other one-handles, if present, have disjoint feet. All two-handle attaching embeddings and their framings are part of the presentation. A finite movie is given on a compact parameter interval, with these conditions: Away from finitely many events the feet and framed attaching curves move by smooth isotopy. No one-handle slides over another one-handle occur during the interval under consideration. The distinguished h persists from an isolated cancelling 1/2 birth to an isolated cancelling 1/2 death. A small birth/death column is disjoint from every other handle attachment. Other births, deaths and slides have already supplied local models, and their supports miss the feet of h. Between those endpoints every event involving two-handles is a framed two-handle slide with its actual band, or a birth/death supported away from h. If further one-handles are present, the present construction is performed on an outer one-handle whose replacement arc is in N and avoids their feet. This is a hypothesis on the supplied ordered movie, not an asserted consequence of function genericity. The full outgoing boundary comparison with a fixed target is recorded at every isotopy, attachment and cancellation. All motions and all supports avoid the protected collar. Choose an embedded framed arc B in N joining the feet. It misses every other attaching curve at the initial parameter. Let A′ be a parallel of the core of h. The union A′∪B, rounded at its two ends, is a framed interior circle γ in the four-dimensional stage. Carry B by a compactly supported ambient isotopy of N extending the motion of the feet. Such an extension follows directly by extending the velocities on the two moving closed balls and integrating a supported field. It fixes the boundary collar. Its values on B supply a smooth family B_t; it need not keep B_t disjoint from the two-handle curves for every t. We prove that replacing h by its framed circle surgery along γ_t gives a finite framed-link movie whose elementary changes are isotopy, two-handle slides O2, and O3 at the distinguished birth/death. Every outgoing boundary comparison is transported in this conversion. The replacement changes the four-manifold in its interior and is not asserted to preserve that four-manifold.

**The actual link after the replacement.** Take disjoint small foot balls and a thin product tube about B. Together they form a three-ball: explicitly straighten the arc in its own product chart I×D², join the two end half-balls, and round the two seams. The union of this ball's collar with h is S¹×D³, with the core circle γ. Perform interior circle surgery there. The disk-factor construction in [[lem-interior-one-handle-trade-and-framed-circle-surgery-pair]] gives two two-handles C_B and U_B before the subsequent cancellation. The first C_B goes once through h along A′ and returns along B, with its supplied framing. The second U_B is its small disk-framed meridian. This is the two-hemisphere decomposition of D²×S², with the second disk factors interchanged. The attaching circle C_B meets the belt sphere of h in one transverse point. The product normal coordinates in the construction identify its attaching strip with one foot-to-foot traversal of h. Therefore the actual one/two-handle cancellation supplier applies, including its outgoing boundary diffeomorphism. Cancel h with C_B. In this cancellation every arc of another attaching curve that went through h is carried to a parallel of B in the chosen tube, with its normal strip carried by the product cancellation map. To verify that description, cut h at its cocore D³: its boundary becomes the two foot spheres with a common equatorial seam. The cancellation identifies the two sides by the core disk of C_B; along its remaining boundary that disk is exactly B. Thus the new boundary chart joins the two foot patches along B. Each disjoint parallel strip is joined by this same chart; its ordering and framing are those of the chosen tube. No new twist may be inserted independently. The remnant U_B is the boundary of a small cocore disk transverse to this routed bundle. It is an unknot with its displayed disk framing zero. It encircles the routed strands once, with their actual signs and multiplicities. Call the resulting link R_B(L)∪U_B, where R_B means this explicit routing of every old two-handle strip through the B-tube. In particular its integer framings are obtained by carrying entire strips, rather than by retaining arbitrary numerical labels after a drawing change. The complement of the ball/tube and the protected boundary collar are unchanged. The cancellation map and the original circle-surgery boundary map determine its outgoing identification.

**A transverse crossing of an attaching curve with the replacement arc.** The only new obstruction to a continuous routed-link isotopy is an intersection between an old attaching curve and B_t. Feet and ends are protected. A finite relative perturbation of B_t and the curves makes all such intersections isolated and transverse, with no intersections at an old event parameter. Here the map from (t,u,v), where u and v are the two arc parameters, to the two equal points in N has source dimension three and the diagonal has codimension three. To obtain the required submersive perturbation, choose a small product box at each possible intersection and add three independent translations of the interior of the B-arc with a bump equal to one in the smaller box. The evaluation difference has these three translations as a basis. Cover the compact parameter/arc track away from endpoints by finitely many boxes, apply the actual finite-dimensional parametric-transversality theorem to their summed perturbation, and additionally avoid simultaneous intersections using the two-point family with independently supported translations. Its two-diagonal codimension is six on a five-dimensional source (one time and four arc parameters). Near the parameter/arc diagonals, embeddedness and the nonzero tangents give one local intersection branch; distinct branches cannot accumulate there. Off these diagonal neighborhoods, the relevant source is compact. Thus transversality gives finitely many individual crossings. The other protected compact tracks remain disjoint after the perturbation is sufficiently small. Near one crossing choose oriented coordinates (x,y,z) in which the replacement arc is {(x,0,0)} and the old attaching strand, with its parameter, is {(0,y,t)}. This follows by the inverse function theorem applied to the three independent tangent vectors of the transverse intersection, preserving t by straightening the spatial arc at each t and then rescaling the nonzero normal velocity. Only the signs of the x/y/z coordinates affect the slide sign. Choose the B-tube x∈[−a,a], y²+z²≤ε². The two routings just before and after t=0 agree outside this box. Inside, join their corresponding endpoints by following the routed strip across the B-tube. The difference is the boundary of a small normal disk to B, connected to the old strand by a thin rectangular band. This boundary is precisely a framed parallel of U_B, transported along the B-tube from its original cross-section; the intervening annulus is the boundary of the product sub-tube between the two cross-sections. Its framing is constant in those product coordinates. Hence one routing is the band sum of the other attaching component with the appropriate signed framed parallel of U_B. The band interior misses all other strands after its width is decreased. This is the geometric definition of O2, with its full normal strip. It also proves the framing assertion: the two old strips and the parallel strip are joined by the displayed rectangle, so the resulting framing is the band framing, including any linking contribution. An unchanged numerical framing is not asserted. This verification is local even when the replacement arc represents a nontrivial relative homotopy class. Neither B nor the union B∪C below is assumed to bound a disk in N.

**Isotopies, other slides and simultaneous strips.** Away from the crossings in step 3.1 the ball/tube construction and cancellation vary smoothly. After shrinking their radii uniformly on the compact parameter interval, their strip routings give a framed-link isotopy, extended by the ordinary compact-source velocity construction. Near each old two-handle slide include its band as one more compact two-dimensional strip in the routing. Choose its width and the B-tube so that the band is in product position at every traversal of h. Routing commutes with joining the two strips along this band: both operations take their union and then use the identical product cancellation chart. Thus an old two-handle slide becomes a two-handle slide of the routed components. If an end of the band must be carried across U_B, the rectangle of step 3.1 gives the additional O2; these are finite because the band is a finite smooth compact product strip in the specified event model and can first be put in transverse position at its edges. A birth/death in a support disjoint from B and the feet is unchanged. Several strands may pass through h. Use distinct normal positions in D² of the B-tube, in the order determined by their attaching embeddings. Every operation above acts on their disjoint thickened strips. At a crossing only the intersecting strip is changed; all other strips are fixed after reducing the crossing box. This supplies the framed, many-strand version and does not replace an embedded strip by an unframed homology class.

**The distinguished birth and death are O3.** At a cancelling 1/2 birth, take the supplied cancelling chart. Just after the birth, the new two-handle attaching circle consists of a core arc A of h and a return arc C in N. It passes once through h. Every older two-handle is disjoint from this chart and hence has no traversal of the new h. The replacement operation in step 2.1 routes the cancelling circle to the closed curve K=C∪B, with corners rounded and its actual induced integer framing. The only other new component is U_B. It is a small meridian of K, because K uses B exactly once in the product tube. Its framing is the meridian-disk framing zero. Other attaching components avoid the chosen tube after B is initially chosen disjoint from them. Thus the result differs from the pre-birth link by the O3 pair K_f,U_0, supported in a small tubular solid torus of K. The integer f is whatever framing the cancellation and circle-surgery charts supply; the actual O3 filling theorem allows every integer. In particular K need not be nullhomotopic. This is why an O3 move, rather than an unsupported assertion that a split Hopf link was added, is the correct relative conclusion. At the death, before cancelling h with its supplied cancelling two-handle C, remove every other two-handle traversal of h by sliding that component over C. For each traversal take the band following its foot patch into the corresponding patch of C, then once through h with opposite signed traversal. The two parallel traversals bound a product rectangle in I×D³, so after the slide they isotope off h. The normal strip is the band strip and hence has exactly the slide framing. Choose parallel bands at different normal positions and perform the finitely many slides sequentially. No other one-handle is crossed by these local bands. Afterward only C goes through h, and the inverse of the birth construction removes the corresponding O3 pair. Routing the preparatory slides is permitted by step 4.1. This proves the distinguished death assertion without requiring the transported B to be isotopic to the short cancelling arc C.

citations.quote: Assume AC. Let a finite smooth relative four-dimensional handle movie be based on a compact oriented three-manifold $N$, with its boundary product collar fixed. Let a distinguished one-handle persist from a cancelling $1/2$ birth to a cancelling $1/2$ death, with no one-handle slides involving it on the interval. Replacing the one-handle by interior surgery on its core joined to that arc, then cancelling the long two-handle, gives a based framed-link movie. Its changes are framed isotopy, $O2$ band slides (including a meridian slide when a strip crosses the replacement arc), and $O3$ at its two endpoints. Here $O3$ is a framed knot with its small disk-zero meridian. All framings and actual outgoing boundary maps are retained, and the boundary collar is fixed pointwise. The statement permits arbitrary homotopy class of the replacement arc and arbitrary finite signed traversals by the other strips. It is local conversion of the supplied movie, not its global existence.

Assume AC. In dimension $d\ge4$, a one-handle whose feet lie in the same connected lower stage can be replaced, by an interior framed circle surgery, with one $(d-2)$-handle. The resulting manifold may change, but its entire boundary, specified collar and every later attaching map are identified with the old ones. The framing for this existence trade is the displayed product framing. Separately, surgery on a prescribed rank-three-framed circle lying in a product three-dimensional level of an oriented four-manifold, with its framing homotopic to a level rank-two framing plus the level-normal line, is represented relative to the unaffected boundary by adjoining two four-dimensional two-handles on that framed knot $K$ and a small disk-framed zero meridian $U$. The statement retains the integral framing of $K$. In a two-handle trace every interior framed circle can be put in this form by the preceding circle lemma. The pair's boundary identification is the boundary-relative local O3 identification.

Assume full AC. Let $N\cong D^2\times S^1$ be an oriented solid torus in the interior of an oriented smooth 3-manifold, let $K$ be its core with any integral framing, and let $U$ be a small meridian of $K$ with the zero framing given by its meridian disk. Simultaneous framed surgery on $K$ and $U$ returns a solid torus diffeomorphic to $N$ by a diffeomorphism equal to the original identification on $\partial N$. Thus inserting or removing this pair preserves the ambient manifold relative to the complement of $N$, including external collars and boundary parametrizations. An embedded colored ribbon graph avoiding $N$ is fixed. No assertion is made that a graph traversing $N$ is fixed, or that this operation belongs to a complete relative move list.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $h_1,h_2$ be $k$-handles attached to $M\subseteq\partial_+W$ as in the slide definition, with $1\le k\le n-2$, and let $h_1'$ be a slide of $h_1$ over $h_2$ (the slid handle attached to $M$ by the band move). Then $W\cup_{f_1}h_1\cup_{f_2}h_2$ and $W\cup_{f_1'}h_1'\cup_{f_2}h_2$ are diffeomorphic relative to $\partial_0W$; more precisely there is a diffeomorphism supported in a neighbourhood of the two handles and the band region carrying the first presentation to the second. Consequently a handle slide does not change the diffeomorphism type of the presented manifold and may be performed on any of two equal-index handles.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

derivations.claim: **Input and framing convention.** Let h be one four-dimensional one-handle with feet in a connected compact oriented three-dimensional base N. Let B and B′ be two embedded replacement arcs joining its feet, with framed product tubes and the same parametrized germs at their endpoints. They avoid every other one-handle foot and the protected boundary collar. A finite system of framed two-handle attaching curves may traverse h any number of times, with either orientation. Apply the explicit cancellation/routing construction with either arc. Its links are $R_B(L)\cup U\qquad\hbox{and}\qquad R_{B'}(L)\cup U.$ Here U may be chosen as the same small zero-framed circle in both diagrams: take its cross-section on the common endpoint germ. Its disk meets each routed strip once for each signed traversal of h. Its framing is the product disk framing. This convention follows by transporting the meridian along the product cancellation tube; it fixes the actual exterior marking. Assume first that B and B′ have disjoint interiors outside their common endpoint germs. No restriction is placed on the homotopy class of their union. The two framed arc strips, with oppositely oriented common germs, join to a framed embedded ribbon annulus about a closed curve K that follows B′ and returns along a parallel of B. More precisely separate the strips by distinct normal coordinates, cut both just inside their common germs, and join the four short ends by the two planar rectangles in the endpoint balls. The core of the resulting annulus is K. Its annular normal is the integer framing used below. This choice records any difference in twisting of the two replacement arc framings; no independently chosen integer is substituted.

**Addition, routing slides and the meridian correction.** Push the K-annulus far enough in the normal coordinate to miss every old routed strip and U. Add a small disk-framed meridian V of K at the B′ branch near one endpoint fork, with its disk missing the old B-routed strips. This is an O3 insertion: before any subsequent slide its meridian disk meets K alone. Choose its radius much smaller than the separation of the ribbon strips. The solid-torus support of K can avoid all old link components. For each traversal of h by an attaching strip, slide that component over a framed parallel of K, using the short band at the relevant endpoint fork. Choose the sign so that the parallel B segment of K cancels the old B segment of that strip. The two oppositely followed, adjacent B strips bound the product rectangle in the B-tube. Pushing their band sum across this rectangle leaves a B′ strip. Outside the B/B′ tubes and the two endpoint balls the old component is unchanged. For multiple traversals choose distinct normal positions, do the slides sequentially, and shrink every band. The same rectangle then applies separately at every traversal. The resulting old attaching curves are exactly R_{B′}(L), with their full framed strips. The integer framing of K was defined by those strips precisely so the cancellation of the B ribbons leaves the prescribed B′ ribbon. Both signs of traversal are handled by reversing the annular orientation and the band direction. There is no assertion that numerical framings remain unchanged during the slides. After these slides V is not yet a clean O3 meridian: the new B′-routed strips pass through its cross-section. Leaving this issue out would invalidate the comparison. Slide V over the oppositely oriented zero-framed parallel of U, with the band lying in the endpoint fork. Let the result be V′. Its framing is zero: U and V initially have disjoint disk interiors in that fork convention and linking zero, so the band framing is 0+0−2lk(U,V)=0. Equivalently the band sum is the boundary of the explicit disk in the next paragraph. The slide does not change U or any other attaching component. The disk and the fact that V′ meets K alone can be verified in a regular neighborhood of the three-edge fork. One edge is the common endpoint germ, and the other two are the separated B and B′ branches. Take a small ball containing only this fork and the parallel ribbon strips. The transverse disk on the common edge is the disk of U. The transverse disk on the B′ edge is the disk of V after the routing slides. Join their boundaries by a narrow strip on the boundary of the fork ball, with the opposite orientation on the common-edge disk. Cutting the fork neighborhood along the two cross-sections displays an ordinary ball with three disk faces: the B face, the B′ face and the common-edge face. This follows directly by thickening the three intervals of a tree; absorb its two terminal vertex balls into the interval tubes. The oriented boundary relation among these three faces says that the band sum of the B′ meridian and the negative common-edge meridian is the B meridian. In particular it bounds the third transverse disk after a product isotopy in this ball. This is an equality of the displayed framed disk faces, not just an equality of homology classes. The old strips now use the common edge and the B′ edge, and therefore miss the B cross-section. K uses the B′ branch and the B branch with opposite orientations, and therefore crosses the B cross-section exactly once. Thus the displayed disk of V′ meets K once and every other attaching strip zero times. It also misses U after reducing the fork ball and using the distinct cross-sections. Its normal framing is its disk framing. Consequently K,V′ is again a clean O3 pair. Remove it. What remains is R_{B′}(L)∪U with the exact routed strip framings. The comparison is therefore a finite sequence $\text{O3 insertion},\quad \text{one O2 per signed traversal},\quad \text{one O2 on the new meridian},\quad \text{O3 deletion},$ followed by the explicit product isotopies. It does not require K to be nullhomotopic in N.

**General arcs and geometric supports.** Two arbitrary replacement arcs can be put in the preceding disjoint position while retaining their common endpoint germs. Perturb the interior of B′ by finitely many local spatial translations. At a possible intersection with B, the evaluation map has source dimension two and the diagonal has codimension three; the same actual finite-dimensional parametric-transversality theorem used for curves gives a disjoint perturbation. It may also avoid the finitely many other foot balls by retaining its original support outside them. Choose the perturbation C¹-small, so it is still embedded and its framing is transported by its small tubular isotopy. The routed link changes by the corresponding framed isotopy, with the old U cross-section fixed. Intersections with old attaching strips need not be excluded during a motion of the auxiliary arc: the explicit transverse crossing calculation in the continuous replacement crossing calculation inserts the necessary O2 moves. For the comparison itself the final arcs and their ribbon parallels are chosen disjoint from the finite old curve system before the O3 insertion; generic one-dimensional position in a three-manifold supplies this, followed by sufficiently small product tubes. All the operations are supported in compact subsets of int(N), consisting of the two arc tubes, endpoint fork balls and the finite slide bands. The boundary collar is pointwise fixed. The maps on the outgoing surgered three-manifold are those of the actual slides and the boundary-relative O3 filling identity, with the displayed cancellation charts. The construction relates the two link outputs. The following trace comparison records its actual outgoing map as well; it does not claim that an arbitrary interior mapping class can be freely substituted.

**Comparison of the outgoing maps.** Work before cancelling h. Let γ_B=A′∪B in the four-dimensional one-handle stage, and let γ_K be a disjoint parallel of B′∪−B. Attach five-dimensional two-handles along these two framed circles. They give the two successive interior circle surgeries. The actual relative handle-slide lemma applies with n=5 and k=2. Slide the γ_B handle over γ_K along the short endpoint rectangle. The oppositely followed B arcs cancel across their product rectangle, so the new attaching circle is γ_{B′}=A′∪B′. Its rank-three framing is the one obtained from the annular ribbon framing and its extra collar-normal direction. The γ_K handle remains. This is a five-dimensional handle slide supported in the interior of the four-dimensional stage; its entire external three-boundary times the movie interval is fixed pointwise. Read its outgoing four-boundary by splitting each inserted D²×S² into the two hemispherical two-handles, with the second disk factors swapped as in the already constructed surgery bridge. The parallel core-disk push defining the five-dimensional slide has two effects on these four-dimensional attaching charts. On every strip traversing h, its band rectangle replaces the B strip by the B′ strip; these are exactly the signed slides over K in step 2.1. On the transverse disk faces it replaces the B′ cross-section by the difference of the B′ and common-edge cross-sections; this is exactly V↦V−U in the displayed three-disk fork ball. Outside these rectangles and fork ball both maps are identity. On each rectangle they are the same product disk push, and on the fork ball they identify the same three parametrized disk faces. Choose the corner interpolations by this same product isotopy. Thus the link-move comparison in step 2.1 is the outgoing restriction of the five-dimensional slide after applying the same h/C cancellation on the two sides. In particular its external three-boundary map is the change of the two recorded cancellation charts, up to the supported collar isotopies already retained in those charts. After removing the clean O3 pair at the second end, the comparison of the resulting three-manifolds is therefore the one induced by those original cancellation/routing identifications. This establishes the marking required for this local arc-choice comparison. It still supplies no arbitrary prescribed diffeomorphism beyond that recorded comparison.

All feet and the specified slide band are compactly contained off the protected boundary collar. Use the actual k=1 handle-slide definition: after attaching h_b, move one foot of h_a along a thin strip across the interval core of h_b to a parallel of its other endpoint. Its normal D³ travels in the strip coordinates. Denote the resulting handle h_a′. The support is a regular neighborhood of the two handles and the slide strip; no homotopy of the three-dimensional base to a ball is assumed. Choose disjoint replacement arcs B_a,B_b in the base, with fixed product germs at the feet. Let γ_a,γ_b be the corresponding interior core-plus-arc circles in H, pushed to disjoint normal positions. In the slid presentation choose B_a′,B_b′ compatibly with the core-disk push: after identifying the two one-handle stages by the actual slide diffeomorphism, γ_b′ is γ_b and γ_a′ is the framed band sum of γ_a with the signed parallel of γ_b along the slide strip. To obtain these arcs, trace the moved foot back through the slide strip and then along a parallel of B_b, joining the remaining end to B_a inside the foot ball. All segments outside the original handle cores lie in N. Round the two joins in disjoint small balls and put the parallels at different normal positions. The result is an embedded arc after a small relative perturbation in dimension three. The product normal framing is transported by the same strip. This construction proves existence of compatible choices; arbitrary other replacement arc choices are compared by [[lem-one-handle-surgery-replacement-is-independent-of-the-base-arc]].

**The traded attaching charts.** For each h_i insert the interior circle-surgery pair C_i,U_i and cancel h_i with C_i, exactly as in the continuous-surgery construction. Its link consists of U_a,U_b and all old attaching curves routed through the B_a,B_b tubes. Both U_i are zero-framed meridians of the corresponding routing tube. The product normal positions make the two meridian disks disjoint; in particular lk(U_a,U_b)=0, and both framings are the displayed disk framings. Strips traversing either handle are retained with their actual order and their orientation of traversal. The supported slide of the thickened two-edge spine has the following elementary effect on its transverse disks: $D_a\longmapsto D_a,\qquad D_b\longmapsto D_b\mathbin{\natural}(-D_a),$ with the sign reversed for the other orientation of the slide. Here the second operation joins a parallel of the two disks by the thin rectangle running along the slide strip. This formula is a geometric disk formula. Cut the original two tubes at D_a and D_b; their neighborhood is a ball with four named disk faces a_+,a_−,b_+,b_−. The foot slide joins the a_+ collar to the b_- collar and then continues from b_+. A disk separating the new b cross-section is the old b disk together with the oppositely oriented a disk and the joining rectangle. Its boundary misses the unchanged a cross-section. Reattaching the four disk faces gives exactly the displayed banded disk; the remaining product collar is unchanged. Thus the disk formula follows from cutting and regluing the explicit tube products, not merely from the inverse-transpose action on homology. Taking boundaries gives the four-dimensional two-handle slide $U_b\longmapsto U_b\#_{\beta}(-U_a),\qquad U_a\longmapsto U_a,$ where β is this specific rectangle. Its framing is the band framing zero, since it is the boundary framing of the displayed banded disk; equivalently 0+0−2lk(U_a,U_b)=0. A small product displacement separates it from every routed attaching strip. The old strips are transported at the same time through the cut-open four-face ball. A strip that does not traverse h_a is unchanged there. A strip traversing h_a enters at a_−, follows the new a tube and then the signed b tube, exactly the edge substitution a↦ab of the specified one-handle slide. The compatible choice of B_a′ in step 1.1 performs the identical substitution in its routed image. Thus the two sets of old routed strips agree after this supported product comparison. Multiple traversals are parallel copies of the same calculation and can be made disjoint by decreasing their widths. At any residual crossing with an auxiliary replacement arc, the already proved transverse-arc rectangle gives an additional O2 on the relevant meridian; it does not create a new move type. This proves the local link conversion: a one-handle slide, with compatible replacement arcs, becomes the indicated O2 on the dual zero-framed meridians, together with the explicit framed isotopies and any auxiliary-arc crossing O2 moves. It does not require the replacement arcs or the slide support to be contractible in N. Arbitrary replacement arc choices add the finite O3/O2 comparison from the companion file.

**Why this is the retained boundary comparison.** There is an equivalent way to check the map, not just the final diagram. On H attach five-dimensional two-handles along γ_a,γ_b. In the slid presentation attach them along γ_a′,γ_b′. The compatible choice in step 1.1 makes these two five-dimensional attachments related by the actual $n=5,k=2$ handle slide along the specified strip. Its diffeomorphism is identity on the entire external three-boundary times the interval because the circles and the strip are interior to H. Split each resulting D²×S² into hemispherical four-dimensional two-handles, interchanging the disk factors in the second hemisphere. On the long core pieces this is the original a-over-b core-disk push. On their transverse disk pieces it is exactly the banded-disk formula of step 2.1, hence the opposite dual-meridian slide. The product normal charts on the band and four disk faces are those used in both descriptions. Cancelling h_a/C_a and h_b/C_b on the two sides therefore yields the same outgoing restriction as the specified O2/product-isotopy link comparison. The incoming base collar and the prescribed external outgoing identification are retained. The five-dimensional lemma is used only inside its verified range 1≤k≤n−2, here k=2,n=5. No claim that diffeomorphic four-dimensional two-handlebodies are two-equivalent is involved. The underlying four-dimensional levels are modified by the circle surgeries; the five-dimensional slide compares these particular modifications and their maps.
