Assume full AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional collared bordism, $d\ge1$, and let $f_s$ be a path supplied by [[lem-relative-one-parameter-morse-path-with-finite-events]], with the given noncritical height fixed on the spatial collars. Prescribe descending endpoint fields, stationary near the parameter ends, standard near their Morse critical points, and having no trajectories from index $i$ to index $j\ge i$. Morse–Smale endpoint fields suffice. Then there is a smooth descending family $X_s$ with those endpoint and collar values such that:

1. Near every fold it is the negative Euclidean gradient of the exact cubic model. At every regular critical point it has a smooth hyperbolic descending model. Near each same-index passage it may be taken to have the normalized linear Morse model at the destination.
2. No ordinary trajectory increases index. The entire family has finitely many same-index connecting trajectories; each occurs at a distinct parameter away from births and critical-value crossings. Each is a transverse parameter passage: on an incoming section at its destination, the $i-1$ source-sphere tangent directions together with the parameter direction map isomorphically onto the $i$-dimensional normal space of the stable section.
3. A sufficiently small parameter neighborhood of each birth contains no same-index trajectory. Between its two newborn critical points there is exactly the standard cancelling trajectory.
4. In successive one-critical elementary bands, the full framed attaching embeddings and actual outgoing boundary maps vary smoothly on each regular function chamber, including through positive-index-drop tangencies. The existing elementary birth and critical-value-crossing comparisons retain their actual outgoing maps, and their composition retains the terminal boundary parametrization.

Disconnected $W$, empty ends, and index $0/d$ births are allowed. This is an elementary-band assertion: it neither asserts slice-wise Morse–Smale transversality at positive index drops nor supplies parameterwise grouping of arbitrary based handle presentations by index or a global Kirby completeness theorem.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge4$, and let $V$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional bordism with corners, horizontal faces $A_0,A_1$, and vertical face $B\times[0,1]$, with compatible product collar charts fixed. Here $\partial A_i=B\times\{i\}$. There are excellent Morse data with all critical points interior, equal to the specified height $t$ on a fixed smaller vertical product collar, zero and one on the horizontal faces with their prescribed inward collar models. They give a finite handle decomposition whose attaching thickenings lie in the interiors of horizontal levels, away from the fixed vertical collar, retaining the actual outgoing identification. Critical values may be ordered by index while this entire boundary height is fixed. If $V,A_0,A_1$ are connected and $A_0,A_1$ are nonempty, there is such a relative presentation with no handles of index zero or $d$. No fundamental-group assumption or h-cobordism hypothesis is imposed.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(f,X)$ be adapted on a compact triad, and choose regular $0<u<c<c'<v<1$ such that the critical set in $K=f^{-1}[u,v]$ consists exactly of finite clusters $P,Q$ at values $c,c'$. Suppose there is no $X$-trajectory from a point of $Q$ to a point of $P$. Then for any $a,a'\in(u,v)$, including $a>a'$ or $a=a'$, there is an adapted Morse $g$ with the same critical points and indices as $f$, $g=a$ on $P$, $g=a'$ on $Q$, and $X$ still downward gradient-like for $g$. The function is $f$ outside the interior of $K$ and near its two end levels, and is $f$ plus a constant near every critical point. On a triad with just these two critical clusters, one may also use its face levels as $u,v$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold with boundary admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $K\subseteq M$ be compact, and let $W\subseteq M$ be open with $K\subseteq W$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:M\to [0,1]$ that equals $1$ on an open neighbourhood of $K$ and satisfies $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq W$.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. For each $p\in M$, let
$\gamma_p:I_p\to M$ be the maximal integral curve through $p$, and set

$$ \mathcal D:=\{(t,p)\in\mathbb R\times M:t\in I_p\}, \qquad \Phi(t,p):=\gamma_p(t). $$

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.

derivations.claim: **Exact input.** Let V be a compact smooth d-dimensional bordism, with fixed horizontal incoming/outgoing faces and a fixed vertical product collar, on which the slicing function is t. Suppose a smooth one-parameter family (F_s,X_s), constant near the parameter endpoints, is supplied with the following proved properties. Each X_s is descending for F_s, is the fixed vertical product field near the protected collar, and is the standard negative Euclidean gradient in the supplied Morse charts and exact cubic birth charts. There are finitely many function events and finitely many transverse isolated same-index connecting-orbit events. No orbit joins a critical point of smaller index to one of larger index. Away from births the stable/unstable sections are smooth in the parameter. The actual compactness theorem for trajectories, including the fold endpoint sections, is part of the input. Near every birth the newborn critical points have no same-index connecting orbit to any other critical point. Their small birth block and the retained critical charts may be chosen uniformly. No slice-by-slice transversality of positive-index-drop trajectories is required. The proposed output is a smooth family g_s with the same critical points and indices, the same cubic births, X_s descending for g_s, and all critical values ordered by index. All boundary heights and protected collars are unchanged. Same-index heights may coincide at isolated crossings. Its full relative handle presentation is index grouped. Its actual equal-index trajectory events are unchanged because X_s is unchanged. The field theorem is used precisely through [F1].

**A value change with smooth orbit cutoffs.** First take a compact regular-parameter neighborhood J with fixed Morse critical charts. At s=s₀ consider two adjacent critical levels, belonging to P and Q, with no connecting orbit from the upper point to the lower. Choose outer regular levels a<b containing just these two critical points. Their stable and unstable trajectory pieces in this slab, closed by their intersections with the outer levels, are compact and disjoint. Indeed the supplied broken-trajectory compactness permits a limit outside the indicated piece only by a broken orbit through the other critical point, which would give the excluded connection. The pieces stay away from the vertical collar, since the product trajectories there cannot approach an interior critical point. These separation properties persist on a smaller parameter neighborhood: a contrary sequence has a broken limit giving the same forbidden connection. Smooth dependence of the field and the Morse sections then applies uniformly. There is a smooth orbit-constant β_s on this slab, equal to one near the P trajectory piece and zero near the Q trajectory piece and the vertical collar. Here are the extension details. On the lower regular face choose a bump equal to one on a neighborhood of the compact P unstable exit section and zero near the Q unstable exit section and the boundary. The sections are disjoint compact sets, so the bump can be chosen uniformly for s near s₀; let it be one on one fixed open neighborhood containing every nearby P exit section. Extend by flow to every trajectory meeting the lower face. Set the extension one on trajectories ending at P and zero on those ending at Q. Near either Morse block the resulting function is constant: in the exact chart entry/exit passage is $(u_0,v_0)\longmapsto (\epsilon u_0/|u_0|,\,|u_0|v_0/\epsilon).$ As u₀ tends to zero its exit lies in the selected neighborhood of the corresponding unstable exit section; hence the extended bump is identically one, respectively zero, on a full neighborhood of the stable sheet and the critical block. There is therefore no nonsmooth quotient at the limiting sheet. On its remaining domain the exit time and exit point are smooth by the implicit function theorem for a regular level. This proves smoothness jointly in s and space. A minimum with no unstable exit has an open attracting set on which the value is set constantly one or zero. Its possible boundary inside the slab would limit to the other critical point; the excluded connection rules that out near the chosen trajectory piece. The same argument applied to the reversed field handles a maximum and an upper-face construction. The extension is zero near the vertical product trajectories because the lower bump is zero there, and the product flow has no critical endpoint there. Thus X_sβ_s=0 everywhere. A cutoff in the level coordinate may be used outside this outer slab; take it only where the height change below is already identity, so it contributes no derivative term. Choose a smooth increasing interval diffeomorphism φ_s of [a,b], identity near its endpoints and affine with positive slope near the P critical value, carrying that value to a desired position still inside (a,b). Define $G_s(u,z)=(1-z)u+z\phi_s(u),\qquad \widetilde F_s=G_s(F_s,\beta_s).$ Then ∂_uG_s>0, and $X_s\widetilde F_s=(\partial_uG_s)(F_s,\beta_s)X_sF_s<0$ off the original critical points. Near P the function is φ_s(F_s), near Q it is F_s, and near the vertical collar it is exactly F_s. This changes the P level across Q without changing either critical point or introducing a new one. The full Hessian near P is multiplied by a positive scalar. All ingredients can be chosen smoothly on the smaller parameter neighborhood. The same construction works for a compact critical birth block in place of P when its complete entry/exit pieces are disjoint from Q: use a bump constant one on a neighborhood of all its exit sections, so the extension is constant on a full uniform birth block. The fold entry/exit compactness in the input supplies that neighborhood. Inside the block the change is chosen positive affine in the function value, so the exact cubic model is retained.

**Compatible prescribed heights.** Away from small disjoint parameter neighborhoods of the births, prescribe $h_p(s)=\frac{\operatorname{ind}(p)+1}{d+2}+\epsilon F_s(p),$ with one sufficiently small positive ε. The margin 1/(d+2) makes different index groups disjoint. For same-index points the prescription preserves the order of their F_s values, hence respects every actual connecting orbit. Every positive-index-drop orbit also has strictly ordered prescribed heights, and index-increasing orbits are absent by hypothesis. Near a birth of indices k,k+1 take the exact critical block and place its common critical height near (k+3/2)/(d+2). On a smaller parameter neighborhood prescribe a positive affine function of the original cubic there. The two values then differ by a positive constant times the actual cubic value gap, of order s^{3/2}, and fit together into a function smooth in the original (s,u) chart. They lie above all the old index-k values and below all the old index-(k+1) values. Interpolate to the ordinary prescription on the outer part of this birth neighborhood by a smooth nonnegative parameter cutoff, zero on the smaller neighborhood and one outside the larger one. Only where that cutoff is positive do the two new branches have separate uniform Morse charts; the interpolation is therefore smooth there, while near the fold it is exactly affine cubic. The birth neighborhoods are disjoint, so these choices do not conflict. There are no same-index orbits incident to these two branches on the neighborhood in question. Their reordered heights consequently violate no orbit inequality; positive index drops still go from an upper group to a lower group. The ordering within every old index group continues to be the original F_s ordering. These prescriptions are strictly compatible with the partial order generated by the actual connecting orbits. Broken chains impose no additional inequalities, because inequalities compose. Values at a same-index function crossing may agree, but there is no orbit between equal-height critical points by strict descent. Those pairs can be kept together as a two-point value cluster during the construction.

**A finite transverse list of critical-value events.** The interpolated heights need not initially have only finitely many crossings. Here is the additional finite-dimensional construction. Protect smaller closed parameter neighborhoods of the folds and of the stationary endpoints. On a sufficiently small fold neighborhood the two birth heights lie in their common middle gap, are unequal away from the fold, and are separated from every other critical height of their respective index; the old same-index heights are distinct there because the original function path has no second event at the fold. On endpoint neighborhoods the original excellent heights are stationary and distinct within each index group. Thus there is no unaccounted crossing on these protected neighborhoods. There are finitely many same-index trajectory parameters by the field input. Choose disjoint small regular neighborhoods of them, missing the protected fold and endpoint neighborhoods. At the center of each, separate any coincident prescribed heights by independent arbitrarily small shifts in the corresponding critical charts. Preserve the strict height gap of the one actual connecting pair by choosing the shifts smaller than one quarter of that gap; preserve the gaps between distinct index groups as well. There are no other same-index trajectories in a sufficiently small chosen neighborhood. The shifts can therefore be extended smoothly with a parameter bump there without violating any trajectory inequality. After shrinking to a smaller neighborhood of its center, all critical heights are pairwise distinct there. Protect that smaller closed neighborhood and the adjusted heights on it. These finitely many preliminary shifts change no birth model or endpoint. They retain every actual orbit and its direction, since X_s has not changed. The remaining possible crossing set is compact and contained in the ordinary parameter region with finitely many regular critical branches. Cover it by finitely many parameter intervals with compact closure in that region. For each such interval choose a parameter bump χ equal to one on a smaller interval, and independently for each critical branch on it allow additions $a_p\chi(s)+b_p(s-s_0)\chi(s).$ Extend them by zero off that interval and that branch's parameter chart. On the smaller interval their value and first derivative can be prescribed independently. The union of this finite list is one finite-dimensional height family. For a same-index pair p,q its difference evaluation is a submersion in these coefficient directions wherever its zero can occur. Its value/first-derivative jet also has the two independent coefficient directions. For two different pair equalities at one time the value evaluations have rank two, including the case of a shared branch (a triple height). Apply the actual finite-dimensional parametric-transversality theorem to the finitely many single-pair value maps and the finitely many two-pair maps. A generic sufficiently small coefficient vector makes every single-pair difference transverse to zero, and excludes the simultaneous vanishing of two different pair differences because its codimension is two on a one-dimensional parameter source. This is the finite critical-height jet/Sard step; no genericity of a newly chosen field is assumed. All perturbations have support outside the protected neighborhoods. Choose their coefficients small enough that no new zero occurs outside the chosen smaller intervals, whose complement had a positive value-gap margin; enlarge the finite cover before making this choice if necessary. Choose them also small enough to retain the positive index-group gaps. The only same-index connecting-orbit parameters lie in the protected neighborhoods, where their strict prescribed inequalities have been left unchanged. Hence every actual trajectory inequality is preserved. The birth height formulas and endpoint heights are unchanged. Every resulting same-index pair difference has a closed zero set in this compact ordinary parameter region, with no zero near its protected boundary. Its zeros are transverse and hence isolated, so compactness makes them finite. Two such zeros cannot occur at the same parameter by the two-pair condition. There are no triple values, no coincident two crossings, and no crossing at any same-index trajectory event. The only remaining critical-value coincidence outside this finite list is the intended birth itself. At any adjusted crossing there is no connecting orbit, precisely because all trajectory-event neighborhoods were protected. The adjusted prescribed heights satisfy the same trajectory inequalities. The local orbit-cutoff value changes already proved in step 2.1 can therefore be used in their realization, with the finite parameter patching below. This gives the asserted finite event list while retaining the same field and its terminal maps.

**Local realization and parameter patching.** At a fixed parameter, the original and prescribed orders are two linear extensions of this trajectory partial order, allowing the just-described clusters. A finite sequence of exchanges of adjacent incomparable elements transforms one extension to the other: move the first element of the target extension to the first position of the source by successive exchanges; every passed element is incomparable because both extensions respect the order; then induct on the remaining list. Each exchange has no trajectory between the two pieces and is realized by step 2.1. Choose the local target gaps slightly larger than needed, then adjust all ordered values to the exact prescribed values by increasing reparametrizations in disjoint value intervals, again with orbit cutoffs zero near the vertical collar. The same construction is smooth on a sufficiently small parameter neighborhood. If an original value crossing occurs at its center, first use a small smooth local value separation of the two critical charts, whose supports are disjoint; they have no connecting orbit near that crossing. If the prescribed heights cross within one index group, the final two local chart values are simply the prescribed smooth functions, and the same no-connection value adjustment realizes their equality. No exchange across a connecting orbit is performed. A birth block is treated as one piece until its value is in the prescribed gap between the old k and k+1 groups, using the block version of step 2.1. Other critical values can be moved past this block only when the target inequalities require it. The no-increasing-orbit condition and the stated absence of same-index birth incidences then exclude any connecting orbit between the two pieces. In a smaller parameter neighborhood the function is exactly positive affine on the whole birth block, as required in step 3.1. These operations give a local smooth family with all prescribed critical heights and no other critical points. Cover the compact parameter interval by finitely many such neighborhoods, taking a single birth neighborhood for each fold. Each local realization is positive affine in F_s near every ordinary critical chart, with its constant term determined by the common prescribed h_p(s). Shrink the chart radii uniformly. At a birth choose the affine function on the common smaller birth block once and require all local realizations meeting that parameter neighborhood to equal it there; this is possible because subsequent value changes have support away from that block. Take a smooth partition of unity ρ_α(s) subordinate to the finite parameter cover and set $g_s(x)=\sum_\alpha\rho_\alpha(s)g_s^{(\alpha)}(x).$ Then X_sg_s is a convex sum of strictly negative numbers at every noncritical point. No new critical point occurs. On an ordinary critical chart it is a positive affine function of F_s, with exactly the prescribed critical value. On a smaller birth block it is the common positive-affine cubic. Near every protected face all summands equal the original fixed height, so g_s has that height. Smoothness follows from the finite smooth sum. Choose the cover and partition stationary on endpoint collars. This proves the proposed parametric grouping conclusion from the exact field input.

**The retained framed data and maps.** Use X_s to carry the local framed unstable disks to regular levels of g_s. Because X_s is unchanged and g_s is descending for it, its unparametrized trajectories and the actual terminal entry/exit maps are unchanged. Changing a regular section only inserts the explicit regular-flow comparison. Thus the index grouping retains the framed elementary attachments and outgoing parametrizations, including through positive-index-drop tangencies. The same field therefore retains each finite isolated trajectory passage and each disjoint value-crossing comparison. Their interpretation in a full based handle movie is a separate construction, and is not a premise of the present grouping lemma.

Assume full AC. On a compact smooth collared bordism, keep the incoming and outgoing parametrizations as part of a finite elementary handle description. A generic adapted function path supplied by [[lem-relative-one-parameter-morse-path-with-finite-events]] induces a finite sequence of changes of its Morse-induced elementary handle descriptions: relative diffeomorphisms and isotopies of the framed attaching embeddings, changes of standard handle-coordinate frame, splitting/merging empty product bands, interchange of two independent disjoint framed attachments, and creation/removal of a geometrically cancelling adjacent-index pair. Assume full AC. Let $q$ be an index-$k$ Morse critical point in dimension $n$, $1\le k\le n-1$, with fixed local coordinates and descending field $f=c-|u|^2+|v|^2$, $X=(2u,-2v)$, for $(u,v)\in\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}$. Let $p$ be a higher critical point of the same index. Suppose a one-parameter family of the descending attaching-sphere sections of $p$ passes through the stable section of $q$ once, at one point, and transversely in the following sense: its $k-1$ sphere-patch directions and its parameter direction map isomorphically onto the $k$ unstable directions at the event. Assume all remaining attaching data are disjoint from the chosen local passage region; retain the joining band, lower regular level, and normal framing, and assume no intervening critical point between that region and the chosen lower level.

The two framed attaching embeddings obtained by transporting below $q$, before and after this isolated passage, differ by the signed framed band sum with a parallel of the attaching sphere of $q$. For $k=1$ this replaces one foot by a parallel of the other foot of $q$ along the band. For $1\le k\le n-2$ this is the handle slide of the existing definition and preserves the relative diffeomorphism type with all later attaching maps carried along. In particular $n=4,k=2$ gives the framed-link slide. For $n=3,k=2$, only the stated local surface band sum with its supplied embedded band is asserted; no higher-codimension band-existence contract is imported. No generic-family existence or global trajectory-completeness assertion is made.

$$F(x,y,\lambda)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y=\varphi(x,\lambda),$$

and

$$D\varphi(x,\lambda)=-D_yF(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda)^{-1}D_{(x,\lambda)}F(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda).$$

When no parameter block is present, this is the ordinary $C^k$ implicit function theorem.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V$ be a compact
smooth $n$-manifold with boundary and let $N$ be a smooth $n$-manifold without
boundary ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $F:V\times I\to N$ be a smooth map such
that $F_t:=F(\cdot,t)$ is a smooth embedding for every $t\in I$
([[def-smooth-embedding]]), and suppose $F$ is constant near the ends: for some
$\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac12)$ one has $F(x,t)=F(x,0)$ for $t\le\varepsilon$ and
$F(x,t)=F(x,1)$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon$, for all $x\in V$.

Then for every open neighbourhood $W\subseteq N$ of the compact image
$F(V\times I)$ there is a smooth map $H:N\times I\to N$ such that
$H_0=\operatorname{id}_N$, every $H_t$ is a diffeomorphism of $N$
([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]),
$$H_t\circ F_0=F_t\quad\text{for every }t\in I,$$
$H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, $H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$
for $t\le\varepsilon/2$, and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $n$-manifold with collared boundary $\partial W=\partial_0W\sqcup\partial_1W$, let $\varphi:S^{k-1}\times D^{n-k}\to\partial_1W$ be an attaching embedding of a $k$-handle and let $\psi:S^k\times D^{n-k-1}\to\partial_1(W\cup_\varphi h^k)$ be an attaching embedding of a $(k+1)$-handle attached after it, where $0\le k\le n-1$. If the attaching sphere of $h^{k+1}$ meets the belt sphere of $h^k$ transversely in exactly one point, then $W\cup_\varphi h^k\cup_\psi h^{k+1}$ is diffeomorphic to $W$ relative to $\partial_0W$. Consequently a geometrically cancelling consecutive pair may be deleted from, or added to, any handle presentation of the same manifold; the diffeomorphism may be taken to act only in a collar of the affected boundary disc and in the two handles, so the attaching data of all later handles are carried along.

derivations.claim: **Fixed index cuts and the based spheres.** Use the exact weak field family (g_s,X_s) after grouping, with its finite simple value crossings, finite separated same-index trajectory events, and exact birth blocks. On a closed parameter interval missing these events choose smooth regular cuts a_{i−1}(s),a_i(s) immediately below and above every index-i group. They exist because the index groups have a uniform strict gap. Identify the cut levels by the actual regular-band flow/trivialization, retaining their maps. At an isolated birth use the outer two cuts of its combined k,k+1 group; no regular cut through the birth critical point is asserted. For an index-i critical point p choose a sufficiently small local unstable sphere S_p≅S^{i−1} in its fixed chart. Every point of this sphere reaches the lower cut a_{i−1} in finite positive time at a parameter with no equal-index connection. Here is the full obstruction argument. If it did not, descending flow on the compact intervening band has a critical limit or a broken critical limit. The height-curve compactness supplied by the field theorem proves this without any slice-wise Morse–Smale hypothesis. An intervening critical point has index at least i, because all smaller indices lie below the lower cut. The first limiting orbit would therefore be index increasing or same-index. Both are absent at this parameter. There is no vertical-boundary limit: X is the fixed noncritical product field there, and its compact interior trajectory sections stay off that collar. A regular infinite-time limit is excluded by the strict descent bound on compact sets away from critical charts. These exhaust the possibilities, so the hitting time is finite. The union of the starting spheres over a compact event-free parameter interval is compact. If their hitting times were unbounded, the same uniform broken-trajectory extraction would give a forbidden index-increasing or same-index orbit at a limiting parameter. Thus the hitting times have a uniform finite bound. At the lower cut dg_s(X_s) is nonzero, so the parameter-dependent implicit function theorem makes the hitting time and hitting point smooth in the sphere variables and s. The flow differential carries the local normal framing. Shrink the full normal D^{d−i} radius uniformly: compactness of the source and the bounded-time flow imply that the full S^{i−1}×D^{d−i} hits the cut as an embedding. The same uniqueness argument gives disjoint core spheres for distinct index-i points: a common point would have one backward orbit with two different critical limits. There are finitely many compact disjoint core images, so their full normal radii can be chosen positive and pairwise disjoint, smoothly over the parameter interval. These are the actual based framed index-i attaching embeddings on the outgoing boundary of the lower-index stage. They are not globally unstable spheres in the original N across all smaller-index critical points. The lower cut is exactly the boundary after the already constructed smaller-index handles. This distinction is what permits positive-index-drop trajectories and their tangencies.

**Product complements and the retained higher attaching data.** Attach all index-i handles on that common lower cut, with the displayed full embeddings. The actual local Morse attachment charts identify their outgoing regions. On their complement use the regular descending flow to identify with the upper cut a_i. To justify this complement map, remove small invariant entry/exit blocks around the finitely many critical points. Every remaining trajectory between the cut faces is regular and, after removing smaller block collars, has a uniform strict descent bound. Its finite hitting map and its inverse are smooth. The side collars of the Morse blocks use their explicit product entry/exit maps; patching is by those same flow coordinates. This gives the ordinary handle-correspondence comparison for the whole index band, with corners rounded in the retained seam collars. Same-index connections are absent on the present interval, so no one block ends at another. The comparison varies smoothly by the uniform bounds of step 1.1. Let d_i(s) be this actual outgoing identification from the index-i attached stage to the upper cut. A later framed attaching embedding A on that upper cut is carried by d_i(s)^{-1}∘A to the new stage, and its terminal parametrization is composed with d_i(s) in the corresponding direction. The product complement map is therefore part of the data, not an equality of unparametrized diffeomorphism types. If incoming cut identifications are h_s and outgoing ones k_s, the written band map changes by the actual conjugation k_s^{-1}d_i(s)h_s. All later embeddings are carried by that conjugation. This explicitly controls every higher-index attachment even if its global trajectory meets a lower stable sheet or undergoes a positive-drop tangency. The weak elementary-band supplier already proves that its one-critical-band embedding is smooth; composing the present smooth outgoing comparisons preserves that property. No higher-index attaching sphere is required to avoid every lower-index passage region.

**Isolation at the one same-index trajectory.** Let s₀ be one of the finite equal-index orbit parameters, with its unique trajectory p_i→q_i. Choose its compact connecting segment between a source sphere near p and an entry face of a small q chart. The generic field supplier gives the exact transverse incidence in that entry face: its (i−1) source-sphere variables plus s span the i normal unstable directions. It also gives a normalized linear q model near s₀, away from every actual fold. The exact hyperbolic passage calculation then applies. The other index-i core sections can be kept away from this passage support. For r≠p,q a sequence of r core trajectories approaching the q stable entry sheet or the chosen connecting segment would, by the uniform broken-trajectory compactness, give at s₀ an orbit or broken chain from r to q or p before reaching the lower cut. Every intervening index is at least i. The no-increase property makes every component same-index, and a chain of two components would give two equal-index orbits at s₀. A one-component limit would give a second equal-index orbit distinct from p→q. Both contradict the supplied finite-event conditions. Thus these finitely many other core sections have a uniform positive clearance on a sufficiently small parameter interval. Shrink their full normal thickenings to keep that clearance. The portion of the p source sphere outside a small neighborhood of the one incidence likewise has uniform clearance: any contrary limiting incidence would be a second point of the same transverse connection, hence the same orbit meeting the chosen source sphere twice. The local source sphere is a one-exit section in its exact Morse chart, so this is impossible. Compactness permits a slightly larger removed patch and one uniform clearance for its closed complement. The q unstable disk itself is kept as the second attaching handle, rather than removed from the model. In q coordinates the stable entry patch is |v|=ε, with incoming u=u_0. Its exit map is $(u_0,v_0)\longmapsto (\epsilon u_0/|u_0|,\ |u_0|v_0/\epsilon).$ The transversality permits the fiber-preserving straightening u_0=(x,s−s₀) on a smaller patch, by the already supplied local lemma. The two parameter sides cover the two complementary hemispheres of q's unstable sphere. Their nonzero v displacement chooses an actual parallel of that sphere, with the transverse direction e fixed by the stable entry point. After choosing two small regular parameter slices, reduce the normal radii so both this parallel patch and the q attaching thickening are disjoint. No positive-width attaching map at the singular parameter itself is required. From the q exit face down to the common lower cut there is no intervening critical point of smaller index, because its height is below that cut; an intervening same/higher-index limit is excluded just as in step 1.1. The compact q exit sphere therefore has uniformly finite smooth transport to the lower cut. It carries the actual parallel, its connecting band and its full normal framing. Other index-i cores remain disjoint by the preceding clearance, so the isolated local passage lemma supplies precisely the based framed handle slide at that cut. Its outgoing comparison is the product passage/collar map retained in that lemma. The higher attaching maps are then transported through that actual outgoing comparison by step 2.1. For d=4 the forward isolated-slide supplier is invoked only for i=1,2, inside its stated range 1≤i≤d−2. An index3 event is handled by reversing the entire local band: use (−g,−X), whose corresponding index is4−3=1 and which still has no index-increasing orbit. The incoming/outgoing marks are exchanged and then exchanged back. Thus its actual comparison is the reverse of the proved index1 slide, not an unsupported invocation of a forward index3 slide theorem. Index0 has no unstable sphere and index4 has no stable sphere, so no such event exists at those extremes. In a general d the same reverse interpretation handles i=d−1; the forward local lemma covers1≤i≤d−2.

**Critical-value crossings and birth blocks.** At a simple same-index critical-VALUE crossing there is no connecting orbit at that parameter: such a trajectory would strictly decrease the critical height. The event lists were also separated from all equal-index trajectory parameters. Hence step 1.1 gives based full thickenings smoothly through the value crossing and step 2.1 gives their product complements. The two attachments are disjoint on one common lower cut. Their quotient gluings commute, and the supplied elementary crossing comparison is exactly the collar-smoothed version of this commuting square. It retains the actual terminal maps. This is a value crossing, not a slide, and introduces no additional based move. At a birth of indices k,k+1 protect its exact cubic chart and use the two outer cuts. The unique cancelling trajectory, its framed intersection and the no-outside-return energy estimate are the actual elementary birth supplier. There is a genuine local cancelling handle pair. On the complement of a smaller birth block, there are no degenerate critical points; choose the other one-critical charts and regular cut transports as in that supplier. The lower groups and the old same-index branches have the uniform no-equal-incidence clearance from the newborn same-index branches, supplied by the weak field theorem near a birth. Their full based data are therefore regular up to the outer faces. For higher groups, including an allowed positive-drop trajectory into the fold, do not assert clearance from the birth block. Instead use the actual outgoing cancellation comparison from the two outer cuts and carry their entire elementary attaching embeddings through it as in step 2.1. This is precisely how the given elementary birth theorem identifies later handle data. It permits older higher attaching maps to pass through the block; it does not require them to remain fixed there. For s on the two-critical side one may choose an intermediate regular cut between the newborn heights, but it is not extended as a regular cut through s₀. The event is read in the combined outer band. The product cancellation chart then identifies the post-birth based presentation with the pre-birth presentation plus the cancelling k/(k+1) pair, with the outgoing diffeomorphism retained. This does not mean that older index-(k+1) attaching spheres automatically miss the born k-handle. In dimension four, for a 1/2 birth, put the older attaching curves transverse to its belt sphere. There are finitely many intersection points. At each, the product rectangle through the new one-handle joins that traversal to the opposite traversal of the cancelling two-handle; sliding over this cancelling handle removes that intersection and transports the complete framing. Choose parallel narrow bands and repeat. These are genuine additional two-handle slides used to put the birth in its isolated based form; their maps are composed with, rather than dropped from, the outgoing cancellation comparison. For a 2/3 birth use the reversed index1/2 calculation. For a 0/1 birth the same transport moves the finitely many other feet across the joining ball/tube, which is the rooted-tree comparison in the conversion proof; 3/4 is its reverse. Higher-index attaching data are carried after the combined band by the actual outgoing map as above. Thus positive-drop incidences at a fold introduce no omitted event type, while the finite normalizing slides are explicitly included in the mixed-handle movie. At a death use its inverse and carry all later data by that same inverse. Changes of the auxiliary cut levels are finite regular-flow comparisons with these stated maps. This is the exact cancellation/birth move in the mixed-handle movie, not a claim that the full later attaching data are pointwise unchanged.

**Finite assembly and the endpoint presentations.** The grouped family has finitely many births, value crossings and equal-index trajectory events by the field theorem and the added critical-height Sard construction. Cover each by one of step 3.1, step 4.1's disjoint parameter neighborhoods. Their complement is a finite union of compact regular intervals, and step 1.1, step 2.1 supply their based framed handle isotopies and product complement maps. Match the incoming identification of each piece to the actual outgoing identification of the preceding piece. The resulting finite mixed-handle movie has only the asserted births/deaths, same-index slides, commuting value interchanges and isotopies. All higher attaching data and the complete terminal parametrization have been carried by the actual maps at every piece. At an all-two-handle endpoint the descending field was prescribed from that given handle presentation. Its based unstable spheres are therefore its original attaching curves and full framings under the original handle-correspondence map. Index grouping has retained that field and only changed critical values. Moving the common lower cut follows the same field to the fixed incoming collar, so it inserts only the recorded regular-flow identification. Choose that identification to be the original incoming N. The endpoint link and its outgoing marking are consequently the given ones, rather than some merely diffeomorphic surgery output. This proves the based-movie bridge from the stated weak-field, elementary-comparison and grouping suppliers. It discharges the extra based-isolation hypothesis left explicit in the weak field proof. This establishes the stated based-movie interface with its actual maps; no further global conversion is used as a premise.

citations.quote: Assume AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth four-dimensional bordism with fixed horizontal faces, fixed vertical product height, and specified all-two-handle endpoint presentations. Apply the finite weak descending-path supplier and its parametric index grouping, with the endpoint fields prescribed from those presentations. Then there is a finite based framed mixed-handle movie joining the given endpoint presentations. Its elementary changes are framed isotopies, same-index handle slides (index3 read as the reverse index1 slide), cancelling adjacent-index births/deaths and commuting critical-value interchanges of disjoint attachments. Older attachments may pass through a birth block; the finite normalizing slides and actual cancellation maps are retained. Every higher attaching embedding and the complete terminal parametrization are carried by the actual outgoing comparisons. All supports fix the vertical boundary collar. No slicewise Morse–Smale condition at positive index drop is required.

Assume AC. Let a finite smooth relative four-dimensional handle movie be based on a compact oriented three-manifold $N$, with its boundary product collar fixed. Let a distinguished one-handle persist from a cancelling $1/2$ birth to a cancelling $1/2$ death, with no one-handle slides involving it on the interval. All feet, actual framed two-handle attaching strips, slide bands, local birth/death supports and outgoing identifications are supplied. Choose a framed replacement arc in $N$ joining its feet and carry it by the foot isotopy; assume other birth/death supports miss its tube. Replacing the one-handle by interior surgery on its core joined to that arc, then cancelling the long two-handle, gives a based framed-link movie. Its changes are framed isotopy, $O2$ band slides (including a meridian slide when a strip crosses the replacement arc), and $O3$ at its two endpoints. Here $O3$ is a framed knot with its small disk-zero meridian. All framings and actual outgoing boundary maps are retained, and the boundary collar is fixed pointwise. The statement permits arbitrary homotopy class of the replacement arc and arbitrary finite signed traversals by the other strips. It is local conversion of the supplied movie, not its global existence.

Assume AC. Fix one four-dimensional one-handle with feet in a connected compact oriented three-dimensional base $N$, and a finite system of actual framed two-handle strips. Let $B,B'$ be any two framed replacement arcs with the same parametrized foot germs and avoiding other feet and the protected boundary collar. The routed link outputs of the continuous one-handle replacement, with their actual outgoing identifications, are connected by finitely many exterior framed isotopies and $O2/O3$ moves, fixing that collar. The core knot in an $O3$ move need not be nullhomotopic. For disjoint arc interiors one comparison consists of adding $K=B'\cup(-B)$ with its small zero meridian $V$, sliding each routed traversal over $K$, sliding $V$ over the negative old zero meridian $U$, and deleting the resulting clean $O3$ pair. All framings, prescribed attaching strips and outgoing maps are retained.

Assume AC. In a four-dimensional handle presentation based on a compact oriented three-manifold $N$, let one one-handle slide over another by a specified framed foot strip, and carry all two-handle attaching strips by that actual slide. Trade both one-handles by their core-plus-base-arc surgeries and cancellations. For compatible arc choices the resulting framed links differ by the opposite band slide of the dual zero-framed meridians, together with the displayed product isotopies and any auxiliary-arc crossing slides. For arbitrary arc choices add the finite comparison of the preceding arc lemma. The cumulative outgoing identification is that induced by the original slide and the two recorded trade comparisons; the protected boundary collar is fixed. No fundamental-group hypothesis or same-trace two-equivalence theorem is assumed.

Assume AC. In dimension $d\ge4$, a one-handle whose feet lie in the same connected lower stage can be replaced, by an interior framed circle surgery, with one $(d-2)$-handle. The resulting manifold may change, but its entire boundary, specified collar and every later attaching map are identified with the old ones. The framing for this existence trade is the displayed product framing. Separately, surgery on a prescribed rank-three-framed circle lying in a product three-dimensional level of an oriented four-manifold, with its framing homotopic to a level rank-two framing plus the level-normal line, is represented relative to the unaffected boundary by adjoining two four-dimensional two-handles on that framed knot $K$ and a small disk-framed zero meridian $U$. The statement retains the integral framing of $K$. In a two-handle trace every interior framed circle can be put in this form by the preceding circle lemma. The pair's boundary identification is the boundary-relative local O3 identification.

Assume AC. Let $N$ be a connected nonempty compact smooth oriented three-manifold, and let $W$ be a finite four-dimensional two-handle trace from $N$, with its full external boundary collar fixed. Every smooth framed circle in $\operatorname{int}W$ avoiding that protected collar is ambiently isotopic, with compact support outside it, to a circle in a pushed-in copy of $N$. The target circle may avoid the old finite attaching link. Its prescribed oriented rank-three normal framing is represented, up to homotopy and isotopy of its small tubular attaching embedding, by an integral rank-two framing in $N$ plus the level-normal line. No condition on $\pi_1(N)$ or on the circle's class is imposed. More generally, freely homotopic embedded circles in a smooth manifold of dimension $d\ge4$ are isotopic whenever their homotopy lies in a prescribed relatively compact open set; the isotopy may be supported in that set. Every loop class in a three-manifold has an embedded representative avoiding a prescribed finite link.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge4$, and let $V$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional bordism with corners, horizontal faces $A_0,A_1$, and vertical face $B\times[0,1]$, with compatible product collar charts fixed. Here $\partial A_i=B\times\{i\}$. There are excellent Morse data with all critical points interior, equal to the specified height $t$ on a fixed smaller vertical product collar, zero and one on the horizontal faces with their prescribed inward collar models. They give a finite handle decomposition whose attaching thickenings lie in the interiors of horizontal levels, away from the fixed vertical collar, retaining the actual outgoing identification. Critical values may be ordered by index while this entire boundary height is fixed. If $V,A_0,A_1$ are connected and $A_0,A_1$ are nonempty, there is such a relative presentation with no handles of index zero or $d$. No fundamental-group assumption or h-cobordism hypothesis is imposed.

Let $Y$ be a compact oriented smooth three-manifold with prescribed boundary parametrizations and a fixed product collar $C\subset Y$. Surgery links lie in $\operatorname{Int}(Y\setminus C)$. For a framed link $L$, let $Y_L$ be its Dehn filling, with the canonical unchanged collar $C$, and let $E_L=Y\setminus\operatorname{Int}N(L)$ denote its exterior. The meridian of the $i$th filling solid torus is glued to the surgery-framed parallel $\lambda_i$ on $\partial N(L_i)$.

A decoration is a finite properly embedded oriented framed ribbon graph, with fixed abstract coupon set, actual coupon morphisms and band labels, fixed attachment order, and prescribed product ribbons in $C$ meeting only the designated marked boundary intervals. Colored graph isotopies keep all these collars, endpoints and labels fixed. Then:

1. Every decoration in $Y_L$ has a representative in $\operatorname{Int}(E_L)\cup C$, relative to its prescribed collar ribbons.
2. Two such exterior decorations that are isotopic as framed labeled graphs in $Y_L$ are connected by finitely many exterior framed colored graph isotopies and framed slides of open graph strands over the surgery parallels $\lambda_i$. Original coupons and colors remain fixed.
3. Suppose the **marked undecorated relative surgery calculus** holds in $Y$: every required collared bordism has a marked surgery presentation, and every specified orientation-preserving identification of two outputs, fixed pointwise on $C$, is realized up to isotopy relative to $C$ by a finite sequence of the canonical local undecorated moves $O1$ (a separated $\pm1$ unknot), $O2$ (a framed surgery-component band slide), $O3$ (a framed knot plus a small zero-framed meridian), and exterior link isotopies. The canonical move maps are the standard local filling identifications, identity outside their specified local neighborhoods. Under exactly this hypothesis, every marked decorated bordism admits an exterior decorated presentation, and two presentations of the same marked decoration are connected by the corresponding undecorated moves, exterior colored graph isotopies, and the open-colored-strand slides in (2).

The hypothesis in (3) concerns the **specified** output identification, not merely existence of some diffeomorphism. No undecorated completeness theorem is proved or assumed silently here. After surgery components are colored by $\Omega$, all the extra graph moves in this conclusion preserve the complete fixed-coupon evaluation by [[lem-kirby-color-full-band-slide-and-coupon-identity]]; the usual local $O1/O2/O3$ normalization identities are separate algebraic suppliers. Connectedness is not required.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $h_1,h_2$ be $k$-handles attached to $M\subseteq\partial_+W$ as in the slide definition, with $1\le k\le n-2$, and let $h_1'$ be a slide of $h_1$ over $h_2$ (the slid handle attached to $M$ by the band move). Then $W\cup_{f_1}h_1\cup_{f_2}h_2$ and $W\cup_{f_1'}h_1'\cup_{f_2}h_2$ are diffeomorphic relative to $\partial_0W$; more precisely there is a diffeomorphism supported in a neighbourhood of the two handles and the band region carrying the first presentation to the second. Consequently a handle slide does not change the diffeomorphism type of the presented manifold and may be performed on any of two equal-index handles.

derivations.claim: **Movie input and the assignment to a surgery link.** Fix connected compact oriented three-manifolds N,M, a specified identification of their boundaries, and the protected vertical collar. A connected four-dimensional bordism W between them is given with its complete boundary markings. Suppose two all-two-handle presentations are joined by a finite index-grouped mixed-handle movie on W: elementary framed attaching maps vary smoothly between events; events are cancelling births/deaths 0/1,1/2,2/3,3/4, same-index handle slides and critical-value interchanges of disjoint attachments. All terminal maps are retained. Positive-index-drop trajectory tangencies are permitted, since the elementary-band attaching maps remain smooth through them. This exact input is stronger than a generic function path. Its explicit supplier is [[lem-index-grouped-relative-descending-paths-give-based-framed-handle-movies]]: common index cuts and bounded-time full framed attachments; compactness isolation at the single same-index passage; reversed index1 treatment of index3; birth/value-crossing comparisons; and actual transport of every higher attaching map and endpoint marking. That construction, together with the weak field and grouping proofs, supplies this input rather than assuming it as a genericity consequence. Assign a two-handle presentation at every ordinary time as follows. Collapse a rooted spanning tree in the initial zero/one-handle graph, eliminating every new zero-handle. Dually collapse a rooted spanning tree in the outgoing dual zero/one-handle graph, eliminating every four-handle. The two roots are the fixed nonempty connected N and M. These collapses leave a presentation with indices1,2,3. On the reversed presentation trade every one-handle (the original index3 handles) by the explicit interior circle surgery, obtaining only indices2,3 in reverse and hence indices1,2 forward. Flatten the successive two-handle attachments into the boundary of the forward one-handle stage. Trade every remaining forward one-handle by its explicit core-plus-base-arc interior circle surgery and cancellation. The result is a finite link in N. Every trade preserves the full external boundary of the four-manifold and changes its interior. Every flattening and cancellation retains its outgoing comparison. The actual local trade, framed-circle-to-level isotopy and two-disk-factor surgery bridge are [[lem-interior-one-handle-trade-and-framed-circle-surgery-pair]] and [[lem-framed-circles-in-four-dimensional-two-handle-traces-move-to-the-base]]. The arbitrary replacement arc comparison is [[lem-one-handle-surgery-replacement-is-independent-of-the-base-arc]]. The one-handle slide after trading is [[lem-one-handle-slides-become-relative-kirby-slides-after-trading]]. No change of replacement arc is declared invisible: it is that comparison's actual O3/O2 sequence with its meridian correction.

**Rooted tree collapses and changes of tree.** The zero/one-handle graph has one old root vertex N and one vertex for every new ball; edges are the one-handles. It is connected because higher-index attaching regions are connected and cannot merge components. Choose a spanning tree T. Starting at its leaves, the union of a leaf ball and its incident tree tube is a ball with one retained attaching disk. Absorb it into its neighbor's collar using the explicit ball-plus-tube product chart. Every other foot and every higher attaching embedding is carried by this very chart. Repetition removes all new zero-handles. The support stays off the protected vertical collar. Reversing gives the outgoing tree collapse. Two trees are compared by single-edge exchanges. If T′ differs from T, choose f∈T′−T. The unique cycle in T∪{f} contains an edge e∈T−T′; replacing e by f reduces the number of differing edges. Finite induction reaches T′. For this one exchange restrict to the cycle plus its attached tree branches; first absorb the branches by the same leaf-ball products. The cycle is now a cyclic sequence of balls and tubes attached to the root component by a tree path. Collapse all but the two edges e,f. The remaining model is two balls joined by two tubes, with its incoming root collar retained. Collapsing the first tube or the second tube gives the same ball-plus-one-handle model with different retained core paths. To see the actual comparison, cut both tubes at transverse three-disks. The cut piece is a ball with the four named disk faces e_±,f_±. Moving the chosen joining tube across the other disk face is the k=1 disk push of the actual handle-slide proof. Other incident feet are moved along the displayed tube by parallel disk patches. Each such movement is a one-handle slide over the surviving cycle handle; its thickening is the product D³ of the corresponding patch. A higher attaching strip is carried by the same product chart. Restoring the absorbed branches transports this finite collection of slides and isotopies to the original graph. Thus a tree change produces only one-handle slides and framed isotopies in the collapsed presentation, with its actual lower-boundary identification. The construction uses the cut four-face ball, not a classification of graph thickenings or a free-group basis argument alone. At a 0/1 birth the new vertex has its cancelling edge. Choose T to contain that edge; the leaf-ball product absorbs the born pair and leaves the assigned presentation unchanged. At a death first choose T to contain the dying edge. If other feet lie on its ball, the same product absorption carries them across the joining tube; in another tree convention this is precisely the finite one-handle-slide comparison just described. Thus the 0/1 row produces only the already controlled one-handle-slide/isotopy changes. Apply the reversed argument to a 3/4 birth or death. It also proves independence of the outgoing tree choice before the dual trades.

**Reversal of a two-handle slide.** We need the local duality calculation, rather than an assumption that a reverse movie has the same diagram. A four-dimensional two-handle is D²_x×D²_y. In the forward presentation x is its core disk and y its cocore; in the reversed presentation their roles are interchanged. For a slide of the first core disk over the second along a band, its new core is the boundary band sum of the first core with a parallel of the second.
